            require(family["immutableColumns"] == list(cols), "PERSISTENCE_IMMUTABILITY_MISMATCH:" + fid)
            require(family["forbiddenOperations"] == ["UPDATE", "DELETE", "TRUNCATE"], "PERSISTENCE_OPERATION_MISMATCH:" + fid)
    event = byid["acceptance_event"]
    old = source_tables["public.ad_v4_review_case_events"]["migrationDeclarations"]
    require(event["legacy0029"] == old, "EVENT_0029_CATALOG_MISMATCH")
    require(event["physicalColumnOrder"] == [c["name"] for c in old["columns"]] + ["candidate_decision_id", "acceptance_signoff_id"], "EVENT_0029_COLUMN_ORDER_MISMATCH")
    for c in old["columns"]:
        current = next(x for x in event["columns"] if x["name"] == c["name"])
        require(current["nullable"] == c["nullable"] and current["sqlType"] == c["type"]["sqlType"], "EVENT_0029_PHYSICAL_COMPATIBILITY_MISMATCH:" + c["name"])
    require(event["delta0030"]["oldBranchNewColumnsNull"] == ["candidate_decision_id", "acceptance_signoff_id"], "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(event["delta0030"]["oldContractVersion"] == "paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-review-1", "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(event["delta0030"]["preserveFunctionAcl"] and event["delta0030"]["preserveTableAcl"] and event["delta0030"]["preserveOldBinaryInsert"], "EVENT_0029_ACL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(event["delta0030"]["draftIntent"] == ["undecided", "reject"], "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    old_union = next(c["expression"] for c in old["checks"] if c["name"] == "ck_ar4_event_union")
    acceptance_union = "event_type='candidate_only_accepted' AND resulting_state='candidate_only' AND draft_revision_id IS NULL AND review_request_id IS NOT NULL AND rejection_id IS NULL AND signoff_id IS NULL AND candidate_decision_id IS NOT NULL AND acceptance_signoff_id IS NOT NULL AND predecessor_event_hash IS NOT NULL"
    expected_checks = copy.deepcopy(old["checks"])
    for check in expected_checks:
        if check["name"] == "ck_ar4_5_version":
            check["expression"] = "(event_type='candidate_only_accepted' AND contract_version='paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1') OR (event_type<>'candidate_only_accepted' AND contract_version='paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-review-1')"
        if check["name"] == "ck_ar4_event_union":
            check["expression"] = "((" + old_union + ") AND candidate_decision_id IS NULL AND acceptance_signoff_id IS NULL) OR (" + acceptance_union + ")"
    require(event["checks"] == expected_checks, "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(all(fk in event["foreignKeys"] for fk in old["foreignKeys"]), "EVENT_0029_FOREIGN_KEY_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(all(u in event["uniqueConstraints"] for u in old["uniqueConstraints"]), "EVENT_0029_UNIQUE_INCOMPATIBLE")
    projection = event["delta0030"]["legacyCanonicalProjection"]
    require(projection["dropBeforeCanonicalization"] == ["candidate_decision_id", "acceptance_signoff_id"], "EVENT_0029_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(projection["retainedPhysicalColumns"] == [c["name"] for c in old["columns"]], "EVENT_0029_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    guard = next(f for f in event["delta0030"]["frozenSqlFunctions"] if f["name"] == "public.paprnav_v4_review_insert_guard")
    replacement = projection["replacementDefinition"]
    require(projection["replacementStatement"] == "r:=to_jsonb(NEW);\n IF TG_TABLE_NAME='ad_v4_review_case_events' THEN\n   r:=r-ARRAY['candidate_decision_id','acceptance_signoff_id'];\n END IF;", "EVENT_0029_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    require(guard["definition"].count("r:=to_jsonb(NEW);") == 1, "EVENT_0029_GUARD_SOURCE_CHANGED")
    require(replacement == guard["definition"].replace("r:=to_jsonb(NEW);", projection["replacementStatement"], 1), "EVENT_0029_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    installed=catalog['postgresqlObservation']['catalog']
    installed_event=next(r for r in installed['relations'] if r['relationId']==event['identity'])
    require(event['legacy0029Installed']==installed_event,'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_CATALOG_MISMATCH')
    delta=event['delta0030']
    require(delta['existingOwnerBefore']==installed_event['owner'] and delta['existingExplicitAclBefore']==installed_event['explicitAcl']
            and delta['existingEffectiveAclBefore']==installed_event['effectiveAcl'],'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_AUTHORITY_MISMATCH')
    require(delta['installedCatalogSha256']==digest(installed),'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_HASH_MISMATCH')
    expected_functions=[{'name':f['name'],'arguments':f['arguments'],'definitionSha256':f['definitionSha256'],
                         'owner':f['owner'],'explicitAcl':f['explicitAcl'],'effectiveAcl':f['effectiveAcl'],
                         'operation':'replace_exact_canonical_projection_statement_preserving_owner_acl' if f['name']=='public.paprnav_v4_review_insert_guard' else 'preserve_definition_owner_acl'} for f in installed['functions']]
    require(delta['installedFunctionPreservation']==expected_functions,'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_FUNCTION_PRESERVATION_MISMATCH')
    installed_guard=next(f for f in installed['functions'] if f['name']==guard['name'])
    projected=delta['installedGuardProjection']
    require(projected['originalDefinitionSha256']==installed_guard['definitionSha256'] and
            projected['replacementDefinition']==installed_guard['definition'].replace('r:=to_jsonb(NEW);',projection['replacementStatement'],1) and
            projected['replacementDefinitionSha256']==hashlib.sha256(projected['replacementDefinition'].encode()).hexdigest(), 'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE')
    expected_triggers=[{'before':t,'afterDefinition':t['definition'].replace(' EXECUTE FUNCTION '," WHEN ((new.event_type)::text <> 'candidate_only_accepted'::text) EXECUTE FUNCTION ") if t['name'] in ['trg_ar4_5_guard','trg_ar4_5_complete'] else t['definition'],
                       'enabledAfter':t['enabled'],'deferrableAfter':t['deferrable'],'initiallyDeferredAfter':t['initiallyDeferred']} for t in installed_event['triggers']]
    require(delta['observedTriggerPreservation']==expected_triggers,'EVENT_0029_INSTALLED_TRIGGER_PRESERVATION_MISMATCH')
    require(persistence['sourceAuthorityDecision']==catalog['sourceAuthorityDecision'],'SOURCE_AUTHORITY_DECISION_MISMATCH')
    branches = byid["external_dependency"]["branchConstraints"]
    require([b["id"] for b in branches] == ["X01", "X02", "X03", "X04", "X05", "X06"], "EXTERNAL_BRANCH_INVENTORY_MISMATCH")
    nullable = {c["name"] for c in byid["external_dependency"]["columns"] if c["nullable"]}
    for branch in branches:
        require(set(branch["required"]) | set(branch["forbidden"]) == nullable, "EXTERNAL_BRANCH_LEAF_INVENTORY_MISMATCH:" + branch["id"])
        require(not set(branch["required"]) & set(branch["forbidden"]), "EXTERNAL_BRANCH_OVERLAP")


def validate(persistence, catalog, model, migration):
    validate_sources(catalog, model, migration)
    validate_persistence(persistence, catalog)
    # Preserved upstream SQL includes wildcard reads. The selection DSL itself
    # forbids them; rejecting historical source text would erase provenance.
    inspected_catalog = {k: v for k, v in catalog.items() if k not in {"migrationSqlStatements",'postgresqlObservation'}}
    inspected_persistence = copy.deepcopy(persistence)
    inspected_persistence["families"][6]["delta0030"].pop("frozenSqlFunctions", None)
    inspected_persistence["families"][6]["delta0030"]["legacyCanonicalProjection"].pop("replacementDefinition", None)
    inspected_persistence['families'][6]['delta0030']['installedGuardProjection'].pop('replacementDefinition',None)
    for document in (inspected_persistence, inspected_catalog):
        for value in walk(document):
            if isinstance(value, str):
                require(not re.search(r"\b(?:TODO|TBD|FIXME|all-columns)\b|SELECT \*", value), "PLACEHOLDER_OR_WILDCARD")


def validate_observed_catalog(catalog, model):
    observation=catalog['postgresqlObservation']; physical=observation['catalog']
    facts=catalog['postgresqlComparison']
    require(facts['status']=='OBSERVED_FRESH_MIGRATIONS_THROUGH_0029','PG_REQUIRED_OBSERVATION_ABSENT')
    require(facts['snapshotSha256']==digest(physical)==observation['validatedSnapshotAfterRollbackSha256'],'PG_OBSERVATION_HASH_MISMATCH')
    require(observation['queries']==PG_QUERIES and facts['queryInventorySha256']==digest(PG_QUERIES),'PG_QUERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH')
    require(observation['ormCrosswalk']==physical_orm_comparison(model,physical),'PG_ORM_CROSSWALK_MISMATCH')
    require([r['relationId'] for r in physical['relations']]==['public.'+n for n in SOURCE_NAMES],'PG_RELATION_INVENTORY_MISMATCH')
    require(facts['relationCount']==74 and facts['columnCount']==983 and facts['functionCount']==69,'PG_OBSERVATION_COUNT_MISMATCH')
    for function in physical['functions']:
        require(function['definitionSha256']==hashlib.sha256(function['definition'].encode()).hexdigest(),'PG_FUNCTION_DEFINITION_HASH_MISMATCH')
    expected_absences={r['relationId']:[] for r in catalog['relations']}
    for selection in catalog['selections']:
        for item in selection.get('joinForeignKeyEvidence',[]):
            if not item['exactFullTuplePhysicalForeignKeyPresent']:
                expected_absences[item['leftRelation']].append({'selectionId':selection['selectionId'],'joinEvidence':item})
    for relation in catalog['relations']:
        require(relation['declaredPhysicalFkAbsences']==expected_absences[relation['relationId']],'PG_FK_ABSENCE_DUTY_MISMATCH')
    probes=observation['liveMutationProbes']
    require(len(probes)==13 and all(p['killed'] and p['rollback'] and p['actualCode'].startswith(p['expectedCode']) and p['statementsSha256']==digest(p['statements']) for p in probes),'PG_RECORDED_LIVE_MUTATION_EVIDENCE_INVALID')
    compatibility=observation['eventCompatibility']
    require(all(b['accepted'] for b in compatibility['oldBranchResults']) and len(compatibility['oldBranchResults'])==4
            and compatibility['replacementOwnerAclPreserved'] and compatibility['replacementRolledBack'], 'PG_RECORDED_EVENT_COMPATIBILITY_INVALID')
    require(compatibility['branchStatementSha256']==digest(compatibility['branchStatement']) and compatibility['shapeStatementSha256']==digest(compatibility['shapeStatement']),'PG_EVENT_STATEMENT_HASH_MISMATCH')


def mutations(p, c, model, migration):
    probes = []
    def run(name, edit, expected):
        pp, cc = copy.deepcopy(p), copy.deepcopy(c)
        edit(pp, cc)
        try:
            validate(pp, cc, model, migration)
        except Failure as exc:
            code = str(exc)
            probes.append({"name": name, "expectedCode": expected, "actualCode": code, "killed": code.startswith(expected)})
        else:
            probes.append({"name": name, "expectedCode": expected, "actualCode": "MUTATION_SURVIVED", "killed": False})
    run("wrong_output_name", lambda p,c: p["families"][0].__setitem__("identity", "public.wrong_decisions"), "PERSISTENCE_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    run("wrong_output_width", lambda p,c: p["families"][0]["columns"][0].__setitem__("sqlType", "varchar(255)"), "PERSISTENCE_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    run("wrong_source_width", lambda p,c: c["relations"][0]["orm"]["columns"][0]["type"].__setitem__("sqlType", "varchar(255)"), "SOURCE_COLUMN_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    run("wrong_nullability", lambda p,c: p["families"][0]["columns"][0].__setitem__("nullable", True), "PERSISTENCE_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    run("wrong_server_default", lambda p,c: p["families"][0]["columns"][0].__setitem__("serverDefault", "gen_random_uuid()"), "PERSISTENCE_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    owner = next(i for i,x in enumerate(c["selections"]) if x["selectionId"] == "owner:ad_v4_candidate_app_product_scopes")
    run("dropped_projection_anchor", lambda p,c: c["selections"][owner]["query"]["where"]["args"].pop(0), "SELECTION_SCOPE_MISMATCH")
    run("dropped_owner_join", lambda p,c: c["selections"][owner]["query"]["joins"][1]["on"].pop(), "SELECTION_JOIN_MISMATCH")
    run("shortened_row_identity", lambda p,c: p["families"][2]["rowIdentity"].pop(), "PERSISTENCE_ROW_IDENTITY_MISMATCH")
    run("omitted_family", lambda p,c: p["families"].pop(), "PERSISTENCE_FAMILY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH")
    run("omitted_column", lambda p,c: p["families"][0]["columns"].pop(), "PERSISTENCE_COLUMN_INVENTORY_MISMATCH")
    run("extra_undeclared_column", lambda p,c: p["families"][0]["columns"].append(dict(p["families"][0]["columns"][0], name="extra")), "PERSISTENCE_COLUMN_INVENTORY_MISMATCH")
    run("event_0029_branch_incompatibility", lambda p,c: p["families"][6]["delta0030"].__setitem__("oldContractVersion", "paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1"), "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    run("event_0029_sql_check_branch_incompatibility", lambda p,c: next(x for x in p["families"][6]["checks"] if x["name"] == "ck_ar4_event_union").__setitem__("expression", "event_type='candidate_only_accepted'"), "EVENT_0029_BRANCH_INCOMPATIBLE")
    run("event_0029_nullable_predecessor", lambda p,c: next(x for x in p["families"][6]["columns"] if x["name"] == "predecessor_event_hash").__setitem__("nullable", False), "PERSISTENCE_SHAPE_MISMATCH")
    run("event_0029_acl_incompatibility", lambda p,c: p["families"][6]["delta0030"].__setitem__("preserveFunctionAcl", False), "EVENT_0029_ACL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    run("event_0029_new_null_columns_in_canonical_record", lambda p,c: p["families"][6]["delta0030"]["legacyCanonicalProjection"].__setitem__("dropBeforeCanonicalization", []), "EVENT_0029_CANONICAL_INCOMPATIBLE")
    return probes


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--disposable-postgres-url',help='Explicit loopback paprnav_bootstrap database, never a production URL')
    parser.add_argument('--live-catalog-mutations',action='store_true',help='Rollback-only DDL probes; requires the explicit disposable URL')
    parser.add_argument('--json-schema-python',default=JSON_SCHEMA_PYTHON,help='Existing interpreter with conforming jsonschema Draft 2020-12; no package installation')
    parser.add_argument('--verify-saved-result',action='store_true',help='Validate all current authority inventories including the saved result mirrors, without regenerating it')
    args=parser.parse_args()
    require(not args.live_catalog_mutations or args.disposable_postgres_url is not None,'CATALOG_DISPOSABLE_TARGET_REQUIRED')
    p = strict_json((RUN / "acceptance-persistence-v1.json").read_text())
    c = strict_json((RUN / "acceptance-source-catalog-v1.json").read_text())
    persistence_schema = strict_json((RUN / 'acceptance-persistence.schema.json').read_text())
    output_authorities={'artifacts':[{'path':path,'sha256':sha(ROOT/path)} for path in RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATHS], 'sources':c.get('sources')}
    if args.verify_saved_result:
        output_authorities=strict_json((RUN/'acceptance-persistence-bootstrap-results.json').read_text())
    registries=authority_registries(p,c,persistence_schema,output_authorities)
    # Exact inventories run before generic schema validators, preserving named diagnostics.
    for _,prefix,_,value,expected,scalar in registries:
        validate_authority_inventory(value,expected,prefix,scalar=scalar)
    expected_tuple={'type':'array','minItems':1,'maxItems':1,'items':False,'prefixItems':[{'const':upstream_literal()[0]}]}
    require(upstream_schema_node(persistence_schema)==expected_tuple,'PERSISTENCE_SCHEMA_UPSTREAM_ENTRY_SHAPE_MISMATCH:'+upstream_literal()[0]['path'])
    require(sha(RUN/'acceptance-source-catalog.schema.json')==CATALOG_SCHEMA_SHA256,'SOURCE_CATALOG_SCHEMA_HASH_MISMATCH')
    if args.verify_saved_result:
        print(json.dumps({'status':'PASS_SAVED_RESULT_AUTHORITY_BINDINGS_ONLY','authorityOccurrenceCount':108,'independentApprovalClaimed':False},sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    schema_documents=[]
    for stem, value in (("acceptance-persistence", p), ("acceptance-source-catalog", c)):
        schema = strict_json((RUN / (stem + ".schema.json")).read_text())
        validate_schema_document(schema)
        validate_schema(value, schema)
        schema_documents.append({'schema':schema,'instance':value})
    schema_engine=independent_schema_validation(schema_documents,args.json_schema_python)
    model = fresh_model_catalog()
    migration, raw_sql = fresh_migration_catalog()
    require(c["migrationSqlStatements"] == raw_sql, "SOURCE_MIGRATION_SQL_INVENTORY_MISMATCH")
    validate(p, c, model, migration)
    foundation=validate_foundation(p)
    validate_observed_catalog(c,model)
    probes = mutations(p, c, model, migration)
    scope_probes = selection_scope_probes(c)
    selection_probes=selection_execution_probes(c)
    physical=c['postgresqlObservation']['catalog']
    catalog_probes=postgresql_mutations(physical)
    if args.disposable_postgres_url:
        compare_postgresql(physical,fresh_postgresql_catalog(args.disposable_postgres_url))
    if args.live_catalog_mutations:
        live_probes=live_postgresql_mutations(args.disposable_postgres_url,physical)
        require(live_probes==c['postgresqlObservation']['liveMutationProbes'],'PG_LIVE_MUTATION_REPLAY_MISMATCH')
        event_probe=live_event_compatibility(args.disposable_postgres_url,physical,p['families'][6]['delta0030']['legacyCanonicalProjection']['replacementStatement'])
        require(event_probe==c['postgresqlObservation']['eventCompatibility'],'PG_LIVE_EVENT_REPLAY_MISMATCH')
    discrepancies = known_differences(model, migration)
    physical_discrepancies = [row for row in physical_orm_comparison(model,physical) if row['columnDifferences']]
    blocked = bool(discrepancies or physical_discrepancies or p["blockers"] or not all(x["killed"] for x in probes+catalog_probes) or not all(x.get("killed", x.get("pass", False)) for x in scope_probes+selection_probes))
    result = {"status": "BLOCKED" if blocked else "VALIDATED_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW",
              "bootstrapInputStatus": "BLOCKED" if blocked else "FOUNDATIONAL_PERSISTENCE_DAG_VALIDATED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW",
              "schemaValidation": "PASS", "modelComparison": "PASS", "migrationDeclarationComparison": "PASS",
              "postgresqlCatalogComparison": {'status':'LIVE_EXACT_MATCH' if args.disposable_postgres_url else 'FROZEN_OBSERVATION_REPLAY_VALIDATED',
                  'liveConnectionExecutedThisRun':bool(args.disposable_postgres_url),'liveMutationExecutionThisRun':args.live_catalog_mutations,
                  'freshCatalogSha256':digest(physical),'queryInventorySha256':digest(PG_QUERIES),
                  'relations':len(physical['relations']),'columns':sum(len(r['columns']) for r in physical['relations']),
                  'constraints':sum(len(r['constraints']) for r in physical['relations']),'indexes':sum(len(r['indexes']) for r in physical['relations']),
                  'triggers':sum(len(r['triggers']) for r in physical['relations']),'functions':len(physical['functions']),
                  'recordedLiveMutationProbes':c['postgresqlObservation']['liveMutationProbes'],
                  'recordedEventCompatibility':c['postgresqlObservation']['eventCompatibility'],
                  'freshMigrationCommands':p['authorityDagRefresh']['commands'],
                  'frozenCatalogHistoricalCommands':c['postgresqlObservation']['commands'],
                  'currentDisposableDatabase':p['authorityDagRefresh']['disposableDatabase']}, "productionImplementationPermitted": False,
              'bootstrapApprovalClaimed':False,
              'independentSbiB001ClosureClaimed':False,
              'overallSlice4BDesignApproved':False, 'currentMappingResourcePermitted':False,
              'openHighFindings':['H-004','H-005'],
              "modelRouting": DAG_ROUTING,
              'modelAssignments':DAG_MODEL_ASSIGNMENTS,
              'foundationValidation':foundation,'independentSchemaValidation':schema_engine,
              'authorityDagRefresh':p['authorityDagRefresh'],
              'sourceAuthorityDecision':c['sourceAuthorityDecision'],
              'bootstrapCompleteness':p['bootstrapCompleteness'],
              "counts": {"sourceRelations": len(c["relations"]), "sourceColumns": sum(len(r["orm"]["columns"]) for r in c["relations"]), "typedOwners": len(c["typedOwners"]), "sourceSelections": len(c["selections"]), "outputFamilies": len(p["families"]), "outputColumns": sum(len(r["columns"]) for r in p["families"]), "mutationProbes": len(probes), "mutationKills": sum(x["killed"] for x in probes)},
              "mutationProbes": probes, "selectionScopeProbes": scope_probes, 'catalogMutationProbes':catalog_probes,
              'selectionExecutionProbes':selection_probes, "sourceDiscrepancies": discrepancies,
              'physicalOrmColumnDiscrepancies':physical_discrepancies,
              "bootstrapBlockers": p["blockers"],
              "artifacts": [{"path": str((RUN / n).relative_to(ROOT)), "sha256": sha(RUN / n)} for n in ("acceptance-persistence-v1.json", "acceptance-persistence.schema.json", "acceptance-source-catalog-v1.json", "acceptance-source-catalog.schema.json", "acceptance-persistence-bootstrap-validator.py", "acceptance-persistence-bootstrap-provenance.md")],
              "sources": c["sources"], "runtime": {"pythonVersion": sys.version.split()[0], "executable": str(Path(sys.executable).relative_to(ROOT)) if Path(sys.executable).is_relative_to(ROOT) else sys.executable, "importedModules": sorted(sys.modules)},
              "command": "PYTHONPATH=backend PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PAPRNAV_DISABLE_DOTENV=1 backend/.venv/bin/python3 .ai/review-runs/T081-V4-SCHEMA-SLICE-4B/acceptance-persistence-bootstrap-validator.py" + (' --disposable-postgres-url '+args.disposable_postgres_url if args.disposable_postgres_url else '') + (' --live-catalog-mutations' if args.live_catalog_mutations else '')}
    result['counts'].update({'catalogMutationProbes':len(catalog_probes),'catalogMutationKills':sum(x['killed'] for x in catalog_probes),
                            'selectionExecutionControls':sum(x.get('pass',False) for x in selection_probes),
                            'selectionExecutionMutationProbes':sum('killed' in x for x in selection_probes),
                            'selectionExecutionMutationKills':sum(x.get('killed',False) for x in selection_probes),
                            'recordedLiveCatalogMutationProbes':13,'recordedLiveCatalogMutationKills':13})
    result['authorityFreshness']=authority_freshness_probes(authority_registries(p,c,persistence_schema,result))
    result['authoritySemanticControls']=authority_semantic_controls(p)
    require(result['authorityFreshness']['freshnessKillCount']==652 and all(x['killed'] for x in result['authoritySemanticControls']), 'AUTHORITY_MUTATION_SURVIVED_OR_WRONG_DIAGNOSTIC')
    result['counts'].update({key:result['authorityFreshness'][key] for key in ('authorityOccurrenceCount','freshnessProbeCount','freshnessKillCount','freshnessSurvivorCount','freshnessWrongDiagnosticCount','freshnessGenericExceptionKillCount')})
    result.update({key:result['authorityFreshness'][key] for key in ('authorityOccurrenceCount','freshnessProbeCount','freshnessKillCount','freshnessSurvivorCount','freshnessWrongDiagnosticCount','freshnessGenericExceptionKillCount')})
    result['counts']['authoritySemanticControlCount']=27
    result['counts']['authoritySemanticControlKills']=sum(x['killed'] for x in result['authoritySemanticControls'])
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 2 if result["status"] == "BLOCKED" else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except Failure as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"status": "FAIL", "code": str(exc)}))
        raise SystemExit(1)

# Candidate-only acceptance persistence requirements, version 1

Requirement version: `paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-persistence-requirements-1`.
Status: proposed immutable foundational requirements; independent review is
required. This document defines requirements for a later persistence contract
subject. It does not approve that subject, install a schema, or authorize use.

## Model routing and authority boundary

Designer runtime: `/root/v4_s4b_design_integrator`. Requested route:
`gpt-6-astra`, `xhigh`. Actual model: `model not exposed by runtime`. Actual
effort: `effort not exposed`. Trigger: standalone persistence foundation after
an indirect authority-cycle finding. No fallback or independent approval is
claimed.

This leaf was authored from the architecture reassessment and retained
persistence design decisions. Its complete normative content is contained
here; it incorporates no external document. In particular it has no dependency
on an aggregate decision document, acceptance matrix, semantic program,
resource-accounting declaration, validator, result, or future review. Those
later artifacts may consume this leaf; their contents and candidate hashes
cannot supply or change its requirements. Once independently frozen, changing
these requirements requires a new version and a separately reviewed migration
of consumers. Do not edit the frozen version in place.

## 1. Purpose, non-authority and source authority

Persistence records independent human acceptance of one exact candidate-only
review request and its complete verified source graph. The retained
classification is always `candidate_only`; `release_blocked` is true,
`authority_effect` is `none`, and `release_blocker` is
`candidate_only_not_release_authority`. No state introduced here means
actionable, released, published, selected, current, or aircraft-specific
authority. Semantic readiness is separately restricted to `candidate_only`
or `human_determination_required`, with the latter more restrictive.

Only verified V4 candidate/evidence, applicability, obligation and review-case
sources may supply authority. The source catalog must independently record the
actual installed schema through revision 0029, ORM metadata and migration
declarations, including exact relation/column identities, types, widths,
nullability, defaults, keys, foreign keys, checks, indexes, functions, triggers,
owners and grants. Preserve the existing 74 selected relations, 983 source
columns, 28 typed owners and 77 anchored source selections for this version.
Reference-only foreign-key metadata is not payload permission. Disagreement
between installed physical facts and application metadata blocks acceptance;
neither a suffix convention nor a generated copy is an independent authority.

No new relation, foreign key, join, fallback, mutation or cascade may confer
authority on V1/V2/V3 or released consumers. Identifiers are interpreted through
typed, table-scoped lookups; a miss is final. Acceptance changes no earlier
candidate, projection, released, search, matching, coverage, compliance or due
state. Existing feature-gate rows retain only their established latest-change
attribution; no additional immutable gate-history claim is inferred.

## 2. Closed physical and transient responsibility

The persistence contract subject must expand exactly the following nine
families and 201 ordered fields. The six first authority families and sentinel
are seven new physical relations; the event family extends one existing
physical relation; pending copies are memory records, never SQL or ORM rows.

| Family | Exact identity | Fields |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| decision_version | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_versions | 65 |
| node_gate | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_node_gates | 20 |
| dependency | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_dependencies | 9 |
| external_dependency | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_external_dependencies | 27 |
| authorship_binding | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_authorship_bindings | 7 |
| acceptance_signoff | public.ad_v4_candidate_acceptance_signoffs | 37 |
| acceptance_event | public.ad_v4_review_case_events | 28 |
| validation_sentinel | public.ad_v4_candidate_decision_validation_sentinels | 3 |
| pending_copy | memory.acceptance_pending_copies | 5 |

The complete ordered field-name inventories are:

These are requirements, not an instantiated SQL schema. Before the subject
can be approved it must declare every leaf fact for every field: exact SQL
type and width/precision/timezone, logical type, independent character/octet
bounds, physical NULL permission, server and application default or explicit
none, closed enums/checks, and canonical encoding. Transient fields declare
`sqlType:null`, a logical encoding and no SQL relation. No field name implies
a storage type. Character limits are not byte limits; SQL NULL, JSON null,
absence, empty values, false and zero are distinct. Unbounded physical text
must not be mislabeled as physically bounded text.

The subject must also explicitly declare ordered PK/unique/FK/index tuples,
predicates, referenced columns, match/update/delete behavior, deferrability,
check expressions, permitted operations, owners/ACLs, row/canonical field
order, hash domains, anchors and source paths. No unresolved group such as
“the relevant projection fields” may replace a declaration. Physical FK gaps
for polymorphic slices or source tables must be identified and enforced by
independent typed SQL branches; they may not be labeled nonexistent FKs.

## 3. Identity, cardinality and immutable evidence

- Decision PK is `id`; case, request and `(proposal_id,
  acceptance_contract_version)` are unique. One pending request binds exactly
  one accepted decision, one signoff, one terminal event and one sentinel.
- Node identity is `(decision_version_id,node_slice,semantic_node_id)`.
  Both frozen semantic inventories have an exact bijection to node rows;
  parent, type, key, source pointer, ordinal, value/identity hashes and exact
  ordered evidence-set hash/count must match the selected source occurrence.
- Dependency identity is `(decision_version_id,parent_slice,parent_node_id,
  edge_kind,child_slice,child_node_id,canonical_ordinal)`. Both endpoints belong
  to the same decision and exact bound projections. Missing, extra, duplicate,
  reordered or differently described nodes/edges fail, even at equal counts.
- External identity is `(decision_version_id,source_change_node_id)`; every
  bound change node has exactly one row. The six disjoint branches are outgoing
  resolved; outgoing unresolved with reason successor identity unknown, not
  this proposal, or target unresolved; outgoing ambiguous with multiple
  predecessors; and incoming resolved. Resolved outgoing rows bind complete
  target identity/hash/version/head and the exact reciprocal incoming row;
  incoming resolved rows bind their exact source dependency and source
  projection metadata. Unresolved/ambiguous rows forbid target/source/reciprocal
  metadata, retain controlled reasons, and never invent a resolved endpoint.
- Authorship identity is `(decision_version_id,source_table,source_id,user_id,
  authorship_role)`. Tuples are exactly all candidate submission actors, bound
  fragment creators and bound fragment admission actors at the frozen cutoff.
  Requesters and draft authors do not become semantic authors merely by role.
- Signoff PK is `id`; decision/case/request are unique. Freeze exact scoped
  actor/membership/action/policy/idempotency uniqueness and composite ownership
  tuples in the subject. Event PK and case/sequence identity remain unchanged.
- Sentinel identity is its decision FK/PK. Generation is integer, required,
  initially zero, bounded 0–256; sealed is required boolean initially false.
- Pending identity is `(decision_version_id,family_id,row_ordinal)`: exactly
  one canonical authority-row frame copy for each decision/node/dependency/
  external/authorship/signoff/event row; no sentinel or recursive pending copy.
  Ordinals follow canonical full-frame order within a family. Lifetime is one
  transaction after preflight; discard on commit/rollback, never cache/retry
  or persist these records. A flush does not create another occurrence.

Row identity includes each declared join occurrence. Shared source bindings
are not deduplicated by physical identity. Anchored outer inventories and
anti-join witnesses must detect foreign, missing, orphan, wrong-type and
duplicate rows that successful inner joins could hide. All authority rows
reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. No repair, silent coercion or fallback is
allowed. New IDs are explicit, with no implicit sequences or unlisted defaults.

## 4. Canonical binding and event compatibility

Persist all frozen candidate/evidence/version, projection/head, cutoff/authorship,
requested/current observation, graph count/set, readiness/non-authority,
authorization, decision/signoff/event bindings named in §2. Every digest binds
an explicitly specified, bounded canonical preimage and separate domain.
Ordered full tuple equality is required in addition to counts and digests.
Node sets order by slice/source pointer/type/key/identity; dependencies by
parent slice/identity/kind/ordinal/child slice/identity; external rows by source
change node; authorship by source table/source ID/user/role. Specify binary
ordering, NULL order and final identity tie-breakers; locale defaults cannot
change persisted meaning.

Allocate decision/signoff/event IDs before hashing. Source verification and
child hashes precede graph-set hashes, decision content/row hash, signoff
signature/row hash, terminal event hash and pending frame hashes. No preimage
includes its own digest. The subject must explicitly list excluded hash/byte
fields, representation of nested payload digests, and every event predecessor.
The internal signature binds decision, frozen request, current and requested
observations, authorization, authorship and signing time; it is an integrity
digest, not PKI or legal non-repudiation.

Retain the complete 26-column 0029 event shape and append only nullable
`candidate_decision_id` and `acceptance_signoff_id`, without defaults. Physical
nullable predecessor/request fields stay nullable; acceptance requires them.
For acceptance: event is `candidate_only_accepted`, resulting state is
`candidate_only`; request, predecessor hash, decision and acceptance signoff
are required; draft, rejection and rejection-signoff IDs are forbidden.
All earlier event kinds retain their original union predicates, versions,
ordering, hashes, uniqueness and object/event completeness. Older event kinds
require both new fields NULL and use `paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-review-1`;
acceptance uses `paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1`.

Old column-named inserts omit the two new columns successfully when acceptance
is disabled. Whole-record old canonicalization must explicitly project out
only those new columns before reconstructing the old preimage; appending SQL
NULLs must not alter historical hashes. Retain prior immutable triggers and
their function bindings. Constrain prior guard/completeness triggers to their
original event branches and add exact acceptance triggers. Preserve every
observed owner, function ACL, explicit grantee/privilege/grant-option and legacy
function behavior except the specifically declared canonical projection repair.
The subject must list exact changed check/index/trigger/function definitions,
with before/after and downgrade restoration, rather than reset privileges.

## 5. Trusted owner and transaction lifecycle

New authority relations are owned by a dedicated non-login, non-superuser,
non-BYPASSRLS trusted role. Runtime owns no authority objects and cannot assume
the trusted owner or migration owner. Runtime receives only explicitly needed
authority SELECT/INSERT; PUBLIC and runtime have no sentinel DML/SELECT,
trusted-function EXECUTE, schema/trigger DDL or sequence escape. Trusted trigger
functions are security definers with fixed hardened search paths and qualified
relation access. Preserve existing event/function grants while making any
ownership transition explicit; deployment role differences require review.

Every authority insertion participates in mandatory sentinel validation.
Statement-level transition tables register/dirty at most once per statement;
sealed decisions reject later writes. Deferred validation independently derives
the final full graph exactly once and seals the sentinel. Subsequent callbacks
are constant-time, including after constraints are forced immediate. Missing
triggers, direct sentinel manipulation, premature sealing, partial events and
unauthorized owners must fail. Catalog inspection must cover every authority
table/trigger/function and actual runtime memberships, not only happy-path use.

Acceptance is one atomic transaction from `pending_review` to terminal
candidate-only state. The frozen request, latest event and stable input identity
must match compare-and-swap inputs. Every candidate/evidence/projection component
is freshly verified; timed observations can differ while stable identity stays
equal. Retained source bytes, source lifecycles, cutoff and authorship must be
rederived, not trusted from page load or caller-provided aggregate values.

The signer is an active user with active matching membership and platform-admin
role under the recorded policy. Server authorization is repeated after actor/
membership locks and at deferred commit. The signer occurs in no authorship
tuple. One independent human signoff is required; no self-review override or
machine-signature shortcut is permitted.

Acquire one global stable lock order: actor then membership; scoped idempotency;
candidate relationship graph; proposal; ordered feature gates; evidence;
globally sorted bound/external projection IDs and their heads; case/request;
decision/children; signoff/event. Preflight discovers the complete external
metadata set before locking, never chases new locks out of order, and rechecks
target heads/reciprocals at commit. A changed target set rolls back and retries.
No target proposal/typed-owner/evidence payload is loaded by metadata traversal.

Exact idempotent retries return the original result; a reused key with different
canonical bytes conflicts. Concurrent accept/reject or accept/accept commits at
most one terminal branch with no partial graph. Accepted cases cannot acquire
later drafts/rejection/acceptance or a same-proposal successor. Rejected cases
retain their original successor rule. Corrections create new candidates/cases;
they do not mutate or promote accepted evidence. Draft intent remains exactly
`undecided|reject`; a frozen reject intent blocks acceptance.

## 6. Fail-closed reconstruction, capacity and compatibility

Independent database logic verifies source-to-output equality both ways,
object/event bijection, hashes/canonical bytes, reference ownership, closed
union shapes, cycles, authorization and signer exclusion. Effective readiness
is the most restrictive base or propagating descendant; integrity-only edges
resolve without propagating. Noncontrolling nodes remain fully verified.
Generated constants or caller hashes cannot alone establish correctness.

Historical reads are bounded, read-only repeatable-read transactions. Dispatch
the frozen source/canonical/version semantics and reconstruct every retained
binding, row, set, lifecycle and signature. Unsupported/unavailable historical
authority or any corruption fails closed. Current eligibility uses separate
live heads/authorization; it never replaces frozen historical membership or
rewrites past validity. No read repairs state. Pages retain exact ordering and
never silently truncate a failed verification.

Count and byte preflights precede payload loading/large allocations/writes and
are independently enforced at construction, commit and read. Pending and stored
occurrences have exact identity accounting; terminal-event source/output overlap
compares all shared old columns before charging one output occurrence. Frozen
retained-document identity/size/hash must match actual streams. Capacity failure
leaves the case pending/rejectable and rolls back all acceptance outputs.
These requirements do not prescribe a downstream accounting artifact as input.

Upgrade is additive from 0029, default-disabled, with no backfill, automatic
acceptance, row rewrite or V3 freeze. Disabled upgraded deployments preserve
0029 old-binary reads and named inserts. Acceptance may be enabled only with
compatible readers/writers; an old binary must never interpret unknown accepted
states as rejected or released. Native/ORM/catalog definitions must agree.

Physical downgrade requires both acceptance application/database gates false,
all seven new physical relations empty, no acceptance event and no unsealed
sentinel. Retained acceptance evidence causes explicit downgrade refusal; it
is never deleted, demoted or translated to rejection to make downgrade succeed.
Only then restore exact 0029 column order/checks/indexes/trigger and function
definitions/owners/ACLs from a verified pre-upgrade snapshot. Logical disable
leaves immutable accepted evidence available through compatible readers.

Before deployment require independent physical/ORM/constraint/owner/ACL parity,
direct-SQL corruption and branch coverage, old-binary disabled compatibility,
upgrade/downgrade refusal/restoration, concurrency/idempotency and read-only
reconstruction evidence. These are obligations for the later subject and
implementation, not claims that this requirements leaf has executed them.

## P00 — Foundational boundary

All normative persistence requirements of this version are present in this leaf.
It incorporates no other document, executable, result, review, or future subject.
The complete literals below are independently reviewable proposed requirements.
Hashes of candidate declarations cannot establish or change these requirements.
Consumers must compare their declarations with these facts and with separately
observed source-catalog facts. A requirement change requires a new reviewed leaf.

## P01 — Purpose, non-authority and source authority

Persistence records independent human acceptance of one exact candidate-only
review request and its complete verified source graph. The retained

state. Existing feature-gate rows retain only their established latest-change
attribution; no additional immutable gate-history claim is inferred.

states as rejected or released. Native/ORM/catalog definitions must agree.

Physical downgrade requires both acceptance application/database gates false,
all seven new physical relations empty, no acceptance event and no unsealed
sentinel. Retained acceptance evidence causes explicit downgrade refusal; it
is never deleted, demoted or translated to rejection to make downgrade succeed.
Only then restore exact 0029 column order/checks/indexes/trigger and function
definitions/owners/ACLs from a verified pre-upgrade snapshot. Logical disable
leaves immutable accepted evidence available through compatible readers.

Before deployment require independent physical/ORM/constraint/owner/ACL parity,
direct-SQL corruption and branch coverage, old-binary disabled compatibility,
upgrade/downgrade refusal/restoration, concurrency/idempotency and read-only
reconstruction evidence. These are obligations for the later subject and
implementation, not claims that this requirements leaf has executed them.

## P07 — Exact limits and authorization constants

All upper bounds are inclusive; cap+1 must fail before the next payload fetch,
frame allocation or write. The complete scalar count/byte ceilings are:

| Quantity | Minimum | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Decisions per accepted case/request/proposal-contract | 1 | 1 |
| Combined stored semantic nodes in accepted root | 1 | 20000 |
| Dependency rows | 0 | 40000 |
| External rows | 0 | 2000 |
| Authorship rows/count and binding count | 0 | 2000 |
| Signoffs, acceptance events, sentinels per accepted decision | 1 | 1 |
| Pending copies; seven authority families only | 0 | 64003 |
| Dirty generation | 0 | 256 |
| Graph work, including declared copies/reserves | 0 | 67108864 octets |
| Canonical byte column and bounded text octets | 0 | 1048576 |
| Existing event auth/request/canonical byte columns | 2 | 1048576 |
| Case-history draft phase | 0 | 16777216 octets |
| Case-history requested phase | 0 | 29360128 octets |
| Case-history terminal phase | 0 | 41943040 octets |
| Graph response page | 0 | 1000 rows |
| Encoded response/reserve | 0 | 1048576 octets |
| Stream chunk/reserve | 0 | 65536 octets |
| Individual pending row frame | 0 | 67108864 octets |
| Bound retained-document stream | 0 | 67108864 octets |
| Checked accounting integer | 0 | 9223372036854775807 |
| JSON depth | 0 | 64 |
| JSON nodes | 0 | 75000 |
| JSON container members | 0 | 2000 |
| Existing case event sequence | 0 | 1002 |

The pending maximum is 1+20000+40000+2000+2000+1+1=64003; an accepted
graph's actual pending count equals the exact seven-family sum, not an optional
zero. A node-family minimum of zero below permits an individual empty slice;
the accepted combined root still requires at least one node. All per-family
cardinality minima/maxima and equality rules in P08 also apply. Counts do not
permit malformed empty graphs. A full row frame is not a one-MiB column.
Physical PostgreSQL integer remains signed 32-bit; canonical integer encoding
is signed 64-bit. Ordinals/counts are nonnegative and bounded by their owning
family/sequence and PostgreSQL width. The 64 MiB work ceiling is deterministic
charged occurrences, not a claim of exact process RSS or database tuple size.

Canonical-history phase sums use actual nonnull bytea octets for the bound case.
The acceptance event participates once in the terminal history sum and once in
its declared graph-output occurrence; exact source/output identity overlap must
compare every shared old column before excluding a duplicate source occurrence.
The decision/signoff remain charged in the total graph budget. Bound document
streams require identical ID/content-hash/storage-size tuples and actual stream
size/hash equality; external-target documents are forbidden. Sorting, scalar
reports, output/pending copies, stream and response reserves are charged before
their next allocation; no hidden full-value sizing materialization is allowed.

| Authorization/API/gate fact | Exact value |
| --- | --- |
| Human command and signoff action | `accept_candidate_only` |
| Endpoint authorization action | `accept_ad_v4_candidate_only` |
| Policy name | `paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1` |
| Policy version | string `1` |
| Validity rule | `status_only_v1` |
| Actor role | `platform_admin` |
| User and matching membership statuses | `active`, `active` |
| Authorized snapshot assertion | `serverAuthorized=true` |
| Acceptance POST | `/ads/v4/review-cases/{case_id}/accept-candidate` |
| Immutable decision GET | `/ads/v4/candidate-decisions/{decision_version_id}` |
| Database write gate, initial value | `reviewer4_candidate_acceptance_enabled=false` |
| Application write flag, initial value | `PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE4B_ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED=false` |
| App-off POST | HTTP 404, `capability_disabled` before mutation |
| App-on, DB-off POST | HTTP 409, `reviewer4_candidate_acceptance_gate_disabled` |
| Capacity failure | `acceptance_capacity_exceeded`; pending/rejectable; no writes |
| Frozen reject-intent failure | `review_intent_conflict` |

The complete closed API body keys are `expectedAuthorizationObservationHash`,
`expectedPredecessorEventHash`, `expectedRequestId`, `expectedInputIdentityHash`,
and `action`. No client-supplied graph, classification, independence or gate is
accepted. The authorization snapshot contains exactly the ordered 19 keys:
`version,policyName,policyVersion,action,actorUserId,authorizingMembershipId,
organizationId,userStatus,membershipStatus,role,validityRule,validFrom,validUntil,
userUpdatedAt,membershipUpdatedAt,serverAuthorized,decisionTime,
authorizationObservationHash,claimsHash`. Validity is status-only; validFrom and
validUntil are null. Snapshot version is
`paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-authorization-1`; its action is the endpoint action.
Actor/membership/organization IDs and timestamps are exact locked source values;
claims, observation and snapshot digests are recomputed under separate domains.
One independent human signature is required and sufficient for retention.
`signed_at=accepted_at=occurred_at`; event auth/request/idempotency fields equal
the signoff, and the signoff decision_hash equals the decision row_hash.

## P08 — Closed field and relation facts

The following expanded facts are normative literals. They are stored here to
make the foundation complete; no consumer may discover missing facts from its
own declaration. Timestamp precision is six fractional digits with timezone,
finite UTC instants from year 0001 inclusive to year 10000 exclusive. Numeric
SQL precision/scale is absent for these output fields. Every physical field has
server/application default `none`, except sentinel generation `0` and sealed
`false`; every memory field has no SQL default. Physical text is unbounded
PostgreSQL text with the separate stated octet work constraint.

### P08-external-version-dispatch

When present, `target_materializer_version` and `source_materializer_version`
are exactly `paprnav-ad-v4-app-materializer-2` for this version, compared against
the frozen corresponding projection. NULL remains mandatory in the forbidden
X01-X06 arms. No arbitrary version64 string grants historical verifier support.
The same closed versions in the field tables apply inside canonical payloads,
not only to SQL scalar columns. Unsupported versions fail without substituting
current implementations. Decision binding also requires exact 3B-to-3A
projection ID, hash and materializer equality.

SQL ownership is not permission to mutate immutable authority evidence: mandatory
guards still reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. `s4b_runtime` has only SELECT/INSERT
on authority relations; it and PUBLIC have no sentinel access or trusted
function EXECUTE. `s4b_login` inherits only `s4b_runtime`. Neither runtime role
has schema CREATE, DDL, sequence access, owner membership or BYPASSRLS. The
trusted role's source privileges are SELECT only except column UPDATE(id) on
users/memberships solely to obtain row locks; its functions must never execute
source UPDATE. Catalog/actual-login attack verification is mandatory.

The register/dirty/validate functions define the one-shot sentinel mechanism;
event guard/dirty, reject-mutation and require-complete are explicit additional
functions with the same hardened owner/ACL/search_path boundary. There is no
claim that the earlier three-function topology exercise implements these seven
production functions. Generation 257, missing sentinel, presealed sentinel,
late child, trigger omission/disable, partial event, and direct sentinel access
must all fail. Deferred validation runs one complete final-graph check and later
callbacks are constant-time, even under SET CONSTRAINTS IMMEDIATE.

The old event union and complete physical shape are fully fixed by P02/P08.
Exactly four old event kinds remain: `case_created`, `draft_saved`,
`review_requested`, `review_rejected`; they yield `draft`, `draft`,
`pending_review`, `rejected` respectively, with the exact field predicates in
P08-acceptance_event. Only `draft_saved` repeats. Every old branch requires
both new IDs NULL. Old rows' canonical preimage excludes exactly the new
candidate_decision_id and acceptance_signoff_id columns before applying its
retained canonicalization; NULL appendage is not hash-compatible by itself.
Sequence zero is case_created with NULL predecessor; later events have a
nonnull predecessor. The acceptance branch requires its exact request and
predecessor and forbids draft/rejection/rejection-signoff IDs.

Existing event relation observations are not normative deployment role names:
preserve each installed explicit grant/grant-option, old trigger binding and
function attributes, while transferring only the event relation to the trusted
owner as declared. Existing implicit owner rights must be explicitly reconciled
so disabled old-binary named INSERTs continue to work. NULL ACL means default
effective privileges, not an empty privilege set. Legacy functions keep their
owners, ACLs, security/search-path attributes and definitions except the exact
two-column canonical projection and branch-scoped guards/completeness needed
for the new union. Record before/after/rollback catalog facts; never reset ACLs
wholesale. No old branch changes its action, authorization, default or hash.

## P10 — Atomic acceptance, readers, rollout and preservation

The acceptance transaction requires existing Slice-4 read/draft/decision
capabilities and the new acceptance capability. Fresh server authorization runs
before writes, after actor/membership locks and at deferred commit. It verifies
pending case history, exact frozen request/latest event, every CAS field,
verified current candidate/evidence/3A/3B observations, cutoff/authorship equality,
signer exclusion, count/byte preflight, and independent version-dispatched
reconstruction. It constructs complete node/dependency/external/authorship sets,
computes maximum semantic readiness and fixed candidate-only retention, appends
decision/graph/signoff/event, flushes, forces deferred constraints immediate,
normalizes only allowlisted integrity/concurrency SQLSTATEs, restores deferred
mode and commits. Exact retry returns the original verified result.

The global lock order is actor then membership; scoped idempotency advisory;
directive candidate-relationship advisory; proposal row; validator-2, 3A, 3B,
Slice-4 draft, Slice-4 decision, then 4B gates; evidence bindings/fragments/
lifecycle by stable ID; all bound/transitive external-target projection IDs
ascending (slice_rank,projection_id) and root/head rows in the same order;
direct 3A children then direct 3B children; locked tuple/head/reciprocal recheck;
case advisory/root, frozen request, latest event; decision and children by
composite identity; acceptance signoff and terminal event. No earlier lock can
be acquired later. Discovery changes cause full rollback and preflight retry.
Every materializer writing reciprocal dependencies follows this order. Commit
rechecks actor/membership, all bound/target heads/reciprocals, request/latest
event, and final sets. Deadlock/serialization victims return stable retry/
conflict and do not start a second uncoordinated write.

Historical integrity dispatches every recorded version, verifies full event
chain and object bijection, both typed reconstructions, exact sets, source
existence, signature and canonical bytes. Current eligibility compares live
heads and present authorization independently. Deactivation or staleness never
rewrites historical evidence. Missing source bytes fail distinctly, with no
substitution or repair. GETs are bounded read-only REPEATABLE READ and pages use
stable decision-bound cursors; queues stay summary-only. Responses always carry
releaseBlocked=true, authorityEffect=none and the fixed releaseBlocker in
canonical bytes. Supporting-document admission, evaluators, normalized-identity
approval, UI, aircraft determinations, automatic acceptance/backfill, publication,
current selection, V3 freeze and all released consumers remain outside this slice.

Migration 0030 is expand-only after 0029, installs neither enabled gate, preserves
all 0029 rows/branches and creates no backfill. Rollout is: gates off; migrate;
deploy all 0030-aware replicas; run 0029 regressions; enable application flag;
enable DB gate; exercise one nonproduction acceptance/verified GET. An old 0029
binary is permitted only while 4B is disabled and unoccupied; there is no
mixed-version write period after enablement. Disabled GET serves only existing
4B rows and otherwise ordinary 404; both disabled combinations preserve exact
0029 request/reject/draft/list/detail behavior and forbid any new 4B value.

Operational rollback disables DB then application gate and retains compatible
readers. Physical downgrade takes bounded table-first locks and refuses any
enabled gate, occupied new authority/sentinel relation, acceptance event or
unsealed sentinel. Test all four gate combinations, each occupied relation,
forged event without root, unsealed sentinel and empty disabled database. Only
empty disabled downgrade succeeds and must restore exact 0029 functions,
constraints, triggers, schemas, gate inventory, owners/ACLs and retained row
validity against a fresh 0029 database. Never delete signed history.

No existing V1/V2/V3 or released/search/matching/coverage/compliance/due row may
change on acceptance; typed released lookup never falls back to this storage.
Only the acceptance service/API writes these rows. No GET, CRUD/cascade, seed,
fixture loader, worker, CLI, repair, provider or legacy route writes them. Gate
administration uses its existing protocol and records latest changed_at/by only.
The Paprnav production deployment/change-management system and its on-call
operator own immutable gate enable/disable approval and rollout evidence.
Deployment closure must attach it; the mutable gate row is not that audit log.

All runtime proof, independent implementation review and closure review remain
future gates. This leaf fixes their requirements and makes no execution claim.

          "code": "DECISION_SOURCE_BINDING",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Bind case/request/proposal/directive through declared composite FKs; compare requested identity bytes/hash and all recorded versions/hashes against locked proposal and both projections; compare 3B app_projection_id/app_projection_hash/app_materializer_version to the bound 3A row.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        },
        {
          "code": "DECISION_FRESH_CAS",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Lock actor, membership, idempotency, directive graph, proposal, gates, evidence, sorted metadata projection closure, case/request/head; rederive closure after locking and abort transaction on any membership/head/tuple change.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        },
        {
          "code": "DECISION_GRAPH_EQUALITY",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Construct expected node, dependency, external and authorship sets from frozen source selection ASTs and versioned semantics independently in SQL; compare expected EXCEPT ALL stored and stored EXCEPT ALL expected, including empty sets and duplicate identities.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        },
        {
          "code": "DECISION_GRAPH_TOPOLOGY",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Reject cycles before effective gates; compute maximum base/propagating-child readiness, exclude integrity-only edges from propagation and noncontrolling roots from aggregate; require at least one controlling root.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        },
        {
          "code": "DECISION_HASHES",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Recompute every row and set digest, then decision_content_hash and root row_hash using declared hash DAG and exact field order; compare bytes as well as digests.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        },
        {
          "code": "DECISION_RESOURCE",
          "implementation": "independent_SQL",
          "obligation": "Count cap+1 and aggregate scalar widths before payload reads or frame allocation; reject total work above 67108864, canonical blob above 1048576, node above 20000, edge above 40000, external/authors above 2000.",
          "failure": "abort_transaction"
        }
