the [omnibus PASS](adversarial-local-semantic-predicate-oracle-design-remediation-5.md)
on the preceding design hash, but does not extend that approval or resume work.

## Decision and evidence

Adopt a closed, structurally extracted **predicate-obligation inventory** with
explicit semantic registrations and independently declared witnesses. An
assertion site, error code, line number, family name or successful mutation
count is not the inventory unit. Text replacement can construct a test subject;
it cannot establish semantic coverage.

The governing boundary remains the [partition amendment](local-cloud-partition-amendment.md)
and its [Package A PASS](adversarial-local-cloud-partition-amendment.md).
The [first FAIL](adversarial-local-semantic-kernel.md),
[second FAIL](adversarial-local-semantic-kernel-remediation-2.md), and
[third FAIL](adversarial-local-semantic-kernel-remediation-3.md) progressively
establish that generic differences, family coverage and finally source-site
coverage are insufficient. The [finding ledger](findings.json) requires this
design gate before implementation resumes.

The third reviewed subject is the current
[kernel](local-semantic-kernel/semantic_kernel.py), SHA-256
`36d3628c3e55a15351eb26f51e0277850495355b61c483907a7cb9b5eaeab22d`, and
[harness](local-semantic-kernel/semantic_harness.py), SHA-256
`8e40f58f49fc722b0673a67d1503526752fd7aab93e06333888d0deaeed886a3`.
Its third-review results had SHA-256
`b307e4f8ed87fc2fd675476c35904ab86ba8b0800b7f8d8fbc2ffec31e981041`,
and reported 88 sites and 299 cases; those totals are historical, not a target or
coverage certificate for this design. Current survivor sets grouped from case
ownership must be replaced by observed counterfactual runs.

## Inventory, IDs and atomicity

An inventory row is one **proof obligation**: a semantic predicate at a bound
source occurrence, with a particular boundary alternative and finite authority
parameter. Its key is `(predicateId, occurrenceId, boundaryId, parameterId)`.
Example semantic names are `selection.node.projection_matches_binding` and
`schema.required.entry_is_string`; names encode meaning, never line order.
Occurrence IDs identify stable named functions/roles or mapping/schema JSON
pointers. Boundary IDs distinguish missing/extra, lower/upper, empty/nonempty,
and each accepted/rejected alternative. A moved expression retains its semantic
ID but receives a refreshed structural binding; changed meaning requires a new
ID and explicit retired-ID crosswalk. IDs are never silently reused.

One predicate expresses a separately falsifiable requirement on an input,
decision or output. Conjuncts with distinct coordinates are separate; tuple
equality splits by coordinate; bounds split by endpoint; exact set equality
splits into missing and extra membership and, where material, duplicate
multiplicity. A quantifier's body and empty-domain behavior are separate.
Repeated runtime rows instantiate a parameterized obligation; they do not
invent unbounded new IDs. Every finite schema/rule/field variant with distinct
authority must nevertheless be enumerated, not sampled away.

Arithmetic steps are not automatically separate invariants. For a derived
identity, the contractual preimage coordinates, slice domain, table tag,
canonical encoding, hash relation, prefix and truncation/output relation are
meaningful obligations when a permitted corruption can distinguish them.
Temporary variables, caching and equivalent loop mechanics may be classified
as implementation details only with an explicit binding to the covered result
or an equivalence rationale. No executable expression disappears merely
because it lacks a `check` or `raise`, is hard to mutate, or is unreachable in
the twenty baseline fixtures. Unreachable supported behavior needs another
witness; unsupported behavior belongs to the defensive tier. An unproved
equivalence, infeasible witness or unclassified construct blocks completion.

Use three reconciled inventories: all kernel decision/dataflow constructs,
all constraints and semantic branches in the frozen mapping/source schemas,
and all approved output invariants in the mapping and retained contracts.
The harness's comparison and coordinate-check decisions are also subjects.
Extractor, registry/case admission and runner/checker logic receive the finite
independent meta-test treatment specified below. These two verification routes
cover every owned function without recursively inventorying the test system.

The extractor must parse Python AST and traverse every executable expression,
including nested functions, lambdas, helper calls, assignments feeding later
conditions/results, ternaries, `if`/`elif`/`else`, exceptions, returns,
comprehensions, generators, `for`/`while`, `break` and `continue`. Each construct
is classified as predicate, boundary, result formula, transparent composition,
or justified implementation detail. Every AST node kind encountered must have
a declared handler/classification; unknown shapes fail inventory admission.
The extractor is a completeness alarm, not a semantic interpreter or authority.

For boolean expressions, preserve the composition tree, polarity, evaluation
order and short-circuit preconditions, then expose every leaf. Trace aliases
such as successive `valid = valid and ...` assignments; do not stop at the final
variable. Expand chained comparisons, `all`/`any`/`next` bodies, comprehension
filters and loop accumulators into domain, per-body-condition and outcome
obligations. Register loops with initialization, per-element selection/update,
zero/one/many iterations, termination and order where observable. Calls to
repository-owned helpers require a registered contract and the same inventory
or independent meta-test route as their caller; they cannot become an unchecked
leaf. Calls to enumerated trusted primitives terminate traversal, while their
owned argument selection and handling remain subjects. Declarative registrations may
describe these structures when automatic extraction is insufficient, but must
bind the complete normalized AST subtree and all child occurrences. The
structural scanner must reject an omitted or newly added child.

Schema extraction recursively resolves local references while retaining both
use-site and definition pointers; cycles need a declared traversal rule.
Register each required member, closure site, union branch/discriminator,
type/const/enum, item constraint, pattern, uniqueness and bound, together with
the validator operation that enforces it. Mapping programs are parsed as their
closed typed AST: each scan/filter/join/select, predicate operand, case,
cardinality and output formula is an occurrence. Unknown vocabulary fails
closed. Freshness/constant-binding checks remain separately identified and
cannot discharge semantic obligations.

## Proof records, tiers and executable contracts

Each obligation has exactly one primary negative record; additional fixtures
are supplemental cases with their own IDs. A shared fixture may support many
records, but none may share an undecomposed coverage claim. The record contains:

- Authority path/hash and semantic clause; predicate, occurrence, boundary and
  parameter IDs; source subtree/path and its hash; proof tier, phase and
  contract class **G**, **F** or **C** as defined below.
- Literal fixture/query/rule identity; exact source and output row selectors,
  expected match count, JSON path/field and preimage; all mutated old/new values.
  A present-row witness must be nonempty and uniquely select its target. An
  absence invariant instead names the exact searched domain, expected zero
  count, exclusion reason and positive companion witness.
- Required operand types, sibling truth values, quantifier domain and boundary
  values; independently specified diagnostic code, semantic ID, exact payload
  coordinates, or complete expected result/delta. A code shared by several
  guards is insufficient without predicate identity and the isolated witness.
- Exact removal/substitution/fault operator, intact and restored subjects,
  conditioning set if any, expected grid outcomes and survivor/effect sets,
  and exact unrelated-change rejection controls. The preimage,
  applied-edit count and equality outside all declared edits are verified.

Two tiers specify the execution horizon, independently of contract class.
**D** proves an exact parser/schema/unsupported-program phase or evidence
admission decision; it makes no graph claim. The omnibus section enumerates
additional defensive domain boundaries, not a generic error-to-D conversion.
**S** requires completed whole graphs. A supported, defined graph-value
invariant cannot move to D because its S witness is difficult. Each subject is a source/module hash plus exact input/program edits
and conditioning IDs. Restoration must reproduce the original source/input
bytes and original outcomes. Disposable source/freshness bypasses admit only
the explicitly bound test edit; admission failure alone is not semantic proof.

**G — guard/validator neutralization.** The intact implementation on valid
literal input succeeds with its exact phase result (D) or frozen whole graph
(S). The corrupted input/program violates one named guard obligation and the
intact guard, under the fixed declared conditioning set, produces the exact
diagnostic, payload, predicate ID and sibling truth vector. A separate subject
neutralizes only that guard atom; it must expose the exact expected decision
escape (D) or complete the declared whole counterfactual graph (S). For malformed
D operands, an explicitly instrumented decision-boundary observation may stop
before unsafe continuation; this is a declared observation, not an exception
kill or completed-phase claim. Replacing only the invalid operand with its valid
literal preimage must then complete the original phase exactly. For S, the
counterfactual graph may equal the baseline if rejected retained-input data do
not affect constructed output; the invalid input and escape remain explicit.
Restoring the guard restores rejection; restoring the input restores success.
Valid-input positive controls must remain exact under G neutralization.

G's cross-grid rows are guard neutralizations and columns are all primary
case inputs, each under its frozen conditioning set. An **escape survivor** is
a formerly rejected G negative that now has its declared D decision escape or
completed S counterfactual; record its exact outcome, not just missing errors.
Expected escape sets are declared per row before execution. Cases that should
still reject must retain their exact declared diagnostics. A neutralization
already present in a column's conditioning set is a declared no-op cell, never
additional survival evidence. Formula/output and comparator controls in the
same grid retain their independently declared observations. Positive damage,
an unexpected escape or a missing expected escape fails this proof.

**F — constructive result-formula or semantic branch fault.** The intact
implementation on valid input completes the frozen graph. The only exception
to valid retained-context inputs is the explicitly bounded selection trap
authority below, including its omnibus occurrence expansion; conditioned
results are test counterfactuals, not accepted graphs.
The primary negative
is an explicit faulted program or result-expression/branch AST on that input;
no input corruption or rejecting guard is required. With the fault active, S
must complete an independently declared full counterfactual graph. The intact
oracle must report exactly its declared delta against the frozen graph. The
fault is removed by restoring the original formula/branch, after which every
control returns its original exact result. If input edits are needed to reach
the formula, bind their independently declared intact graph before applying the
fault and hold those edits fixed in both subjects. D is reserved for a formula
whose contract is itself a defensive phase result, with its exact phase-result
delta; it is not a fallback for a failing graph construction.

F's grid rows are constructive faults and columns are all primary case inputs
plus all twenty valid controls. Declare each row's **effect set**: the cases
whose completed results must change, with an exact expected graph/delta for
each. Affected positive controls are expected to change; requiring them to stay
equal to the baseline would invalidate the experiment. Unaffected controls must
stay exact. Rejection-only columns may retain a named earlier diagnostic and
are marked as pre-fault-unreached, not formula proof. At least one completed
effect witness is required for every F obligation. An **undetected-fault
survivor** is an affected completed output wrongly accepted as the baseline by
the intact oracle; its expected set is empty. The effect set and survivor set
are separate observations. Unexpected deltas, incorrect nonempty effect sets
or a survivor fail the proof, while the declared formula effect is success.

**C — comparator or evidence-admission fault.** Inputs are fixed pairs of
completed literal graphs or literal evidence records with exact valid/invalid
verdicts and diagnostic lists. Keep kernel/program outputs unchanged. The
intact comparator/checker must accept all valid controls and return the exact
diagnostics for the corrupted graph/record. The faulted subject changes only
one comparator/admission atom or outcome emission. It must return the declared
remaining diagnostics/verdict; a fault may intentionally suppress the target
diagnostic and admit a specific invalid record. Restore its source and reproduce
all intact outcomes. Judge these observations using the independent terminal
meta-test procedure below, never the comparator/checker being faulted.

C's grid rows are comparator/admission faults and columns are all valid and
invalid literal comparison/evidence controls. A **checker-escape survivor** is
an invalid record newly accepted, or a comparison with the designated diagnostic
missing; distinguish those two outcomes explicitly. Declare each exact escape
set and each remaining diagnostic list before execution. Valid controls remain
accepted unless a separately declared C fault intentionally corrupts acceptance;
such a fault requires its own exact false-rejection effect set. A swallowed
exception is not an acceptance outcome. Missing/wrong diagnostics outside the
declared effect fail the proof.

Across G/F/C, record every applicable grid cell from actual execution. These
are class-specific grids: there is no universal rule that a fault preserves
positives or must produce a diagnostic. Any omitted cross-class combination
must name its distinct input type and reviewed inapplicability; it contributes
no coverage. Never derive observed sets from case ownership or fault IDs.
Caching is permitted only for identical source/input/conditioning/runtime hashes;
identify cached cells as reuse, not fresh executions. A generic exception,
timeout, partial graph or unexpected downstream diagnostic cannot kill an S
mutant. A named earlier rejection may be corroboration but cannot replace the
required completed F effect or G counterfactual.

Conditioning applies only when a separately named guard necessarily masks the
target: use a minimal fixed set with a logical reason for every member. For G,
conditioned intact-guard rejection and conditioned neutralized-guard escape are
the required pair. For F, conditioned original-formula completion and
conditioned faulted-formula completion with its exact delta are the pair; no
target diagnostic is required. C normally has no conditioning; a necessary
earlier admission guard may be conditioned only in the isolated meta-test,
with the same exact-record/verdict pairing. Always record an unconditioned
control. Every conditioning guard needs its own obligation; restoring each
member individually must reproduce its declared masking diagnostic. Unknown,
expanding or family-wide disable sets are forbidden. An unresolved downstream
failure leaves the obligation open, rather than changing its class or tier.

Worked **F retention** witness: on each of the twenty frozen inputs, replace
only the retention result formula with literal `"oracle_fault_retention"` in an
in-memory subject. All twenty graphs must complete with exactly one changed
field, `/retentionClassification`, from `"candidate_only"` to that literal;
every other tuple and array position stays exact. The intact comparator returns
the one declared value mismatch per graph. The effect set is all twenty
fixtures; the undetected-fault survivor set is empty. Restoring the formula
restores twenty exact matches. No conditioning or rejection is expected.

Worked **G masked evidence guard** witness: select one exact retained evidence
link by frozen fixture/node/link ID; change only its `purpose` to a literal wrong
value. Leave generated evidence unchanged. Intact construction rejects at
`evidence.purpose`; neutralizing that atom alone subsequently rejects at
`evidence.set`, which is masking evidence, not successful survival. With the
single declared conditioning guard `evidence.set` neutralized, the intact
purpose guard still rejects exactly; additionally neutralizing only the purpose
atom completes the original literal graph because generated evidence ignores
the corrupted retained purpose. Restoring `evidence.set` while purpose is
neutralized must reproduce its exact mismatch. Restoring the purpose guard or
the input restores the respective rejection or valid baseline. The registry
must bind the real literal row, payload and exact sets, and supply an independent
`evidence.set` obligation; these symbolic selectors are not executable evidence.

Each class also needs target fault/corruption alone, an unrelated real field/row
change alone, and both together, with declared class-appropriate outcomes. The
unrelated change alone cannot satisfy the target oracle; both together cannot
hide an extra delta. Include a competing diagnostic and wrong-row/query/path,
zero-match and unapplied-edit controls, not only an ignored marker.

nor an admissible conditioning certificate. Required E13 edges outlive omitted
A11 parents, so execution cannot complete at the direct propagation lookup.

Retain that probe as exact structural-failure corroboration, with zero semantic
kills. Replace it as the primary F/S witness with the following paired,
row-addressed predicate faults. Both truth directions remain required; a
permissive witness alone cannot discharge inclusion. The target remains the
same A11 node-type equality occurrence, with separate `exclude-nonmatch` and

remain separate. Do not relabel it unsupported or move it to phase-only D.

**Eligibility is limited to these two A11 test traps.** Copy frozen `3a-main`
and leave its envelope, bindings, main semantic nodes/owners, relations and all
original endpoints byte-identical. Append one auxiliary context containing
exactly one node, one owner and no relations, and append its one retained
evidence link. The auxiliary bag deliberately uses bound coordinates despite
being carried by `unboundProjectionContexts`; the label asserts no valid foreign
projection. The traps violate retained-context ownership/occurrence or required
edge authority explicitly. Source-envelope validity and successful conditioned
execution must never be reported as validity of that retained context.

Construct both traps by literal copy of node
`avn_b7df6ddffb7d3bbe4c8df461a4e84e9d` (`/applicabilityRules/0`), its unique
`ad_v4_candidate_app_rules` owner and retained `ev-context`/`rule_clause` link.

Rebind only owner `semantic_node_id` and evidence `nodeId`/ID/hash to that
variant. Apply the approved identity/evidence preimages with independent

identity hashes are respectively

The registry must materialize/freeze every full preimage and row, not rely on

An admitted fault hook substitutes the evaluated left operand of exactly this

Each pair uses an identical, finite atomic conditioning set:

- Both variants may neutralize only the extra-selected-member direction for

These are distinct atomic obligations even where current source groups them
under `selection.complete_set`, `selection.node_type` or `edge.cardinality`.
Do not disable those whole compound IDs. Each condition requires its independent

Let `G0` be the complete frozen `3a-main` golden. For each variant independently

hashes are respectively

Every original node/evidence row, all 122 edges, references, identity mappings,
external rows, aggregate and retention remain exact. Positional comparison
deltas must include array insertions/shifts; do not pretend an insertion is
only one changed comparison path.

Required completed pairs are exclusion `G0 → G+` and inclusion `G+ → G0`.
Restoring the operand fault restores the exact left-hand result. Removing the
trap and its link restores the unconditioned frozen fixture and `G0`; all twenty
unmodified fixtures still match their goldens with either row-specific hook
enabled but unapplied. With no conditioning, exclusion/intact is `G0`, while
exclusion/faulted rejects the exact trap at `SELECTION_NODE_TYPE_MISMATCH`;
inclusion/intact rejects `SELECTION_MULTIPLICITY_MISMATCH`, while its row-specific
fault removes the trap and completes `G0`. Condition restoration must separately
expose exact extra-member, count and `CARDINALITY_MISMATCH:E13` failures.

The F effect set for each operator is its own paired trap case; its expected
undetected-fault survivor set is empty. Cross-variant and clean-fixture cells
have zero hook hits and unchanged outcomes. Controls must reject wrong trap ID,
wrong predicate occurrence/operand, zero/multiple hook hits, altered sibling
conditions, a second auxiliary row, removed original endpoints, undeclared
conditioning and unrelated output changes. Keep the original twenty `KeyError`
probes labeled incomplete; this amendment does not convert them into effect
witnesses or remove them from the evidence history.

Alternatives were considered narrowly. A different mutation without a completed
effect is insufficient; the paired row-addressed faults above provide that
effect for both boundaries. Reclassification as G or unsupported D would hide
constructive selection behavior. A test continuation that invents absent
parents, drops edges or supplies readiness is unnecessary and is not authorized.
The deliberately inconsistent traps are admitted solely as these conditional
F experiments, with exact known violations; they establish no persistence,
production acceptance or new semantic authority. The separately specified
closed-cohort amendment extends the exception to nine exact families; the final
28-family reconciliation defines the remaining eighteen exact constructions.
Nothing beyond those enumerated selection cases inherits this exception.

Read-only design probes established the original twenty failures and both
row-addressed pairs/restorations against independently declared full expected
graphs, with one affected predicate invocation per fault. They are feasibility evidence,
not the future atomic-hook/conditioning implementation PASS. Design approval
invalidates the old A11 primary-case binding and its dependent grid claims;
retain unchanged literal authorities and prior diagnostics. Exit requires the
frozen paired records, both exact whole-graph deltas, actual hook-hit counts,
all conditioning/control outcomes and independent review of the new atomic
implementation. If either pair cannot complete under exactly this scope, leave
A11 open and return to design; no added mask or downstream-error kill is allowed.

## Closed mandatory-edge cohort amendment

This section resolves the nine-family witness issue recorded by
`implementation.md` SHA-256
`8089b670e4235fd1c302793dd7cf1b5ef63d47a4b517f301f57dc0bb849d2058` and
`results.json` SHA-256
`fba374cb71c03d4eeb008809f0d344388c71d295288405313eeaa99bcc62d13e`
under `local-semantic-kernel/`. Their nine whole-family omissions, nine
one-original-row omissions and nine permissive unchanged controls remain
diagnostic evidence with zero semantic kills. It extends A11's method to the
closed set **A07, A08, A12, A13, A14, B01, B03, B12, B13** only, and only to
the `/query/from/where/terms/1` node-type equality's inclusion/exclusion
obligations. This section alone does not authorize traps for other families;
the final reconciliation below supplies the other eighteen exact recipes.
Neither section authorizes another predicate, union or alternative source branch.

For an ordinary valid retained context, each selected parent in these nine
families has a mandatory propagating outgoing edge. A node-query-only omission
leaves that source-driven edge in place, so the unmodified propagation lookup
cannot complete. A permissive type predicate is instead masked by the valid
typed-owner join and produces no effect. Neither tested route supplies F/S
evidence. An unrelated gate/retention/result-field fault would not cover this
predicate. No already-valid completed witness for these two node-selection
truth directions is established; the approved solution is a detached test
trap, not reclassification, a zero-effect claim or exception continuation.

### Finite construction and conditioning rule

For each row make two independent fixture copies. Append exactly one auxiliary
node/owner context with no relations and one retained evidence link, preserving
all original records, bindings and source-envelope bytes. This deliberately
inconsistent context is a conditional test input, not a valid persisted graph.
Set the cloned node's parent to null, its `nodeKey` and listed owner key to
`oracle-trap-<ruleId>`. Inclusion keeps the original node type; exclusion uses
`oracle_trap_<ruleId>`. Keep source pointer, ordinal, source hash, source-derived
values, owner table, slice/proposal/projection and all unlisted fields exact.
Replace only each listed detached owner field with the literal
`oracle-detached-<ruleId>-<fieldName>`; prove those sentinels match no node,
owner key or relation endpoint in any loaded context. No suffix heuristic may
invent another detached field. Detachment prevents additional source-driven
edges/references in both variants; original source relationships remain intact.

All nine use the generic `semantic-node` identity preimage
`{projectionId,nodeType,nodeKey,pointer}` with the existing slice domain and
`avn_` or `aon_` prefix/truncated digest. Rebind owner `semantic_node_id` and the
evidence node/ID/hash. A evidence identity uses `nodeId`; B uses
`semanticNodeId` plus the retained ordinal. Preserve purpose, evidence key,
binding, canonical ordinal and source-fragment authority. Recompute full hashes
with independent canonical-byte primitives and freeze the exact row/preimage
crosswalk. This exception does not apply to special designation-value or
identity-mapping recipes. The twenty literal golden files remain untouched.

The existing one-hit A11 operand-hook contract applies with the exact family
occurrence and trap ID: substitute the evaluated left operand to the family's

### O1: finite defensive domain horizons

The normative mapping's `executionContract/inputPreconditions` already requires
verified source/owner/relation/reference sets. Its node construction, ordered
inner-join composition, evidence source rules and readiness rules assume
defined operands. Mapping-schema validity alone does not establish those
semantic program preconditions. Approve D for the following **closed domain
violations**, retaining S for well-defined values and membership effects:

| Propagating edge endpoint absence | `construct_edges` target validation, before an absent endpoint could reach `propagate`; 38 rules × parent/child = 76 G/D obligations. | Present endpoint coordinates, edge production, propagation and gates. | Evidence choice/source domain | Ordered policy decision and exact no-policy rejection before `policy["source"]`; a wrongly selected source branch's explicit required-key/pointer-domain decision before an undefined read. | All defined evidence generation, binding, ordering, multiplicity and empty-evidence effects. |

Required fields come from the frozen `sourceFields`, typed owner/formula reads and the bound query projection; required map entries are live IDs registered in `nodes`, with their `owners`, `raw`, `node_rules` entries. | Well-shaped wrong coordinates/values, whole-row inclusion/omission, multiplicity and the constructed graph. For a malformed query/assembly result without an existing named kernel guard,

The phase checker and the stop/observation machinery receive C tests, including

Do not add a production fallback, synthesize a referent, skip a source edge,
repair an intermediate state and call it the same counterfactual, or continue

replacement is a separate substitution control, not completion of the invalid
subject. Native exceptions, generic inequality and checker's self-reported
success are never primary evidence. This finite domain list cannot grow from
observing a crash. Any other defined semantic obligation uses S or an explicit
equivalence classification, not a new implicit phase exception.

changed edge and the target atom identity. The neutralized D event contains
that same edge, the missing lookup, the remaining existing endpoint and the

retain the real-ID positive. Both-absent, wrong endpoint/rule/query/row, changed
slice/type and an extra corruption are rejection controls, not substitutes for

## Required decomposition and calibration

The following are required coverage dimensions, not a fixed predicate count.

| Domain | Mandatory distinct obligations and witnesses |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean and quantified conditions | Each conjunct/disjunct independently determines the result with siblings held neutral; include negation, short-circuit preconditions, each quantified-body condition, empty/one/many domain and no/one/multiple matches. |
| Schema, strings and types | Container type, per-entry type, accepted type alternatives, bool-versus-int, duplicate required names, supported vocabulary, string encoding/NUL/pattern, lower and upper bounds at boundary and adjacent values; missing versus null; zero/one/multiple union matches. |
| Selection and identity | Slice, projection, proposal, owner table and owner/node binding separately; selected set missing and extra members versus owner cardinality; duplicate selected rows; pointer existence/escaping, value hash, each identity recipe and prefix/hash relation, parent absence/presence and valid optional-root branch. |
| Evidence and consumption | Own/parent/none source branches; keys absent/empty/present; proposal and key filter conjuncts; binding count zero/one/multiple; fragment ID/hash separately; owner coordinates, purpose, ordinal and every link coordinate; equal counts with unequal members, missing/extra and duplicate links; selected identity set both directions, source owner and zero/one/multiple consumers. |
| Edges and references | Every rule/query's scope/filter/join/select operands; parent/child existence, slice/type/key/projection independently; each tuple coordinate; identity uniqueness; lower/upper/unbounded cardinality; canonical ordinal type/value; all 13 reference queries with exact nonempty endpoints and explicit absence alternatives. |
| Ordering and graph decisions | Source canonicalization, set-versus-sequence order, sort-key coordinates and tie behavior; optional slot absence without compaction; controlling/noncontrolling/reachable roots; propagating versus integrity-only edges; cycle detection and completed counterfactual policy; maximum gate truth table, aggregate root selection, empty-root rejection and retention literal. |
| External and comparison | All six external branches, unresolved/ambiguous/other-proposal/incoming boundaries, zero incoming direct evidence, selected external multiset; comparison type/missing/extra/length/value, per-field traversal and omitted tails, exact path attribution; separate test-only coordinate detectors. |

The four confirmed third-loop gaps are calibration examples only:
`selection.node_scope` requires separate projection and proposal witnesses;
`node.identity` separates stored-hash equality from node-ID prefix/truncated-hash
equality; `selection.complete_set` separates set membership in both directions
from owner count; `required` separates list shape, each string entry and
uniqueness. The coherent node-ID replacement and `{"required":[7]}` must be
retained as exact regression witnesses. Finding these four entries does not
establish the complete inventory.

## Finite trust boundary and independent meta-tests

The trust root is the pinned CPython runtime, the following primitive operations,
and an independent reviewer's direct inspection of raw observations and small
literal assertions. It excludes every repository-owned semantic, inventory,
mutation, comparison and evidence-admission function. Trust in the runtime is
an explicit engineering assumption; this package does not prove Python,
cryptographic libraries or the host OS. Primitive internals are not recursively
added to the predicate inventory.

| Trusted primitive surface | Exact use and retained owned obligation |
| --- | --- |
| CPython language/built-ins | Literal scalar/collection creation; function/class calls and attribute access; iteration/comprehensions/generators; boolean short-circuit, arithmetic and comparisons; exception/traceback propagation; indexing/slicing; `type`, `isinstance`, `len`, `range`, `enumerate`, `zip`, `sorted`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `all`, `any`, `next`, `getattr`, `str`, `int`, `bool`, `chr`, `tuple`, `list`, `dict`, `set`, `frozenset`, and `print`. The choice of comparison, exact type policy, bounds, order keys, operands and callbacks remains owned code. |
| Built-in scalar/collection methods | String/bytes comparison and concatenation, `encode`/`decode` with UTF-8 or UTF-16-BE and strict errors, `replace`, `split`, `rsplit`, `lstrip`, `removeprefix`, `startswith`, `endswith`; `float.is_integer`; dict `get`/`keys`/`values`/`items`/`setdefault`/`update`; list `append`/`extend`/`pop`/`sort`; set membership/union/intersection/difference/add/remove. Pointer escaping, canonical ordering and JSON-type equality rules remain owned. |
| JSON and copying | `json.loads`/`json.dumps` and their standard decoder/encoder; `copy.deepcopy` only for acyclic built-in JSON-like values. Decoder hooks, duplicate/nonfinite rejection, serializer options, admitted types and literal expansion are owned and tested; custom object hooks or arbitrary objects are not primitive exemptions. |
| Hashing and regex | `hashlib.sha256` with `update`/`digest`/`hexdigest`; `re.compile`, `re.search` and compiled-pattern matching. Domain tags, preimages, truncation, expected digests, patterns, flags and regex error handling remain owned. No hash equality substitutes for exact semantic comparison. |
| Syntax inspection | `ast.parse`, `ast.walk`, `ast.iter_child_nodes`, `ast.dump` and `ast.unparse`, and standard AST node field access. Selection, traversal completeness, normalization, classification and fault registration are owned; parser internals are trusted. |
| Read-only orchestration | `pathlib.Path` construction, path joining, `resolve`, `parent`, `is_file`, `is_relative_to`, `read_bytes`, `read_text`; standard module import/loading through `importlib.util`; `sys` module/version/executable metadata, `sys.addaudithook`/`sys.audit`, module inventory and stdout/stderr; `argparse` option parsing. Exact path/import allowlists, audit decisions and result/exit handling remain owned and meta-tested. |

This is a closed surface, not permission for any stdlib function. Transitive
stdlib implementation dependencies are covered by the pinned runtime/module
manifest, but repository calls to another primitive require a reviewed surface
addition. Network/process/database primitives, arbitrary `eval`/`exec`/`compile`
and dynamic imports from fixture data remain forbidden by the entry fence.
Faults use registered, default-inert hooks or the interpreted mapping AST;
Python AST inspection verifies their exact source binding. It is not a license
to evaluate arbitrary source supplied by a test record.

The observed design runtime is CPython **3.13.14**, cache tag `cpython-313`,
Darwin arm64, SOABI `cpython-313-darwin`; executable
`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/bin/python3`, SHA-256
`ee3c4103b97e32a98e98cfad7f6ca4d09b2ab2dc16f3d28e18b54a4a0244efe0`.
Before implementation evidence, `entry-fence-v2.json` must pin that executable's
resolved path/bytes, full `sys.version`, implementation/cache tag/ABI, platform,
Unicode/runtime encoding facts, and complete actual loaded-module origin/hash
inventory for the admitted primitive surface. Include used extension binaries
and their linked runtime/crypto libraries, or an exact distribution/runtime
image digest covering those bytes; an executable hash alone is insufficient.
Record the actual hash backend and loaded dependency bytes rather than assuming
OpenSSL. No runtime installation/change is authorized; an unavailable or changed
profile needs reviewed rebinding and replay, not silently different versions.

The finite owned-code universe is both local Python files, all their nested
functions/classes/module expressions, and the admitted JSON registry/case/fence
files. No repository helper outside those files may be imported. At freeze,
enumerate every qualified symbol/source range and assign exactly one route:

- **Predicate inventory:** all `semantic_kernel.py` code, including strict JSON,
  canonicalization/hash recipes, schema/AST evaluators, construction, test hooks
  and `compare_graph`; plus harness coordinate comparison and any semantic
  expected-value/result transformation. Opaque owned helpers inherit this
  route. Semantic formulas cannot be hidden as orchestration.
- **Independent meta-tests:** harness `detector_inventory` and replacement
  extractors/classifiers; registry/case parsers and materializers; `patch_value`,
  `matching_rows`, `GraphOracleKernel` and fault operators; `assert_inventory_bijection`,
  `exact_semantic_difference`, diagnostic/result admission, all `run_*_oracle`
  methods, grid/survivor accounting; `require`, `sha256`, read/import/audit helpers,
  CLI/main orchestration and meta-test dispatch. Any new helper receives its
  caller's route unless an explicit semantic responsibility requires inventory.
  Every registry/case field has closed-schema, stale/duplicate/extra/missing and
  meaning-specific admission controls; JSON data are not exempt evidence.

The symbol manifest names actual final functions and resolves overlaps by
responsibility; an unassigned symbol or unresolved route prevents execution
approval. Meta-tested symbols receive complete branch/boundary listings and
literal positive/negative controls reviewed independently, but their tests do
not recursively become new predicate obligations. Existing function names above
locate responsibilities, not permission to preserve their current logic.

The small runner/checker's entire responsibility is to admit byte-bound closed
records, dispatch their declared G/F/C operations and fixed conditioning sets,
record raw results/errors and applied-edit counts, compare exact typed literal
outcomes, reconcile inventories/grids, and emit deterministic observations and
verdicts. It may not choose semantic expected values, infer missing cases,
classify generic errors as kills, relabel diagnostics, enlarge conditioning,
infer executed grid cells or decide finding/review closure. Its semantic
decisions must be declarative inputs; its admission decisions remain C subjects.

Independent testing terminates as follows. The separate reviewer authors and
freezes small literal meta-vectors and expected transcripts before running the
checker: exact valid records and one-field wrong ID/path/type/value/preimage,
missing/duplicate/extra/stale entries, unapplied/multiple edits, wrong survivor
sets, swallowed errors and omitted grid cells. The reviewer calls individual
owned routines directly, captures their return values/exceptions outside the
runner's admission path, and checks exact type/value/sequence membership with
short visible assertions using only the trusted primitives. C faults are
applied to each owned admission branch and must change those raw outcomes as
declared. For extractor controls, literal micro-programs have manually listed
AST obligations, including compound/quantifier/helper/merge/split variants;
their expected inventory is not produced by that extractor.

The independent report preserves vector hashes, exact invocation/assertion
text, primitive/runtime bindings and raw observations; the reviewer inspects
the finite assertion code and every owned branch/control crosswalk. It neither
imports the subject's comparator/`require`/meta-runner to judge results nor uses
the subject's PASS as the terminal verdict. The terminal literal assertion code
and human review are the stated trust endpoint, not recursively inventoried
repository subjects. This is independent engineering evidence, not a proof of
the verifier or an automated reviewer-identity attestation.

Any owned-source, registry/case or authority change invalidates dependent
bindings and evidence. Extractor/classifier changes invalidate the entire
inventory and its downstream grids; admission/comparator/runner changes
invalidate every verdict they produced and require independent meta-test replay.
Primitive/runtime/module/extension/crypto changes invalidate all B execution
evidence, require a new pinned profile and full positive/negative/meta replay;
literal semantic expectations remain fixed. A new primitive also requires
independent design review of the enlarged trust boundary.

## Bijection and negative controls for the oracle

Within the explicit predicate-inventory route, at the expanded obligation-key
level require a **source ↔ predicate ↔ primary negative bijection**, with unique
keys and equal memberships in all three inventories. The finite meta-test route
has its separate owned-branch/control crosswalk and independent attestation; it
does not recursively extend this bijection. Shared semantic IDs across
occurrences remain separate rows;
supplemental cases do not inflate the bijection. Each registered source
composition must account for every child and boundary. A fully scanned source
classification report, including justified implementation details, prevents an
unregistered source construct from being hidden outside the equality check.

Before claiming coverage, meta-counterexamples must reject: missing/duplicate/
extra source registrations, predicates and primary negatives; stale source or
authority bindings; a same-count predicate replacement; compound-child addition
or removal while retaining the outer guard ID; predicate merge/split without
the required ID crosswalk and changed cases; moving a condition into a helper,
quantifier or intermediate variable without updating its structural binding;
an unknown AST shape; empty or wrong target selection; an ignored mutation;
wrong diagnostic/path; overlapping masks; downstream failure; and an unrelated
delta presented as the intended result. Operator controls must prove an AST
mutation affects exactly its bound leaf, preserves sibling structure and order,
and fails if zero or multiple targets match. Inventory failures and semantic
failures are reported separately. No self-derived counts or fixed historical
site total may substitute for these controls.

## Independent expectations and mechanical construction

Preserve the five hashes in the original
[entry fence](local-semantic-kernel/entry-fence.json), including literal goldens
`abc00a1bfe25e8e9cfc7a3e76c40c7074dc94a910d9d7f566e7345850e2c4b5b`.
The [mapping PASS](adversarial-mapping-reconstruction.md) and
[oracle provenance](acceptance-semantic-oracle-provenance.md) distinguish
approved literal semantics from historical executable controls. Historical
407 source/499 mapping mutations, reference-control results and the current
334 local mutations stay bound to their original subjects and limited claims;
they may corroborate a new obligation only through an explicit crosswalk and
fresh exact witness. They cannot certify the new inventory by their totals.

Expected rows, counts, truth vectors and deltas must be declared from the frozen
source/schema, approved mapping and retained semantic contracts, or copied by
explicit selectors from independently authored literal goldens. They must be
frozen before running their negative/counterfactual subjects. Never use kernel
query output to choose an expected row/count, execute the historical reference
engine to manufacture expected values, or call kernel hashing/comparison/gate
functions to generate the oracle. Mechanical expansion may copy named literal
rows, apply declared edits, compute independently specified canonical bytes,
and sort by already approved keys; it may not discover semantic output. New
expectations need provenance and review; a true frozen-golden defect requires
a separate authority change, not adaptation to a failed subject.

The bounded construction sequence after design PASS is:

1. Extract the finite structural/schema/contract inventories and reconcile every
   node/constraint. Publish exact counts and unresolved rows; do not code around
   an unresolved semantic choice. Establish all semantic IDs and boundaries.
2. Materialize a declarative registry and primary cases using finite templates
   for the listed patterns. Freeze their hashes before negative execution.
   Unknown templates fail closed. Generate the complete execution grid and
   declared survivor sets without consulting results.
3. Add only the instrumentation/refactoring needed to address exact predicates,
   preserving evaluation order and disabled-by-default test hooks. Verify the
   independent comparator, extraction/mutation operators and meta-controls.
4. Execute all positives, negatives, counterfactuals and cross-case controls;
   report every obligation and grid cell, not only totals. Complete the coherent
   local predicate-oracle family under this design, including the entire
   28-family selection cohort, then request one full implementation review.

There is no reviewer turn per predicate or generated file. If inventory
reconciliation reveals an unresolvable atomicity, conditioning, expected-value
or unsupported-source issue, publish that specific unresolved choice and return
to design review before further dependent implementation. No such choice is
silently delegated to a heuristic. This proposal selects the architecture;
the full enumerated manifest and executable proof remain unbuilt.

## Entry, allowed changes and exit

This assignment writes only this document. It does not alter the existing
kernel/harness/results, finding/review/state files, or run any database/cloud
operation. Independent design PASS is necessary before the next B builder
starts. The coordinator records that review outside the subject and binds the
exact approved document; no future review is an input to its own subject.

On resumption preserve the original `entry-fence.json` byte-for-byte. An approved
`local-semantic-kernel/entry-fence-v2.json` must extend it with exactly these new
files: `predicate-registry-v1.json`, `predicate-cases-v1.json` and
`predicate-oracle-results-v1.json`. Allowed edits remain the existing local
`semantic_kernel.py`, `semantic_harness.py`, `implementation.md`, `results.json`,
plus those four new files. Runtime reads add the new fence/registry/cases and
self-source only; runtime writes remain denied and results are captured by the
coordinator. All other existing read/import restrictions remain. Test hooks
must be inert in normal construction and rejected for unknown predicate IDs.
Any additional path/import or semantic-authority change requires an explicit
reviewed fence amendment before use.

Verify at entry and exit the five frozen semantic inputs and all ten exact
production-family hashes from the original fence. Preserve every saved 0030
byte, generator, service, model and test. Inspect staged, unstaged and untracked
scope and active callers/imports. No backend/infra integration, database,
credential, AWS, ACL, snapshot, ownership, successor schema/count/hash or
production authority work is authorized. Five database calibration round trips
remain deferred to Package F; the three 74-case coordinate cohorts remain
test-only and do not become snapshot totals.

Exit evidence consists of the complete byte-bound registries/cases, source
classification and crosswalk, exact expected/observed outcomes and survivor
and effect sets under distinct G/F/C contracts, the pinned primitive/runtime
manifest and independent terminal meta-test transcripts, no unresolved or
excluded-without-rationale obligation, all meta-controls,
twenty exact literal graphs, the approved union/node/edge/identity/reference/
external and optional-boundary coverage, retained historical regressions,
separate coordinate cohorts, strict JSON and import/read/write audits, identical
two-run pure replays, pre/post preservation hashes and clean diff/Markdown/link
checks. Source, case or authority changes invalidate their dependent evidence.
The independent reviewer must inspect the full local family and surrounding
preserved scope, challenge compound and masked predicates, and reproduce the
whole-family evidence before Package B PASS.

`B-SEMANTIC-H-001` can close only after this design PASS, completed implementation
evidence and a fresh independent PASS verifying its entire requirement, followed
by the coordinator's disposition. B completion supplies component evidence for
D/F; C's native RDS feasibility remains upstream of D and later production gates
remain intact. This document alone closes no finding or package.

# Slice 4B normative acceptance, gate, and dependency matrix

This file is normative for `T081-V4-SCHEMA-SLICE-4B`. Python construction,
PostgreSQL commit validation, read verification, fixture goldens, and API
serialization may not invent a different rule.

The reconstructed machine authority is the single `/typedAst` program in
`acceptance-mapping-v1.json`, executed under the frozen bootstrap AST grammar
and executor named and hash-bound by its envelope. It replaces the former
nonexecuting selector labels, separate branch/evidence/cardinality tables, and
unresolved field groups. The envelope also fixes source union inventory,
occurrence identities, evidence preimages, ordering, and scope prerequisites.
It contains no expected fixture arrays or oracle result data. The grammar's
fixed internal `paprnav-independent-bootstrap-reference-1` version identifies
the adopted language; the outer mapping version identifies this subject.

The subject-side `acceptance-synthetic-vectors.py` constructs every actual
graph before loading immutable literal goldens, then uses the approved
executor/comparator for exact tuple and semantic mutation checks. The frozen
semantic interpreter's historical CLI remains a legacy diagnostic entry point;
it is not rewritten or used to claim the reconstructed subject is blocked.
These are design-mapping checks; independent design review and the separate
persistence, resource, SQL, authorization, and production gates remain required.

The current downstream authority audit is `decision-authority-map-v2.json`,
version `paprnav-ad-v4-decision-authority-map-2`, with sibling
`decision-authority-map-v2.schema.json`. The immutable v1 map/schema preserve
the historical 347-statement/292-exclusion extraction, not current approval
flags. Only its two explicitly version-qualified historical snapshot overrides
resolve old persistence/resource bytes; no current-path or latest-version
fallback is permitted. The standalone persistence requirements v2 remain the
single persistence requirements upstream; resource retains exactly ten inputs.
The current detached persistence, mapping and resource PASS reports apply only
to their exact component bytes. H-005 and H-004 are closed at design level by
those reports; overall integration review and production enforcement remain
separate gates. `authority-versioning-remediation-4.md` fixes the acyclic
63-file integration inventory and current/historical namespaces.

## 1. Frozen versions and outcomes

| Concern | Version |
| --- | --- |
| acceptance contract | `paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1` |
| mapping manifest | `paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-mapping-1` |
| generator | `paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-mapgen-1` |
| gate rules | `paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-gates-1` |
| dependency rules | `paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-dependencies-1` |
| event fold | `paprnav-ad-v4-review-lifecycle-2` |
| authorization | `paprnav-ad-v4-candidate-acceptance-1`, policy `1` |
| stable input / observation | existing `paprnav-ad-v4-review-input-identity-1` / `paprnav-ad-v4-review-observation-1` |

The only terminal decision classification is `candidate_only`. The only node
gates are:

| gate | rank | meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `candidate_only` | 0 | retained source semantics; no automated or affirmative conclusion |
| `human_determination_required` | 1 | a later aircraft-specific human decision is required |

`actionable`, `release_eligible`, `released`, `selected`, `current`, and
`published` are invalid values, not aliases. Every decision stores
`release_blocked=true`, `authority_effect='none'`, and
`release_blocker='candidate_only_not_release_authority'`.

Semantic readiness uses the safety order above:

`effective(node) = max(base(node), effective(each propagating child))`.

`max` means the most restrictive reachable requirement. Integrity-only edges
must resolve but do not enter this maximum. Acyclicity is required before
evaluation. Separately, after every integrity prerequisite passes, the decision
retention classification is the fixed literal `candidate_only`; it is neither a
minimum nor maximum of semantic-readiness gates.

Exhaustive propagation truth tables (C=`candidate_only`,
H=`human_determination_required`):

| shape | base | propagating child gates | effective | retention classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| leaf/base C | C | none | C | candidate_only after integrity |
| leaf/base H | H | none | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent C + child C | C | C | C | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent C + child H | C | H | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent H + child C | H | C | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent H + child H | H | H | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent C + children C,C | C | C,C | C | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent C + children C,H | C | C,H | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent C + children H,H | C | H,H | H | candidate_only after integrity |
| parent H + any children | H | any | H | candidate_only after integrity |

| special shape | semantic-readiness behavior | aggregate behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| integrity-only C or H child | child must resolve; excluded from propagation | no readiness effect |
| noncontrolling root C | verify full reachable subtree | root excluded from aggregate maximum |
| noncontrolling root H | verify full reachable subtree | root excluded from aggregate maximum |
| controlling roots all C | aggregate readiness C | retention candidate_only |
| any controlling root H | aggregate readiness H | retention still candidate_only |
| no controlling root / integrity failure | no result | acceptance forbidden |

## 2. Decision row contracts

### Decision version

Required non-null columns: ID; case/request/proposal/directive IDs; proposal,
evidence, cutoff, authorship, 3A projection, 3B projection, graph-set, decision-
content, and row hashes; both projection event-head hashes; schema, validator,
canonicalization, materializer, 3B mapping/digest, acceptance mapping/digest,
gate/dependency/lifecycle/auth versions; requested/current input and observation
hashes; current identity/observation bytes and observed time; graph counts;
`classification`; `release_blocked`; `authority_effect`; `release_blocker`;
canonical bytes; accepted time.

None is nullable. No release/publication/selection/V3 FK or column exists.
Classification is exactly `candidate_only`. Requested and current stable
identity hashes must be equal; observation hashes need not be.

### Node gate

Primary identity:
`(decision_version_id,node_slice,semantic_node_id)`.

Required non-null columns: decision/proposal ID, node slice (`slice_3a|slice_3b`),
bound projection ID, semantic node ID and identity hash, node type/key, source
pointer, canonical node hash/ordinal, evidence-set hash/count,
`representation_status`, `base_gate`, `effective_gate`, `root_role`,
`reason_code`, row hash. `parent_node_id` is nullable exactly when the bound
projection node parent is null. `root_role` is
`controlling_root|reachable|noncontrolling_root|noncontrolling_reachable`.

The row repeats the authoritative projection-node columns exactly. Evidence set
is the canonical ordered list of that node's existing projection evidence links
`(purpose,canonicalOrdinal,evidenceKey,candidateBindingId,linkHash)`; zero links
are represented by the hash of `[]`, not null.

### Dependency

Primary identity:
`(decision_version_id,parent_slice,parent_node_id,edge_kind,child_slice,child_node_id,canonical_ordinal)`.
All fields including `propagates_gate` and row hash are non-null. Endpoints must
exist in the same decision. No arbitrary metadata JSON exists.

### External dependency

Primary identity: `(decision_version_id,source_change_node_id)`. Common non-null
fields are decision/proposal/3A projection IDs; source semantic node ID;
dependency ID/key/kind/hash; predecessor/successor AD numbers; resolution state;
row hash.

| branch | required | forbidden |
| --- | --- | --- |
| outgoing `resolved_candidate` | target projection/proposal/hash/event-head; reciprocal incoming dependency ID/hash | unresolved reason; source dependency ID |
| incoming `resolved_candidate` | target projection equals the bound source projection; source outgoing dependency ID/hash and its source projection/proposal/head | unresolved reason; a second target |
| outgoing `unresolved` | one of `successor_identity_unknown|successor_not_this_proposal|target_candidate_not_resolved` | every target and source-dependency field |
| outgoing `ambiguous` | reason `multiple_predecessor_candidates` | every target and source-dependency field |

Incoming rows are never unresolved or ambiguous. An outgoing resolved row and
its incoming reciprocal form a bijection: the outgoing row names exactly one
target and the target contains exactly one incoming row naming that outgoing
dependency. Every reason/state/nullability combination not listed is invalid.

External-target snapshot protocol: an identifier-only preflight follows every
resolved outgoing row to its target and every resolved incoming row to its
source outgoing row, takes the transitive union with the bound 3A/3B
projections, and freezes `(slice,projection_id,proposal_id,projection_hash,
materializer_version,event_head_hash,dependency_id,dependency_hash)`. It then
locks the complete set in ascending `(slice_rank,projection_id)` without
lock-chasing. If discovery changes, rollback and retry from preflight. After
locks, before insert, and in the deferred validator, the exact union and every
tuple are rederived and compared. Slice-3A reciprocal materialization uses the
same set-order rule. Target payload rows are never loaded. Tests cover A↔B
reciprocal dependency, new target event, changed reciprocal row, target
replacement, new ambiguity, and materializer/acceptance races.

The exact union follows the trusted 3A change-dependency row. A resolved target
is current only when its event head equals the frozen head.

### Authorship binding

Primary identity:
`(decision_version_id,source_table,source_id,user_id,authorship_role)`.
All fields, `bound_hash`, and row hash are non-null. Closed source roles:

| source table | role | bound hash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ad_v4_candidate_submissions` | `candidate_submitter` | request hash |
| `ad_evidence_fragments` | `fragment_creator` | fragment hash |
| `ad_evidence_fragment_lifecycle_events` | `fragment_admitter` | admitted event hash |

Bindings equal the request's frozen authorship bytes and independently rederived
current set in both directions. The signer cannot appear by user ID.

### Accepting signoff and event

Accepting signoff has non-null case/request/decision/proposal/directive/actor/
membership/organization IDs; action `accept_candidate_only`; decision hash;
requested/current input and observation hashes; authorship set hash/count;
authorization observation; request/idempotency/auth policy values; canonical
bytes; signature and row hashes; signed time. It has no rejection ID.

The acceptance case event has:

- `event_type='candidate_only_accepted'`;
- `resulting_state='candidate_only'`;
- exact review request, decision, and acceptance signoff IDs;
- null draft-revision, rejection, and rejecting-signoff IDs; and
- signoff auth/request/idempotency/time values exactly.

The existing rejection branch is the inverse nullability union.

Draft intent remains the exact 0029 union `undecided|reject`; 0030 adds no value.
Acceptance forbids a frozen `reject` draft. No draft or an `undecided` draft is
allowed only because the terminal acceptance request/signoff is the authority.
Rejection semantics remain unchanged.

## 3. Common representation and base-gate rules

Every node first requires the exact projection verifier, typed owner, canonical
value, relation set, reference set, and expected evidence-link set. Failure is
an aggregate integrity failure; no decision graph may commit.

Representation status:

| source branch | representation status |
| --- | --- |
| value assertion `unknown` | `explicit_unknown` |
| designation/group association `unknown` | `explicit_unknown` |
| timing group `unknown` | `explicit_unknown` |
| recurrence `unknown` | `explicit_unknown` |
| every other valid branch | `exact` |

Common value-assertion state gate (A03/B02):

| branch | base gate | reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unknown/conflicting_evidence` | `human_determination_required` | `conflicting_evidence_requires_human` |
| `unknown/source_ambiguous` | `human_determination_required` | `source_ambiguous_requires_human` |
| any other valid `unknown` | `candidate_only` | `source_value_unresolved` |
| `known` or `not_applicable` | `candidate_only` | `literal_source_no_executable_contract` |

The source value is never normalized or rewritten by this gate.

The machine-readable, schema-validated row/branch expansion is
[`acceptance-mapping-v1.json`](acceptance-mapping-v1.json). The tables below are
its review index; where prose and JSON differ, review fails rather than choosing
one. Every node retains its verified persisted canonical ordinal. Slice-3A
object children have ordinal `0`, while array occurrences retain their source
ordinal. Slice-3B has its retained fixed source slots: document assertions
number/revision/retention `0/1/2`; requirement action/activation/branch/initial
timing/recurrence/effect `0/1/2/3/4/5`; recurrence condition/timing `0/1`; and
recurrence-group initial/recurring timing `0/1`. Expression operands, action
steps, and timing terms retain their source array ordinals. Dependency slots
are separately declared and never rebase or compact semantic-node ordinals.

Evidence is exact, ordered, and non-inherited unless a row explicitly says
otherwise. Slice 3A purposes are: product `scope_clause`; designation scope
`designation_scope`; condition/group `condition_clause`; condition direct and
group-member assertions `subject_value` except member manufacturer
`identity_support`; rule `rule_clause`; search node/group/member and source
display `search_hint_clause`, while group/member manufacturer assertions use
`identity_support`; outgoing change dependencies use `supersession_clause`.
Incoming supersession signals retain their exact synthetic source value and
zero direct evidence; their source dependency provides the retained provenance.
Identity mappings, designation values/ranges, and expressions also have zero
direct evidence. A product manufacturer source assertion alone uses sibling
`normalizedIdentity.evidenceKeys`. Slice 3B uses own/one-or-more/no-inheritance
evidence except action-step and expression nodes, which have none/zero.
Slice-3B assertion purposes select the actual owner `field_code`:
`document_number|revision -> document_identity`,
`retention -> document_retention`, and
`approving_authority -> amoc_authority_clause`; `owner_kind` is not an
assertion column. The AST declares every evidence clause and its ordered
first-match selection explicitly.

Every identity mapping is consumed exactly once through one selector: product
manufacturer; listed model designation; direct condition manufacturer/model;
group-member designation; group-member manufacturer; search-group manufacturer;
search-model designation; search-model manufacturer. An outside, missing, or
duplicate mapping consumption forbids acceptance.

The closed identity selector/consumer pairs are `I01/E01`, `I02/E04`,
`I03/E06`, `I04/E11`, `I05/E12`, `I06/E19`, `I07/E21`, and `I08/E22`.
I01 emits for every present manufacturer object. I02 emits only for listed
model values. I03 emits only for present known manufacturer/model-or-series
assertions under conditions; absent, unknown, and not-applicable assertions
have none. I04/I07 require a mapping for every model or series member.
I05/I06/I08 emit only for known manufacturer assertions. The selected mapping
must retain its exact source occurrence, identity kind, normalization origin,
context evidence parent, and one consumer edge. Matching source strings never
merge occurrences.

Every edge query explicitly scopes both endpoints, owners, and relation rows
to the bound proposal and appropriate projection. Slice-3B expression targets
in Slice 3A additionally compare `app_target_projection_id` to the bound 3A
projection. No node-type-only or proposal-only lookup supplies a target.
Each source collection is already verified under the retained 3A/3B contract;
query results equal that collection, with broad per-family bounds as a second
check. Such a bound does not replace source union cardinality: listed/range
members, group members, composite operands, and known timing terms retain their
source-schema minimums; expression leaves and absent properties emit no rows.
`terminates` permits an empty `requirementKeys` set and therefore zero E37
edges. `none` also emits zero, without creating an implicit termination target.

The thirteen reference queries retain exact expression targets, rule exclusions,
action document references, prerequisites, recurrence membership, termination
targets, and optional requirement-to-group references. They include target
slice/projection/node/type/key and the source relation ordinal where defined.
Requirement-state references retain their required-state literal. Source
projection is validated before the fixed reference serializer omits that
redundant field; serializer renaming cannot remove targets or change membership.
Rule exclusions have both E14 gate edges and explicit reference records.

External branches are individually executable: X01 outgoing resolved; X02
outgoing unresolved/successor identity unknown; X03 outgoing unresolved/not
this proposal; X04 outgoing unresolved/target not resolved; X05 outgoing
ambiguous/multiple predecessors; X06 incoming resolved. Every change node
produces exactly one branch row. Resolved queries bind metadata and the exact
reciprocal/source dependency; unresolved and ambiguous queries require null
target/source IDs and emit no target/source metadata fields.

Rule-exclusion plus expression edges must be acyclic. Requirement prerequisite
plus cross-slice expression-target edges must be acyclic. Recurrence membership
and termination targets are integrity-only to avoid invented cycles or gate
contamination.

All pass in one locked snapshot:

| verified official source/evidence binding | `source_identity_or_evidence_missing` |
| current admitted fragment heads/retained bytes | `evidence_not_current` or source integrity |
| current 3A/3B reconstruction and parent binding | `projection_integrity` |
| one product scope | `minimum_product_scope_missing` |
| one applicability rule | `minimum_rule_missing` |
