| complete graph/external/authorship sets/hashes | `gate_graph_incomplete` |
| acyclic propagating graph | `gate_dependency_cycle` |
| frozen request cutoff/authorship equals current | `review_request_stale` |
| independent active signer | `independent_signer_required` |
| count/byte limits | `acceptance_capacity_exceeded` |

Aggregate roots are all 3A product scopes, applicability rules, change
dependencies, and all 3B requirements. Their semantic-readiness maximum is
stored separately from the fixed `candidate_only` retention classification.
Noncontrolling roots are excluded only from this maximum, never from
completeness.

## 8. Canonical sets and hashes

Canonical values use restricted JCS and domain-separated SHA-256. Set order:

| set | order |
| --- | --- |
| node gates | slice, source pointer, node type, node key, semantic node ID |
| dependencies | parent slice/ID, kind, ordinal, child slice/ID |
| external dependencies | source node ID |
| authorship | source table, source ID, user ID, role |

The semantic comparison surface also orders identity mappings by semantic-node
ID; evidence by slice/node/purpose/ordinal/key; and reference records by their
restricted-JCS bytes. Node evidence remains the ordered five-tuple array
`(purpose,canonicalOrdinal,evidenceKey,candidateBindingId,linkHash)`, with the
hash of `[]` for zero links. Equality includes complete tuple contents and
array order, not only row counts or hashes.

Decision-content bytes contain every frozen binding, four set hashes/counts,
classification, and fixed non-authority fields, excluding actor, idempotency key,
and wall clock. The row envelope adds audit fields. Signature hash binds decision
content/row hashes, frozen request/observation, current input/observation,
authorization, authorship, and signed time.

Python/SQL vectors cover every domain, non-ASCII, escaping, absent versus null,
and order.

### Exact cross-layer capacity formula

The current resource authority is `resource-accounting-v2.json`, whose contract
version is `paprnav-ad-v4-resource-accounting-3`. It has **89 families**, **1,639
ordered fields**, and every one of the **201 persistence output columns**:
77 source selections copied exactly from the approved catalog, three external
metadata families with 4/7/13 columns, and nine persistence families. Those nine
are decision, node gate, dependency, external dependency, authorship, signoff,
the complete 0029 event plus its two nullable 0030 additions, sentinel, and
`memory.acceptance_pending_copies`. The prior 57-family/740-field inventory,
47-direct-source/one-external selector inventory, and sum-of-set-bytes-only
formula are historical and non-authoritative.

Each field retains its complete physical or approved transient declaration:
SQL type, character width, nullability, default, numeric/timestamp facts, and
separate resource encoding. Source varchar hash-looking names remain UTF-8
varchar, not inferred ASCII hashes. Only persistence fields explicitly declaring
hex64 use exactly 64 ASCII octets. Nullable fields distinguish NULL from
present-empty; required fields have no null tag. Additional alias/column
operands for joins, ordering, identity, and scope witnesses are counted once
per source occurrence. Shared bindings retain their complete occurrence
identity; physical-row equality never licenses DISTINCT. The reference-only
discovery relation cannot supply payload.

For name `k`, value `v`, nullable flag `q`, field count `m`, row count `n`, sum
of row lengths `L`, and `h(n)=ceil(log2(n))` with `h(0)=0`, the exact work is:

```text
F(k,v) = 2 + UTF8_length(k) + q + 8 + canonical_value_octets(v)
R(row) = 2 + SUM(F(k,v))
S(f) = 10 + UTF8_length(domain_f) + 8*n + L
A(f) = 16*n + 2*h(n)*L
M(f) = 26 + UTF8_length(family_id) + 16*m
W(f) = S(f) + A(f) + M(f)
W = SUM(W(f) for all 89 families)
    + distinct_bound_retained_document_octets + 65,536 + 1,048,576
```

`A` reserves deterministic stable-mergesort work and `M` counts the scalar
preflight report. The stream reserve is 65,536 octets and the response reserve
is 1,048,576 octets. The contract carries executable arithmetic ASTs. Work is a
deterministic accounting quantity, not an RSS or database latency measurement.
Python preload, PostgreSQL commit, and historical read each apply this complete
ledger separately; their charges do not accumulate across phases.

The simultaneous ceilings are 20,000 combined nodes, 40,000 dependencies,
2,000 external rows, 2,000 authorship bindings, 256 dirty generations, one MiB
per bounded canonical value, 1,000 response rows/one MiB encoded response, and
`W <= 67,108,864`. Every family retains its exact count and byte subcaps.
Checked nonnegative int64 arithmetic rejects overflow before multiplication or
addition. Existing history ceilings remain 16/28/40 MiB for draft/requested/
terminal history. The terminal acceptance event is included in terminal history.

Every decision/node/dependency/external/authorship/signoff/event authority row
has one exact pending frame; sentinel and pending do not copy themselves.
Pending identities include decision, unprefixed family, and canonical frame
ordinal. SQL and historical read reserve the same exact virtual pending widths
without querying or allocating a nonexistent pending SQL table. Flush does not
add an occurrence. Pending copies are discarded on commit or rollback.

At commit/read the terminal event may also occur in the source history. The
explicit overlap operation checks its physical identity and every shared 0029
column, rejects duplicates or mismatches, then excludes that source occurrence
and charges the full 0030 output once. Historical reconstruction uses verified
frozen proposal/projection/cutoff membership. Live heads are current-eligibility
inputs only; missing frozen authority fails closed without substitution.

Retained payload work counts each exact distinct bound document tuple
`(id,content_hash,storage_bytes)` once; differing hash/size for the same ID fails.
Actual stream size/hash must match. External closure permits only the approved
metadata masks, bounded visited identity, reciprocal links, and unique heads.
No external document, target proposal, typed owner, or payload is authorized.
Cap+1 counts, anti-join integrity checks, scalar widths, output/pending sizing,
and all subcaps precede the next payload fetch or allocation.

The downstream integration validator checks all 63 frozen authority files,
55 registries/1,926 occurrences, 31 ordered registries/1,581 entries and at
least 10,961 exact-diagnostic freshness executions, separately from semantic
mutations. It checks frozen authority hashes, complete inventories,
mapping-to-persistence coverage, occurrence/anchor/type facts, phase formulas,
and honest evidence status, then replays the source, persistence, resource, and
current mapping components read-only. The resource workload exercises all 89
families and seven authority-derived pending frames: 1,279,635 framed/sort/report/
reserve octets plus 65,829,229 retained bytes equals 67,108,864; one more retained
byte gives 67,108,865. This is a typed width workload, not a full persisted graph.

Production SQL enforcement, historical-read/cutoff enforcement, production
query/allocation spies, real 64 MiB persistence/driver-memory measurements,
migration/runtime privileges, and response serializer/page spies are **NOT_RUN**.
Declarative SQL arithmetic and design dispatcher controls are not those proofs.
Its only successful builder status is
`DESIGN_INTEGRATION_VALIDATED_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW`; this status grants
neither independent overall design approval nor production permission. H-004/
H-005 design-level dispositions belong to the immutable component reviews,
not this validator. Calibration replay and isolated sentinel-topology replay
remain design evidence, never production SQL/read/query-spy proof. The finalized
matrix is hash-bound downstream; it does not consume validator, result,
provenance or future overall-review hashes.

## 9. PostgreSQL commit rules

Every decision owns one internal sentinel with `generation` initially 0 and
`sealed=false`. Every authority-child `INSERT` has an `AFTER STATEMENT`
transition-table trigger that locks the sentinel, rejects a sealed decision,
increments generation once per statement, and rejects generation above 256.
Authority UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE is rejected. A deferred constraint trigger on
sentinel INSERT/UPDATE performs the full aggregate validation only when
`sealed=false`, then sets `sealed=true`; callbacks caused by later dirty updates
or the seal return without another graph scan. An early `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL
IMMEDIATE` seals the aggregate, so any later child statement fails. A later
transaction also sees sealed and fails before mutation. The runtime role cannot
write the sentinel directly, execute its functions, or disable triggers.
Authority tables and three trigger functions are owned by the non-login
`s4b_trusted_owner` role, which is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS. Functions
are `SECURITY DEFINER`, fix a hardened `search_path`, and qualify safe names.
PUBLIC/runtime EXECUTE and runtime sentinel DML are revoked; runtime has named
authority INSERT/read grants only, owns no relation/sequence, has no DDL or role
membership escape, and cannot `SET ROLE s4b_trusted_owner`. Catalog assertions
freeze function owner/security/search-path, relation/sequence owner and ACLs,
trigger inventory/state, role attributes, and membership before and after attack
tests. The PostgreSQL 16.14 harness proves legitimate runtime-login writes and
rejects 43 direct attacks with SQLSTATE 42501.
The closed inventory is: decision root registers its sentinel; node gates,
dependencies, external dependencies, authorship bindings, acceptance signoffs,
and acceptance-kind review-case events dirty it. A decision may not seal before
all six child families have contributed their exact expected set/cardinality;
an event for a rejection branch never targets a 4B sentinel.

The one-shot validator independently:

1. lock actor/membership, gates, proposal/projections/case/request/event in order;
2. require enabled acceptance and exact authorization action;
3. rederive all-verified observation and stable-request equality;
4. rederive cutoff/authorship and exclude signer;
5. derive expected node rows from semantic and typed-owner tables and compare
   both `EXCEPT` directions;
6. derive all dependency/external/authorship rows bidirectionally;
7. validate gates/reasons/representation/root roles, acyclicity, and `max`
   effective gates against the complete truth table;
8. recompute row, set, decision, signoff, signature, and event hashes/counts;
9. prove one request -> decision -> signoff -> terminal event, exclusive of
   rejection; and
10. reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE or extra/missing objects; and
11. perform the commit-boundary actor/membership, source-head, external-target-
    head/reciprocal, request, and predecessor-event CAS recheck.

Submitted JSON, counts, digests, reasons, or signer sets never prove themselves.
The SQL derives expected sets with one aggregate pass per family and compares
both `EXCEPT` directions; it does not run a full-graph validator once per child.
The limit/max-plus-one benchmark and query plans are frozen in
[`sql-topology-benchmark.md`](sql-topology-benchmark.md).

## 10. Read-time verification

One read-only repeatable-read snapshot verifies the 0029 prefix; dispatches all
recorded versions or fails `historical_verifier_unavailable`; reconstructs
frozen candidate/evidence/3A/3B; streams all graph rows under ceilings and
compares to the Python expectation; recomputes all hashes/bijections; then
computes current eligibility separately.

Corruption returns `review_integrity`; unavailable retained evidence returns a
distinct fail-closed source status. Neither returns partially trusted semantics
or calls a released consumer.

## 11. Direct-SQL corruption matrix

Each row requires a positive control and failing direct-SQL case. Node and edge
cases are parameterized across every type/kind above.

| family | required corruptions |
| --- | --- |
| decision identity | wrong case/request/proposal/directive/projection ID/hash/version/digest; unequal stable identities |
| non-authority | false release block; non-none authority effect; any release-like state/event/payload |
| node inventory | missing/extra/duplicate/cross-slice/projection; wrong type/key/pointer/parent/ordinal/identity/canonical hash |
| node semantics | wrong representation/base/effective/root/reason/evidence count/hash; fabricated actionable |
| dependencies | missing/extra/swapped/cross-decision; wrong kind/ordinal/propagation; duplicate mapping consumption |
| algorithms | every base/child/multi-child/integrity/noncontrolling truth-table row; rule/expression/prerequisite cycle; wrong max effective gate; noncontrolling root in aggregate |
| external | positive outgoing resolved/unresolved/ambiguous and incoming resolved; missing/extra; illegal state/reason/nullability; wrong target/source/hash/head/reciprocal |
| authorship | missing/extra/forged; wrong bound/count/set hash; omitted signer; post-request append |
| authorization | inactive/wrong-role/cross-user/cross-org; forged snapshot; role/status race |
| signoff | wrong decision/request/observation/authorship/action/signature/time; duplicate |
| lifecycle | wrong predecessor/state; acceptance with rejection IDs; rejection with acceptance IDs; absent/extra object/event |
| idempotency/concurrency | key reuse with different bytes; duplicate predecessor; accept/accept and accept/reject; reciprocal A↔B; external target-head append; Slice-3A materializer races; changed preflight target set causes rollback/retry |
| freshness | changed relationship, evidence head/source bytes, 3A/3B head, mapping digest, or 3B parent |
| cardinality/hash | wrong counts/order/set/decision hash; over declared bound |
| downgrade | enabled gate; each occupied table; acceptance event; incomplete 0029 restoration |

Every forbidden release-like spelling is attempted in scalar and canonical
payload fields; CHECK and deferred semantic validation both reject it.

## Independence boundary

The enumerator imports only standard-library modules. It does not import or
call any acceptance builder, generated acceptance expectation module, mapping
manifest, or SQL fragment. It does not import the `app` package and asserts
that no application module is present in `sys.modules` at completion.

The input surface is deliberately narrow:

1. Five existing proposal JSON fixtures.
2. Existing source and fragment manifests for deterministic portable binding
   substitutions, identical in value to the established test convention.
3. The three AST-selected functions `_known`, `_member`, and
   `validator2_calibration_envelope` from the existing calibration test.
   No import, decorator, top-level test, or application function from that module
   is executed. Their whole source file hash is bound into the golden.
4. This independent script's explicit canonical array policies, graph traversal,
   gate/reason branches, dependency relationships, reachability, and max lattice.

The script contains its own graph traversal and source-key canonicalization.
Reading existing projection code and comparing its output was used to confirm
projection truth; no projection builder or generated mapping participates in
golden generation. The separate comparison below imports existing projection
builders solely to compare the independently enumerated source node shape.
It cannot calculate acceptance edges, reasons, effective gates, or semantic
graph golden hashes for the enumerator.

The calibration transform is intentionally shared fixture truth, so this is
independent of acceptance implementation, not independent of the fixture author.
An adversarial reviewer must still examine the independently written rules and
confirm that the portable hashes serve the eventual integration test oracle.

## Hash identity and ordering

Portable source-node identities are the literal tuple encoded as
`slice:type:source-pointer`. The pointer is rooted at the canonical proposal;
slice distinguishes the two semantic inventories. Node keys reproduce source
keys, with one explicit substitution: an identity-mapping key that is a persisted
source-node ID is replaced by that source node's portable identity. Structural
parents and edge endpoints use the same substitution. Source ordinals remain
source ordinals; gate-edge slots are separately specified.

Canonical object keys sort by UTF-16 code units; fixture sets sort by their
explicit stable key (or encoded value), and sequence arrays retain order.
No numeric/null fixture values are permitted. Output count/ordinal metadata
uses JSON integers and structural root parents use null. These are design-oracle
JSON conventions, not a claim to implement production acceptance JCS envelopes.

Node set order is slice, pointer, type, key, portable ID. Edge set order is
parent portable ID, edge kind, ordinal, child portable ID. SHA-256 domains are
`independent-acceptance-semantic-oracle-1:nodes\\0`,
`...:edges\\0`, and `...:graph\\0`, where `\\0` is one NUL byte.
Graph hash binds both full sorted arrays. Portable candidate and 3A/3B subtree
hashes are unprefixed SHA-256 of the independently canonicalized content;
they are labeled accordingly and are not persisted projection IDs/hashes.

Root-role reachability includes listed propagating dependencies and structural
ownership. Structural ownership does not introduce extra gate-propagation edges.
This accounts for product manufacturer/sourceValue assertions, whose source
parent is the product scope even though the current dependency contract links
the product directly to its identity mapping. Every mapping is consumed once,
including series-expression mappings. Rule-expression object roots have source
ordinal zero even when their gate edge is condition slot one. Recurrence
expression/timing gate slots are zero/one, respectively.

## Unclosed scope and required later evidence

These are exact portable semantic graph goldens, not a complete persisted
acceptance oracle. The following cannot honestly be frozen from portable
fixtures alone and are not fabricated:

- persisted candidate evidence-set hash, 3A/3B projection IDs/hashes/event heads;
- evidence-link IDs and hashes, lifecycle admission records, authorship users/
  source IDs, signer exclusion, authorization observations, and their set hashes;
- resolved or ambiguous external dependencies and incoming signals;
- request, decision-content/row, signoff/signature, terminal event, and audit
  timestamps/identity hashes;
- actual retained source-byte verification and official-admission proof;
- correction foundation/binding reconstruction and unchanged released/V3
  database-state digest;
- independent hand approval or adversarial review of the generated numbers.

The production integration slice must create deterministic persisted fixture
identities, verify all source/admission/projection prerequisites, translate
persisted IDs to the portable identities above, and compare full semantic graph
hashes/counts before signing. Persisted and external/authorship/signoff hashes
need separate independently specified vectors. These gaps are mandatory
implementation/verification work, not accepted risk or evidence of completion.

## Evidence ownership and selector coverage

Every semantic node binds source selector, source pointer, purpose, cardinality,
inheritance=`none`, ordered evidence keys, and key-set hash into its node/graph
hash. `evidenceOwnerInventory` partitions all nodes by slice/type/policy with
exact owner/link counts, including zero-link families. Portable evidence
owner-set hashes bind each node's policy and keys. Link totals are 65, 130, 94,
85, and 59 in packet order above.

There is no generic parent-evidence inheritance. Identity mappings, expressions,
designation values/ranges, and action steps have zero direct links. Product
manufacturer/sourceValue assertions use the explicit normalizedIdentity
key selector. Other evidence-owning nodes use their own key sets. The separate
projection comparison passed for every observed evidence owner/purpose/key pair.

All eight identity selectors have explicit presence rules, present-mapping
counts, absent-source-slot counts, and named absence reasons including zero
counts. Model and series-expression member mappings are both mandatory;
absence for an existing member is forbidden. Search-group coverage names paired,
source_group, and unknown/conflicting_evidence, unknown/source_ambiguous, and
unknown/other. Search-model and condition-member coverage names model and
series_expression. Zero denotes unexercised fixture coverage, not an impossible
branch.

Observed search-hint coverage is concentrated in 2002: seven paired groups,
19 model members, and one series-expression member. No packet exercises an
unknown search group. Five synthetic oracle-only vectors passed: paired and
source_group -> exact/candidate/noncontrolling_search_hint; conflicting_evidence
and source_ambiguous unknowns -> explicit_unknown/human with matching reasons;
other unknown -> explicit_unknown/candidate/source_value_unresolved. Two member
vectors passed model/noncontrolling_search_hint and
series_expression/unsupported_expression. These are oracle checks, not
production integration tests or independent review approval.

The closure-1 review correctly found that the earlier JSON accepted duplicated
IDs, prose predicates, and three contradictory presence rules. The controlling
design is now produced and checked by the stdlib-only
`acceptance-design-validator.py`. It imports no `app.*` module. It reconstructs
the hash-bound canonical V2 schema by applying the exact candidate-service V2
overlay to the base extraction schema, then freezes 29 enums, 31 constants,
eight union sites with 29 discriminator-complete alternatives, and 25 optional
property sites. Every union alternative has a nonempty closed discriminator.

The emitted Draft 2020-12 schema uses exact `const` source inventories and
`prefixItems`/`const` for the ordered 28 node, 40 edge, eight identity, and six
external inventories. The independent stdlib checks additionally enforce
unique/exact IDs, reference integrity, typed-owner/table parity, no unknown
keys, no semantic placeholder phrases, and current source/resource hashes.
Future generators must pass both validations before consuming the manifest.

The corrected contracts are:

- E02: each of `modelScope`, `serialScope`, and `partNumberScope` contributes
  zero or one edge independently; the total is zero through three.
- E13: `scopeExpression` is required and `conditionExpression` contributes an
  edge only when present.
- A01/I01: a product manufacturer identity mapping exists whenever the
  manufacturer object exists, even when its normalized state is unknown or
  not applicable.

`acceptance-synthetic-vectors.py` is a second stdlib-only executable. Its saved
result binds its own source hash, the manifest hash, and the unchanged five-
packet golden hash. It selects exactly one case for each of 53 branch-policy
cases and records eight optional-scope combinations, two condition-expression
presence cases, one normalized-unknown manufacturer case, four five-packet-zero
search-group branches, and all 29 source-union alternatives. Both validator and
synthetic output report `runtimeApplicationImports: []`.

## Decision and bounded invariant

The installed PostgreSQL 16.14 schema produced by existing migrations through
`20260913_0029` is physical authority. Correct exactly four ORM metadata leaves
in `backend/app/models/core.py` to describe that schema:

| ORM field | Required metadata | Deliberately unchanged |
|---|---|---|
| `ADV4CandidateCorrectionSemanticBinding.obligation_projection_id` | `String(36)` | `Optional[str]`, nullable, no default, FK/check/unique definitions |
| `ADV4CandidateCorrectionSemanticBinding.obligation_semantic_node_id` | `String(36)` | `Optional[str]`, nullable, no default, FK/check/unique definitions |
| `ADV4FeatureGate.enabled` | server default SQL `false` | `Boolean`, nonnullable, application `default=False` |
| `ADV4FeatureGate.changed_by` | server default literal `migration` | `String(128)`, nonnullable, application `default="migration"` |

`String`, `Boolean`, and `text` are already imported from SQLAlchemy at
`core.py:6`. **No import is added, removed, or reordered.** Use
`server_default=text("false")`, not a quoted string containing the word false;
this renders SQL `DEFAULT false` and has the same SQL expression/default facts
as migration 0027's `sa.false()`. Use `server_default="migration"`, exactly the
migration's literal form, which renders `DEFAULT 'migration'`. Do not replace
application defaults with server defaults. Do not add validators, value
normalization, string truncation, eager-default flags, new FKs, or on-delete
changes.

The earlier bootstrap proposal used the illustrative spelling `sa.false()`.
The frozen spelling here uses the already imported `text` and produces the same
physical SQL/default expression without an extra import. This is a declaration
spelling decision, not a different default value or a waived discrepancy.

## Evidence and why there is no migration

At current `core.py:1539-1540`, the two obligation IDs use
`mapped_column(nullable=True)` and resolve to unbounded `String()`/`varchar`.
Migration `20260911_0028_add_ad_v4_obligations.py:808-809` already adds them as
nullable `sa.String(36)` columns. The fresh, hash-bound installed catalog confirms
`character varying(36)` with no server default for both.

At `core.py:913` and `:915`, the feature-gate columns already have application
defaults `False` and `"migration"`. Migration
`20260907_0027_add_ad_v4_applicability.py:101` and `:103` already installs physical
server defaults `false` and `'migration'`. The installed catalog reports
`boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` and
`character varying(128) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'migration'::character varying`.
Migration 0029 changes the gate-key set and administrative function, not these
four physical leaves.

The reviewed physical snapshot covers 74 relations, 983 columns, 879 constraints,
307 indexes, 208 noninternal triggers and 69 functions. Its canonical observation
SHA-256 is
`0583a88e75fb95e9c1e4a7237cc63aba13bf86d5656061db7298af6a8286d871`.
The proposal changes the ORM's description, not that database. No new Alembic
revision, upgrade, downgrade, `ALTER TABLE`, backfill, row rewrite, canonical
rehash, or application data update is needed or allowed. Existing migrations
must remain byte-identical. Fresh migration-based databases will keep installing
the same schema as before; existing migrated databases require no DDL at rollout.
A deployment whose physical leaves differ must fail the comparison and be
separately investigated, not silently repaired by this metadata-only change.

## Runtime meaning, compatibility, and explicit limits

For **supported migration-created PostgreSQL databases**, all stored values,
accepted SQL domains, defaults, constraints, row identities, audit bytes, hashes,
capability versions, gates, authorization and locking remain unchanged. A
`String(36)` declaration does not trim a value or add application validation;
the existing database already enforces the physical width. Ordinary string
binding/result handling must remain identical. Existing Slice-3A NULL obligation
IDs remain NULL; existing Slice-3B IDs remain exactly the same strings. FKs,
nullable union branches and reconstruction checks are untouched.

Normal ORM inserts still supply the existing application defaults when those
values are omitted. Explicit `True`/`False` and explicit `changed_by` values still
win over defaults. Attribute `None` and SQL `null()` are distinct ORM inputs and
must be tested separately; neither is licensed to enable a gate. Explicit SQL
NULL remains prohibited for the two nonnullable gate columns. Direct SQL on an
already migrated database already receives the two server defaults when columns
are omitted, so it cannot gain a new enabled capability from this edit.
Administrative `paprnav_set_v4_feature_gate` remains unchanged and writes explicit
`p_enabled`, `p_actor`, and `now()` under the existing lock order.

Mixed old/new application binaries operating against the same migrated 0029
schema therefore retain the same data contract. This does **not** expand the
supported schema-version boundary: an application expecting 0028/0029 is not
made compatible with an earlier schema that lacks obligation columns. Existing
capability checks and old-reader/rollback tests remain authoritative.

There is one intentional observable metadata-DDL change, which must not be
hidden under a blanket "no behavior change" claim. A *new* database created via
`Base.metadata.create_all()` will now render widths/defaults matching these four
physical leaves. Current SQLite test fixtures use `create_all()` at
`backend/tests/conftest.py:30-43`; new raw inserts omitting the gate fields will
now obtain defaults there instead of failing non-null checks. SQLite does not
enforce PostgreSQL varchar length, so it is not a width oracle. This is correction
of the test/metadata DDL description, not a production migration or a new runtime
meaning for a migrated deployment. Existing metadata-created schemas are not
altered by `create_all()`; tests must recreate their disposable schemas. No
production schema bootstrap via `create_all()` was found in the inspected app or
scripts; production must continue using Alembic.

No claim of universal equivalence for arbitrary custom schema-creation tools,
SQL compilation consumers, or unsupported schemas is made. Such consumers must
consume the corrected metadata authority or receive a separately reviewed
migration decision. The safety claim is the bounded, falsifiable migrated-schema
invariant, not an assertion that metadata bytes cannot change.

## Reflection and autogenerate

Design inspection used the installed SQLAlchemy **2.0.52** and Alembic **1.19.1**;
`backend/requirements.txt` does not pin those packages. Record versions again at
implementation verification and investigate differences rather than assuming
this behavior across arbitrary versions.

Reflection describes installed types/nullability/server defaults and will expose
length 36 and PostgreSQL's quoted/cast default expression. Reflection does not
reconstruct Python application defaults. Preserve and assert those separately.

`backend/app/db/migrations/env.py` configures `target_metadata` but does not turn
on `compare_server_default`. Alembic's installed
`DefaultImpl._column_args_match()` avoids flagging a specified argument against
an unspecified one. A read-only design diagnostic confirmed that
`compare_type(varchar(36), varchar)` and `compare_type(varchar(36), varchar(36))`
both return false in this version. Therefore ordinary `alembic check` or absence
of a generated revision does **not** prove the current widths are correct.

The verification must combine exact metadata/reflection assertions with a
read-only autogenerate comparison using `compare_type=True` and
`compare_server_default=True`. Scope its no-op expectation to the four approved
columns; exclude unrelated indexes/constraints from that particular comparison,
and separately prove their inventories are unchanged. Do not claim the entire
repository ORM perfectly reproduces migration-owned SQL functions, triggers or
additional constraints. A full unfiltered comparison may retain unrelated
baseline differences; compare its before/after operation inventory and reject
new out-of-scope deltas without modifying unrelated metadata. Never run
`alembic revision --autogenerate` as this change's implementation step.

Required bounded no-physical-delta test body, against a freshly migrated disposable
PostgreSQL database and the corrected model:

```python
from alembic.autogenerate import compare_metadata
from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
from app.db.base import Base
from app.models import core

scope = {
    "ad_v4_candidate_correction_semantic_bindings": {
        "obligation_projection_id", "obligation_semantic_node_id"},
    "ad_v4_feature_gates": {"enabled", "changed_by"},
}
def include_object(obj, name, kind, reflected, compare_to):
    if kind == "table":
        return name in scope
    if kind == "column":
        return obj.table.name in scope and name in scope[obj.table.name]
    return False

# connection must be the verified disposable PostgreSQL connection.
context = MigrationContext.configure(connection, opts={
    "compare_type": True, "compare_server_default": True,
    "include_object": include_object,
})
assert compare_metadata(context, Base.metadata) == []
```

## Affected consumers and non-changes

- `ad_v4_candidates.require_v4_database_gate` (`:929` onward) reads the persisted
  gate and fails closed for missing/disabled values. `ad_v4_reviews._database_gates`
  (`:135` onward) locks/reads persisted flags in its existing order. Their
  conditions, queries, defaults-on-missing behavior and exceptions are unchanged.
- `ad_v4_applicability.py:2924-2997` reads correction bindings and verifies slice,
  proposal, projection, nullable fields, semantic node, and hashes; `:3258`
  constructs Slice-3A bindings with obligation fields absent/NULL. No selector,
  canonical payload or verifier changes.
- `ad_v4_obligations.py:3785-3840` constructs/folds Slice-3B binding IDs and hashes.
  `ad_v4_obligation_persistence.py:365-370` persists them;
  `:1034-1043` reconstructs exact binding rows via `obligation_projection_id`.
  Python dataclasses, identity generation, SQL predicates and values are unchanged.
- Existing gate seed SQL and `paprnav_set_v4_feature_gate` in migrations
  0027/0028/0029 remain unchanged. No rollout toggle or administrator action is
  requested. Test helpers that explicitly supply gate fields keep doing so.
- The source-catalog validator is an intentional metadata consumer: after the
  approved edit it must observe zero discrepancies, not whitelist the old four.
  Source hashes and declaration facts must be refreshed under separate authority;
  running it against old frozen bytes first must fail rather than silently accept
  stale hashes. No resource mapping/oracle generation is enabled by that refresh.

## Falsifiable invariants and required verification

These are **planned tests, not implementation results**. The proposed test files
below do not exist as outputs of this decision. They require separate write
scope after design approval. Every PostgreSQL check uses an explicitly verified,
freshly migrated disposable PostgreSQL-16 database; no developer/production DB
may be substituted. Skipped PostgreSQL tests are not passing evidence.

### A. Exact metadata leaves and no fifth change

Proposed `backend/tests/test_ad_v4_model_source_authority.py` must contain:

1. `test_correction_obligation_id_metadata_matches_installed_0028`: for exactly
   both named columns assert `isinstance(type, String)`, `.type.length == 36`,
   `.nullable is True`, `.default is None`, `.server_default is None`,
   `.onupdate is None`, and `.server_onupdate is None`. Assert both existing
   named composite FKs and the slice-union check are unchanged, including full
   ordered column/reference tuples. Do not replace them with inferred scalar FKs.
2. `test_gate_defaults_preserve_application_and_physical_defaults`: assert
   `enabled` is Boolean/nonnullable with `.default.arg is False` and
   `str(.server_default.arg) == "false"`; assert `changed_by` is String(128),
   nonnullable with `.default.arg == "migration"` and
   `.server_default.arg == "migration"`. Assert `changed_at` remains timezone-
   aware with `func.now()` and its prior nullable/default attributes.
3. `test_only_four_model_metadata_leaves_changed`: compare the complete live
   `fresh_model_catalog()` to the bound baseline catalog, replacing only the
   two type profiles (length 36, UTF-8 max 144 and compiled varchar(36)) and two
   server-default facts. Require exact equality of every other column fact,
   table identity/order, PK/FK/check/unique/index and application default. Also
   require the source diff to equal the four-line proposal above and all
   migrations to retain their bound hashes. This proves the no-op comparator's
   column filter cannot conceal an unrelated edit.
4. `test_string_width_metadata_does_not_rewrite_bound_values`: assert the
   PostgreSQL dialect's String bind/result processors for unbounded String and
   String(36) have identical handling of NULL and unchanged strings, including
   36 and 37 characters. Database width enforcement is verified separately;
   this test must not claim client-side String length validation.
5. `test_orm_gate_defaults_and_explicit_values` parameterized over omitted,
   attribute `None`, explicit false/actor and explicit true/actor for ordinary
   ORM flush/refresh, ORM bulk insert, and SQLAlchemy Core insert. Omitted or
   ordinary ORM None inputs retain `(False, "migration")`; Core explicit None
   is an explicit SQL NULL and must fail non-null validation rather than be
   confused with omitted input. Explicit values round-trip unchanged.
   Test ORM `sqlalchemy.null()` separately and require non-null rejection.
   Assert field values after flush and requery, not just constructor attributes.

### B. Fresh PostgreSQL, defaults, width and no physical delta

Proposed `backend/tests/test_ad_v4_model_source_authority_postgres.py` must contain:

1. `test_reflected_four_leaves_equal_exact_metadata`: migrate 0001–0029 and use
   SQLAlchemy inspection plus `pg_attribute`/`pg_attrdef` to assert both ID widths,
   nullable bits, absent ID defaults, Boolean default false, String(128) literal
   default migration, and unchanged PK/FK/checks. Normalize only PostgreSQL's
   explicit quoting/type casts for comparing the same constant default; retain
   exact installed expressions in evidence.
2. `test_metadata_import_produces_no_catalog_change`: compare the entire 74-table,
   69-function bootstrap physical observation before/after importing the corrected
   models and exercising ORM reads. All facts and canonical snapshot hash must
   remain equal to the bound physical snapshot. A changed owner, ACL, function,
   trigger, width, default or constraint fails this invariant.
3. `test_four_column_autogenerate_produces_no_operations`: execute the exact
   bounded comparison above with both compare flags true; require `[]`. Also
   prove the strict assertions detect a deliberately changed width of 35 or 37,
   an unbounded width, a flipped/null default or a removed application default.
   The unspecified-width mutation must be killed by exact metadata assertions,
   even if Alembic ignores it.
4. `test_direct_sql_gate_defaults_are_existing_physical_defaults`: in a transaction
   on the disposable migrated database, delete only the seeded
   `validator2_write_enabled` row, insert that allowed key without `enabled` or
   `changed_by`, and require returned `enabled is False`,
   `changed_by == "migration"`, and nonnull `changed_at`. Roll back to restore
   the seed. Repeat with explicit values and with explicit NULL (SQLSTATE 23502,
   isolated savepoints); no constraints/triggers may be disabled. Use the existing
   allowed gate key rather than an invented key that would violate the gate check.
   Direct SQL must behave identically before/after the model-only edit.
5. `test_postgres_orm_gate_insert_preserves_values_and_defaults`: repeat A.5 on
   PostgreSQL, with ordinary Session, bulk and Core paths explicitly distinguished,
   a rollback-restored seeded key, and direct SQL requery of stored values.
   Confirm no omitted-input path produces enabled=true. Existing gate readers
   still report the inserted default-false gate disabled.
6. `test_corrected_ids_preserve_existing_rows_and_database_width`: use the existing
   valid Slice-3A/Slice-3B materialization fixtures with real parent rows, check
   both-slice reconstructors and canonical hashes before/after switching model
   metadata, and assert identical IDs/NULLs/bytes. Attempt a 37-character ID in
   each physical column in a rollback-only savepoint and require PostgreSQL
   SQLSTATE 22001, not silent trimming. Existing valid IDs of at most 36
   characters must round-trip. Do not use a short invalid FK as a positive case.

## Rollback and deployment sequence

1. Independent reviewer approves this decision; coordinator explicitly authorizes
   the bounded production edit and test-file scope. No such approval is claimed.
2. Apply only the frozen model diff, add approved tests, run the required matrix,
   and obtain separate implementation review. Never alter the installed schema
   to match the formerly incorrect unbounded/default-free metadata.
3. Refresh/replay the bootstrap only under explicit artifact-write authority and
   obtain independent bootstrap closure. Mapping/resource and overall Slice-4B
   gates remain distinct; this correction is not permission to cross them.
4. If rollback is required, revert only these four metadata lines and the
   separately approved accompanying tests/artifact revision. No Alembic downgrade,
   row update, hash change or DDL is part of rollback. The database remains the
   authoritative migrated 0029 schema and old binaries retain their previous
   behavior. Reverting reintroduces the four metadata discrepancies, so restore
   blocked bootstrap status and invalidate dependent approval/hash evidence.
   Never retain an approved refreshed catalog while reverting its model source.

Alternatives rejected: widen the database IDs to unbounded varchar, remove
physical defaults, change Python defaults, add a redundant Alembic migration,
or waive/whitelist the mismatches. Each either changes authority/runtime meaning,
adds needless deployment risk, or fails SBI-B-001's consumer-parity invariant.

### First failed run and dispositions

Before the final run, the same PostgreSQL module was run against the first
freshly migrated container on port `59953`. It exited `1` with **3 passed and
3 failed** in `2.45s`. All three failures were test-only defects; no production
edit followed:

1. The reflected check text placed the PostgreSQL cast on the column
   (`binding_slice::text`) rather than after the equality expression. The test
   expectation was corrected to the exact reflected spelling.
2. Repeated delete/reinsert cases reused one Session identity map, so a gate
   reader could observe a stale mapped identity during the assertion. The test
   now expunges identities at the case boundary before exercising the reader;
   stored SQL values were already correct.
3. The imported correction fixture deliberately produced a Slice-3B
   requirement correction only. The test now also creates a valid
   independently materialized Slice-3A `productScopes` correction and verifies
   both branches rather than claiming the original fixture covered both.

The failed-run container was destroyed rather than reused. The corrected test
module then passed on the replacement empty/migrated database. An earlier
URL-unset collection yielded six skips and was explicitly treated as
non-passing preflight evidence, not as PostgreSQL verification.

## 2. Exact retained ACL rule

Canonicalize declared ACLs with aclexplode(COALESCE(relacl,
acldefault(kind,relowner))). Relkind r/p/v/m/f maps to ACL kind r; sequence S
maps to lowercase s; i/I/t/c or unknown kinds reject. Current retained
allowlist is only r. Column default kind is c. PUBLIC is grantee OID zero,
not a role named PUBLIC. Join all nonzero principals to pg_roles, anti-join
unknown owners/grantors/grantees before expansion, reject zero grantor and
duplicates, and retain grantor/grantee/privilege/isGrantable exactly.

Principal shape remains {"kind":"PUBLIC","name":null} or
{"kind":"ROLE","name":"exact role name"}. The separate identity map records
each role's OID. Sort by PUBLIC-before-ROLE grantee rank, grantee name C,
grantor name C, privilege C, grantability false before true. Arrays remain
arrays; empty tuples are [], never null. Table-like privilege enum is DELETE,
INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE; sequence enum SELECT,
UPDATE, USAGE; column enum INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, UPDATE. Do not infer
owner grant options, merge grantors, expand inherited/effective rights or
collapse column ACLs into table privileges.

These are the PostgreSQL 16 ACL APIs; uppercase S is a foreign-server default,
not a sequence default. [PostgreSQL ACL functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/functions-info.html)

Native raw equality includes NULL versus empty, ACL item order, dimensions,
all privilege/grant-option bits and OIDs resolved to the original principals.
Owners may have revoked their own ordinary privileges, so explicit empty
cannot be replaced with owner defaults. The new table stores the native
aclitem[] as well as the independently checked canonical representation.
[PostgreSQL privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/ddl-priv.html)

After a successful empty downgrade, accept each retained relation only if:

~~~text
identities/owner/relkind/non-ACL facts unchanged
AND all retained raw column/function/schema ACLs unchanged
AND canonical relation ACL unchanged
AND (
  pre.relacl IS NOT DISTINCT FROM post.relacl
  OR (
    exact allowlist member AND original relkind='r'
    AND pre.relacl IS NULL AND post.relacl IS NOT NULL
    AND post.relacl IS NOT DISTINCT FROM acldefault('r', original_owner_oid)
  )
)
~~~

The exception never applies to an aborted migration, any non-NULL pre-ACL,
column/schema/function ACLs, an unlisted relation, extra zero-privilege item,
default-plus-extra grant, missing owner privilege, wrong grantor/option/owner,
or an altered native representation. Retain actual before/after raw digests;
do not pretend the old raw digest was restored.
