Same-name/new-OID, schema move/replacement, owner/OID change, role replacement
and kind change are identity failures, even when names or canonical grants
look equivalent. Lookup the captured OID first, then compare exact schema
name/OID, relation name/OID, owner name/OID and kind. Never resolve by name and
silently accept whichever object currently occupies it.

## 3. Database-local snapshot authority

### 3.1 Trust root and relation

Family: acl_rollback_snapshot. Exact relation:
public.ad_v4_acl_rollback_snapshots. Version:
paprnav-ad-v4-persistence-acl-snapshot-1. Policy:
paprnav-ad-v4-persistence-acl-rollback-2. Role binding version:
paprnav-ad-v4-database-role-binding-1.

The repository-approved migration and persistence contract create the table.
Its owner is the persisted per-database s4b_trusted_owner role, not runtime,
login or PUBLIC. All runtime/login/PUBLIC table and column privileges are
empty, and no API, ORM relationship, export, graph selector or runtime helper
reads it. No sequences, identity defaults, RLS escape or SECURITY DEFINER
read endpoint is introduced. The migration administrator can read it through
its existing trusted DDL authority; application runtime cannot assume that
administrator or the trusted owner.

The supported bootstrap executor is a trusted cluster-administration session,
with session_user.rolsuper=true, distinct from every application runtime
principal. This deliberately avoids PostgreSQL 16's automatic non-superuser
role-creator membership variants. Do not grant superuser privilege to a
runtime account to meet it. A deployment without this existing authorized
DDL executor fails before mutation; a managed non-superuser bootstrap profile
requires its own later reviewed contract. SQL superuser/owner tampering is
outside the enforcement trust boundary, as it is for every existing protected
authority table. Hashes detect corruption; they do not authenticate a malicious
database administrator.

Before any retained-object ACL, owner, function or schema mutation, the
transaction locks/captures the 0029 facts, creates the three new roles and this
new table, inserts its complete closed rows and verifies the seal. New-object
creation/ownership initialization is permitted during capture; no retained
object may be changed before sealing. The new roles' actual allocated OIDs
are thereby stored in the same atomic unit. No hidden table or out-of-band
receipt is added later.

### 3.2 Exact 24 ordered fields

No field has a SQL/server/application default. All mandatory values are
supplied by the reviewed migration; no application model inserts audit rows.
Nullable means SQL NULL is allowed only in the discriminated arms below.

| # | Field | PostgreSQL type | Nullable | Exact rule |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | snapshot_version | varchar(64) | NO | constant paprnav-ad-v4-persistence-acl-snapshot-1 |
| 2 | row_kind | varchar(16) | NO | HEAD | RELATION | COLUMN | DELTA | ROLE |
| 3 | row_ordinal | integer | NO | 0..1137, primary key |
| 4 | relation_ordinal | smallint | YES | 1..74 when applicable |
| 5 | attribute_number | smallint | YES | positive original attnum when applicable |
| 6 | relation_schema | varchar(63) | YES | original schema, at most 63 UTF-8 octets |
| 7 | relation_name | varchar(63) | YES | original name, at most 63 UTF-8 octets |
| 8 | relation_oid | oid | YES | original nonzero relation OID |
| 9 | relation_kind | varchar(1) | YES | r for every retained relation |
| 10 | owner_oid | oid | YES | original nonzero owner OID |
| 11 | owner_name | varchar(63) | YES | original role name, at most 63 UTF-8 octets |
| 12 | column_name | varchar(63) | YES | original column name, at most 63 UTF-8 octets |
| 13 | raw_acl_is_null | boolean | YES | mandatory on RELATION/COLUMN; SQL NULL is distinct from empty |
| 14 | raw_acl | aclitem[] | YES | native original ordered ACL with OIDs/dimensions |
| 15 | raw_acl_dimensions | text | YES | exact array_dims(raw_acl), including NULL for empty array |
| 16 | canonical_acl | jsonb | YES | closed ordered tuple array; [] not JSON null |
| 17 | identity_payload | jsonb | YES | closed kind-specific identity/non-ACL facts |
| 18 | delta_payload | jsonb | YES | closed temporary-grant inverse only on DELTA |
| 19 | canonical_bytes | bytea | NO | exact frame, maximum 8,388,608 octets |
| 20 | row_sha256 | bytea | NO | 32 octets, derived from row frame |
| 21 | aggregate_sha256 | bytea | YES | 32 octets on HEAD only |
| 22 | row_count | integer | YES | 1138 on HEAD only |
| 23 | byte_count | bigint | YES | actual sum of frame octets on HEAD, <=16,777,216 |
| 24 | installation_id | varchar(32) | NO | lowercase 32-hex UUID nonce, equal on all rows |

Native oid is a positive uint32 identity, represented as an int64 for resource
accounting. installation_id is exactly 32 ASCII hex octets, not a UUID spelling
with hyphens. Name fields additionally enforce octet_length<=63, not merely
63 Unicode characters. aclitem[] and oid receive explicit declared type
profiles; the generator must not infer them from suffixes.

Named constraints:

- pk_s4b_acl_snapshot: PRIMARY KEY(row_ordinal).
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_version: exact snapshot version.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_kind: exact five-kind enum.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_ordinal: row_ordinal BETWEEN 0 AND 1137.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_installation: installation_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_union: the complete closed arm matrix below, including
  every unused field IS NULL; no partial arm or arbitrary JSON object.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_raw: on RELATION/COLUMN, raw_acl_is_null equals
  (raw_acl IS NULL), and raw_acl_dimensions IS NOT DISTINCT FROM
  array_dims(raw_acl); native empty ACL remains non-NULL.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_frame: 1<=octet_length(canonical_bytes)<=8388608 and
  octet_length(row_sha256)=32.
- ck_s4b_acl_snapshot_head: aggregate/row_count/byte_count are present only on
  HEAD, aggregate is 32 octets, row_count=1138 and 1<=byte_count<=16777216.
- uq_s4b_acl_snapshot_relation: unique relation_ordinal WHERE row_kind='RELATION'.
- uq_s4b_acl_snapshot_column: unique(relation_ordinal,attribute_number)
  WHERE row_kind='COLUMN'.

No FK to a system catalog, user row, decision, signoff or external audit system.
No DELETE cascade. Cross-row identities/counts are independently validated
and sealed rather than implemented as an impossible aggregate CHECK.

| Kind | Ordinals/count | Mandatory payload / allowed identity fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HEAD | 0, count 1 | identity_payload; all relation/column/raw/canonical-ACL/delta fields NULL; aggregate/count summaries present |
| RELATION | 1..74, count 74 | relation_ordinal=ordinal; schema/name/OID/kind/owner; raw triple, canonical_acl, identity_payload; attribute/column/delta NULL |
| COLUMN | 75..1057, count 983 | same relation identity, original attribute_number/column_name; raw triple, canonical_acl, identity_payload; delta NULL |
| DELTA | 1058..1134, count 77 | relation identity and delta_payload; attribute/column only for the two column lock deltas; raw/canonical-ACL/identity_payload NULL |
| ROLE | 1135..1137, count 3 | identity_payload for trusted/runtime/login respectively; all relation/column/raw/canonical-ACL/delta fields NULL |

COLUMN order is allowlist relation order then original positive attnum. DELTA
order is the same 74 source SELECT obligations, UPDATE(id) on users then
organization_memberships, then event runtime INSERT/SELECT. ROLE order is
logical trusted, runtime, login. All 1,138 rows share one installation_id.
Exact row-kind counts, unique/full column identities, all cross-row equalities,
closed JSON payloads and seal are rechecked before every use.

### 3.3 Closed payload schemas and raw identity

HEAD identity_payload has exactly version, policyVersion, roleBindingVersion,
contractVersion, contractSha256, databaseIdentity, snapshotRelationIdentity,
migrationPrincipal, captureXid, retainedGlobalCatalog, preexistingRoleIdentities.
No self hash is included.

databaseIdentity has exactly systemIdentifier (decimal string), databaseOid
(integer), databaseNameAtCapture (string), encoding (UTF8), serverMajor (16).
systemIdentifier comes from pg_control_system(); an unavailable value refuses
capture, not a database-name fallback. databaseNameAtCapture is historical
metadata; database identity is systemIdentifier/databaseOid. A supported
database rename changes neither. Do not recompute role names from the current
database name.

snapshotRelationIdentity has schemaName="public", namespaceOid, relationName,
relationOid, relkind="r", ownerRoleId="s4b_trusted_owner". migrationPrincipal
has name and oid, matched to the actual administrative session. captureXid is
the PostgreSQL xid8 serialized as unsigned decimal. It binds all initial
capture steps to one transaction; it is not compared to a later downgrade XID.

retainedGlobalCatalog has exactly context, schema, functions from the existing
69-function 0029 extraction. Context separates identity observations (name,
connection/user/server-version observation) from retained schema facts.
All retained relation/column/constraint/index/trigger/function/schema facts and
owners/ACLs are preserved exactly. A deliberate database rename is not a
relation/schema rename and does not waive any of those facts. Fresh 0029
fixture validation remains byte-exact, including its context; no existing
source-catalog digest is normalized or rewritten.

preexistingRoleIdentities is the complete referenced role/membership closure,
sorted by name C: each record has name, oid, flags, memberships. flags are
login, superuser, createDb, createRole, inherit, replication, bypassRls,
connectionLimit, validUntil; memberships are roleName/memberName/grantorName/
adminOption/inheritOption/setOption sorted by the three names C. All referenced
existing grantors/grantees/owners and intervening roles are included. No password
or password hash is collected. Secret rotation is not a privilege identity;
all listed role flags/memberships remain exact. Unknown nonzero OIDs reject.

RELATION identity_payload has exactly namespaceOid and retainedFacts.
retainedFacts is the full old relation record excluding columns, owner,
explicitAcl/effectiveAcl and relationId/kind already represented explicitly;
all remaining facts/keys are kept, not selected opportunistically.
COLUMN identity_payload is the full old column record excluding its explicitAcl
and name/ordinal already represented explicitly. Its key inventory is the exact
per-column source-catalog schema. The snapshot schema expands those closed
inventories from independently reviewed constants, not from a live candidate.

canonical_acl uses the validated §2 form. Native raw_acl keeps all original
ACL OIDs and array dimensions; identity verification precedes name rendering
or canonicalization. A same-name recreated role cannot silently reinterpret
the native ACL or hash input.

DELTA payload has exactly id, scope, columns, requiredPrivileges, grantor,
grantee, addedTuples, inverse. IDs SRC-01..SRC-74, LOCK-01, LOCK-02,
EVENT-RUNTIME are fixed; scope RELATION/COLUMN; privileges SELECT, UPDATE or
[INSERT,SELECT] as appropriate; inverse is
REVOKE_ADDED_TUPLES_RESTRICT_BEFORE_OWNER_RESTORE.
Logical future roles resolve to the stored ROLE rows, never a user-supplied
name. addedTuples is the independently derived missing explicit-recipient
privilege set, with no added grant option. A source event owner SELECT already
present from any grantor is not regranted. An owner-revoked SELECT is recorded
and removed before owner restore. Original custom grants/options survive.

ROLE identity_payload has exactly logicalRoleId, name, oid, flags, memberships,
comment. logicalRoleId is the closed three-value enum. flags/memberships/comments
are exactly §4; no wildcard additional member. Raw credentials are not stored.
The JSON schema rejects duplicate keys/nonfinite numbers, unknown fields,
missing/extra/reordered rows and any unsupported policy or contract version.

### 3.4 Hash DAG and seal/immutability enforcement

For row r, construct native PostgreSQL JSONB of the ordered array of the first
18 declared fields plus installation_id: exactly 19 values. OIDs are explicitly
cast to bigint before JSON conversion; raw_acl is encoded as its ordered text[]
only after original OID-to-name verification. Other values retain SQL NULL
versus JSON structures. canonical_bytes is UTF8 of this JSONB's PostgreSQL-16
text representation. This is a new admin-only frame; it does not change the
portable decision canonicalizer. Independent SQL extraction recomputes it
from actual columns, never trusting the supplied canonical_bytes. The
independent checker also verifies the exact typed fields and raw ACL identities;
matching an opaque digest alone is insufficient.

~~~sql
row_sha256 = sha256(
  convert_to('paprnav-s4b-acl-snapshot-row-1','UTF8') || decode('00','hex')
  || int8send(octet_length(canonical_bytes)::bigint) || canonical_bytes
);
aggregate_sha256 = sha256(
  convert_to('paprnav-s4b-acl-snapshot-set-1','UTF8') || decode('00','hex')
  || int8send(1138::bigint)
  || string_agg(int4send(row_ordinal) || row_sha256,
                ''::bytea ORDER BY row_ordinal)
);
~~~

The derived five fields canonical_bytes, row_sha256, aggregate_sha256,
row_count and byte_count do not occur in the 19-value frame. HEAD is included
as one normal row hash, but its aggregate/count fields are excluded from its
frame: no self-hash fixed point. byte_count must equal the independently
computed sum of all 1,138 frame lengths. The fixed aggregate row-hash input
has 1,138×36=40,968 bytes before its domain/count, so it never aggregates the
whole payload again. No pgcrypto extension is required; PostgreSQL 16's native
sha256(bytea) was verified in the isolated probe.

Add public.paprnav_s4b_acl_snapshot_validate(), RETURNS trigger,
SECURITY DEFINER, LANGUAGE plpgsql, owner stored trusted role, search_path
exactly pg_catalog,public, all relation references qualified, PUBLIC/runtime/
login EXECUTE denied. It performs the complete closed shape/identity/count/
row-frame/hash/aggregate/bound checks above; it performs no writes.

Create trg_s4b_acl_snapshot_seal as a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint
trigger AFTER INSERT FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.row_kind='HEAD') calling that
function. Insert HEAD plus all rows in one capture transaction, then SET
CONSTRAINTS trg_s4b_acl_snapshot_seal IMMEDIATE and independently verify the
same full seal before any retained mutation. Install unconditional
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE row and BEFORE TRUNCATE statement triggers
using the existing reviewed paprnav_s4b_reject_mutation() function. The latter
already rejects mutations; its exact body must be verified to reject INSERT
as well, not silently special-case only its old event/table callers. No new
runtime-callable function is introduced for reading or resetting the seal.

The two immutability triggers are named trg_s4b_acl_snapshot_immutable_row and
trg_s4b_acl_snapshot_no_truncate. The complete table owner, raw ACL, column
ACLs, trigger event/timing/enablement/function bindings, function owner/body/
security/search_path/ACL and constraints/indexes are compared to the approved
contract before every snapshot consumption. Absence, disabled triggers,
rewritten body, changed owner or a self-consistent forged replacement is a
named failure. The snapshot's own stored relation OID must match the native
table; runtime cannot replace/reseal it.

Before every upgrade-finalization, downgrade preflight or restore comparison,
the administrative checker verifies native identity/ACL/trigger topology,
all 1,138 rows and seal from a fresh read under the locks. It never caches a
prior PASS across a transaction. The trigger's initial seal is not a perpetual
authorization token.

## 4. Exact per-database role namespace and lifecycle

### 4.1 Construction and collision policy

Hold the database-specific transaction advisory lock
pg_advisory_xact_lock(1395937794, (database_oid::bigint-2147483648)::integer).
The second argument is defined for every nonzero uint32 database OID.
Then generate at most eight candidate installation IDs with
replace(gen_random_uuid()::text,'-',''), lowercase exactly 32 hex characters.
This is PostgreSQL's UUID random nonce; do not describe it as 128 independent
random bits or replace it with a timestamp/name/hash suffix.

For unsigned OID d, let D=lpad(to_hex(d::bigint),8,'0'). Names are exactly:

~~~text
trusted: pn4b_t_ + D + _ + installation_id
runtime: pn4b_r_ + D + _ + installation_id
login:   pn4b_l_ + D + _ + installation_id
~~~

Each is 7+8+1+32=48 ASCII octets, below PostgreSQL's 63-octet limit.
Before the first CREATE/GRANT/ALTER, check all three candidate names absent in
pg_roles and all new 0030 object names absent. A pre-existing role is never
adopted, even with matching attributes/comment. A collision abandons that
candidate with no mutation and tries the next, up to eight. If none is free,
ACL_ROLE_NAMESPACE_EXHAUSTED. There is no truncation or overwrite.
The bound is eight read-only attempts, not unbounded retries.

After choosing a free triple, create all three in the enclosing transaction.
A concurrent external creator racing the check causes ACL_ROLE_CREATE_RACE
and rollback of the whole attempt; no partial adoption or automatic in-place
repair. A subsequent explicit retry starts from a verified 0029 state with a
new nonce. Ordinary same-database migrations are serialized by the advisory
lock. Different databases have distinct D values and can upgrade independently.

### 4.2 Exact attributes, memberships and comments

| Logical ID | LOGIN | INHERIT | Other flags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| s4b_trusted_owner | false | false | NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS |
| s4b_runtime | false | false | same |
| s4b_login | true | true | same |

All three have CONNECTION LIMIT -1, VALID UNTIL null, no role GUC settings,
security labels or unlisted memberships. Creation uses PASSWORD NULL; a
login credential may later be rotated through the existing credential
administration path without changing these identity/privilege flags. Neither
password bytes nor their hash are snapshot authority. The two NOLOGIN roles
remain NOLOGIN regardless of credentials.

Exactly one membership edge exists involving these roles:
GRANT runtime TO login WITH ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT TRUE, SET TRUE, grantor the
recorded administrative session. There is no trusted-owner membership, no
runtime-to-login reverse edge, no migration-principal membership granted to
applications, and no GRANT runtime TO CURRENT_USER. The administrative executor
already has its trusted DDL authority; an extra cluster membership is needless.
Validate both incoming and outgoing pg_auth_members edges for all three OIDs.

Each role comment is exactly:
"paprnav/s4b/role-1 " followed by PostgreSQL-16 JSONB text of the object with
keys version, systemIdentifier, databaseOid, installationId, logicalRoleId.
version is paprnav-ad-v4-database-role-binding-1; identity values match HEAD.
Store the exact comment in the ROLE row and independently reconstruct it.
The comment contains no aggregate or own hash, avoiding a circular seal.
A comment is a cross-check, not the trust root or permission to adopt a role.

The actual allocated name and OID are captured after CREATE ROLE and before
retained ACL mutation. All authority tables/functions use stored trusted role,
runtime ACL grants use stored runtime role and login tests use stored login.
The snapshot role resolver is administrative only; deployed application
connection configuration receives its exact role name during deployment,
not through a new API read of the private table. All consumers must reject
unresolved logical roles and hardcoded unqualified s4b_* SQL names.

PostgreSQL roles are cluster-wide, so using a globally fixed name for a
database-owned role is insufficient. The reviewed per-database identity
prevents a second database from taking or dropping the first's roles.
[PostgreSQL CREATE ROLE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-createrole.html)

### 4.3 Rename, reuse, restore and cross-database behavior

| Event | Exact behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Database rename | Accept same systemIdentifier/databaseOid; use stored names/OIDs/nonce; databaseNameAtCapture remains historical. No role rename/recomputation. |
| Database dropped and its OID later reused | A new 0029 database has no snapshot and selects a fresh nonce; existing names are never adopted. Orphan roles from the old installation are not automatically removed. |
| Role renamed, dropped/recreated or same-name/new-OID | Refuse ACL_ROLE_IDENTITY_CHANGED; matching comment/name/privileges cannot override stored OID. |
| Role OID reused for a differently named role | Refuse name/OID/comment/installation mismatch; never match only numeric OID. |
| Trusted-role flags, memberships, comment, GUCs or labels drift | Refuse ACL_ROLE_TOPOLOGY_CHANGED before restoration or role cleanup. |
| Complete physical cluster restore preserving system ID, database/role/relation OIDs and bytes | Treat as the same database lineage; verify every seal/topology/native identity before use. No new role allocation. |
| Logical pg_dump restore, CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE from a 0030 database, or cross-cluster import with changed OIDs | Refuse ACL_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE_IDENTITY_CHANGED or ACL_IDENTITY_CHANGED; no rebinding/rehashing. Start a second database from fresh 0029 and upgrade normally. A supported logical-restore migration needs a separate reviewed version. |
| A then B upgrades | Distinct three-role installations and private snapshots; both usable. |
| A downgrades while B remains | Remove only A's exact objects/grants/roles; B unchanged. Same in reverse order. |
| Foreign database owns/grants something to A's role | Refuse ACL_ROLE_FOREIGN_DEPENDENCY, roll back; never DROP OWNED/CASCADE in that database or drop a shared role. |
| Name collision across installation attempts | Eight read-only candidates; then refusal, no arbitrary suffix or adoption. |

Before role cleanup inspect pg_shdepend for each stored OID, including shared
dependencies (dbid=0) and every foreign database, and pg_auth_members for all
edges. Only this installation's enumerated local dependencies and its one
membership edge are allowed. A foreign dependency is a policy violation, not a
signal to delete foreign objects. Do not scan or mutate each database to
“repair” it. DROP ROLE performs a final native dependency check inside the
transaction, covering a race after the precheck; its refusal rolls back
local table/role cleanup too.
[PostgreSQL shared dependencies](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/catalog-pg-shdepend.html)

Never use DROP OWNED as broad cleanup. Revoke exact temporary grants and remove
exact owned objects; require zero residual unapproved dependency, then drop
login, runtime and trusted roles by their verified stored identities. No
existing role or other installation's role is dropped. DB OID/name reuse
cannot select a prior installation because the current snapshot nonce and
stored triple, not a prefix search, are the authority.

## 5. Bounded capture and resource accounting

Closed capture size is 1+74+983+77+3=1,138 rows. Select scalar counts and byte
length upper bounds before fetching ACL arrays, role closures or function/
catalog text. Validate every existing object identity against the approved
closed source selection, with no name wildcard. Administrative bounds:

| Parameter | Inclusive ceiling |
| --- | ---: |
| Total canonical snapshot frames B | 16,777,216 octets |
| Any one canonical row frame | 8,388,608 octets |
| Any one raw ACL's canonical/text payload | 1,048,576 octets |
| Total exploded relation+column ACL tuples | 65,536 |
| Pre-existing participating roles including membership closure | 4,096 |
| JSON nesting depth | 16 |
| Total JSON tree nodes in snapshot payloads | 131,072 |
| Administrative work W_admin | 67,108,864 octets |

A deployment above a bound refuses before retained mutation. It is not
“normalized” into a smaller ACL or missing role chain. These limits preserve
arbitrary compatible grants within an explicit admitted envelope rather than
assuming default ACLs. Capture streams at most one bounded row; use scalar
native array cardinality/length metadata to reject oversized ACLs before
client-side serialization. Oversized server metadata may be inspected for
length on the server, but its payload must not be fetched first.

Define N=1138 and W_admin=3*B + 128*N + 65536. The 3B term charges captured
payload/frame/verification material, 128N row/index/hash metadata, and 65536
stream reserve. The maximum B yields 50,542,848 work octets. The explicit
64-MiB cap remains a fail-closed independent check; it does not promise RSS or
permit B to exceed 16 MiB. At downgrade the bounded transaction-local copy
needed for read-before-drop is included in 3B, not silently free memory.
No acceptance pending-copy record is created for audit rows.

Resource successor has 90 registered families/1,663 declared fields:
the old 89/1,639 decision families/fields plus this 1/24 admin family.
The three decision phase ledgers still contain exactly the old 89 families
and identical W_decision formula/caps. Add a distinct migration_capture/
migration_restore administrative ledger with this one family. No per-decision
loading/charging of all database audit rows. Resource output declarations
distinguish graph families=9/201 from total persistence families=10/225;
a field is not omitted just because it is outside a decision ledger.

The independent resource crosswalk must explicitly prove this family has no
mapping AST source, pending allocation, API serializer or historical decision
read path. Its new fields, OID/native-ACL encodings, row-count/frame limits and
ledger scope are independently checked. Existing 2,416 resource mutations
remain; add exactly 64 named mutations: 24 field omissions, 24 wrong field
type/nullability/encoding declarations, eight scalar-cap changes (the eight
rows above), three decision-phase contamination cases, admin family missing,
duplicate, wrong row count, wrong W_admin coefficients, and wrong no-pending
classification. Total resource mutation count/kills required is 2,480,
zero generic/wrong-code/survivor kills. Positive cap-equality tests are recorded
separately, not disguised as mutations.

## 6. Single-transaction upgrade/downgrade and crash table

### 6.1 Framework contract before any DDL

Use PostgreSQL 16, one driver connection and one explicit outer transaction.
The later administrative runner is scripts/migrate-s4b-with-acl-audit.py and
helper backend/app/db/migrations/acl_audit.py. They require a normal supported
psycopg transaction, autocommit=false, and an already begun outer transaction.
Alembic env.py must honor config.attributes["connection"], configure
transactional_ddl=true, and must not create another engine/connection or
commit per operation. Crossing 0029↔0030 in offline mode, a raw unguarded
Alembic path or an autocommit path refuses ACL_TRANSACTION_CONTEXT_REQUIRED.

Before role/table mutation verify driver transaction state and
pg_current_xact_id(); verify the same XID at every phase and after Alembic's
revision update but before outer commit. No autocommit_block, intermediate
COMMIT/ROLLBACK, transaction control in generated SQL, CREATE INDEX
CONCURRENTLY, separate capture connection or two-phase PREPARE TRANSACTION.
A static review and named fault tests prove the code honors the contract;
a final XID comparison alone cannot undo an earlier accidental commit.

The repository's current env.py always makes its own connection. It is not
already compliant. A later authorized implementation must make that bounded
change and test the actual command used by docker compose run --rm migrate.
The database table, unlike a local receipt, survives the ephemeral container.

### 6.2 Upgrade order

1. Verify revision 0029/no current snapshot/no new 0030 objects, source profile,
   trusted administrative session and transaction contract. Acquire the
   per-database advisory transaction lock. Lock all 74 retained tables ACCESS
   EXCLUSIVE in schema/name C order with lock_timeout=5s; require no concurrent
   administrative role/function/schema DDL in the controlled migration window.
2. Verify non-ACL source shape/owner profile; all original source owners remain
   paprnav_user for this supported version. Existing event PUBLIC privileges
   remain unsupported by its PUBLIC=[] authority boundary; other retained
   sources may have PUBLIC SELECT but not PUBLIC mutation privileges. Preserve
   all compatible named-role grant chains/options/column ACLs. Schema PUBLIC
   CREATE must already be false; never rewrite its raw ACL to achieve that.
3. Bound/capture source facts, select the collision-free nonce/triple and create
   roles. Create snapshot table and its seal function/trigger, initialize exact
   new-object ACL/owner, compute all rows/deltas and insert them. Seal, verify,
   install immutability triggers and independently read/verify the complete
   table. No retained ACL/owner/function mutation precedes this point.
4. Execute the unchanged additive 0030 graph/event/gate work, with roles resolved
   from the sealed snapshot. Initialize only new-object ACLs. Preserve old
   custom ACLs; never blanket REVOKE ALL on an existing relation/schema/function.
   Transfer event ownership explicitly and add only recorded temporary grants.
5. Compare exact installed 0030 DDL/ACL/role transform, old-binary compatibility
   and source preservation against the snapshot; reverify snapshot seal and
   topology. Alembic updates its revision row on this same transaction.
6. Validate revision=0030, unchanged transaction XID, eight new tables including
   valid audit snapshot, default-disabled gate and all exact role identities.
   Commit once. Any exception rolls back roles, comments, table, rows, grants,
   owner changes, functions and revision together.

### 6.3 Downgrade order: read and verify before drop

1. Enter the same transaction contract; lock advisory key and all 82 tables
   (74 retained + eight new) ACCESS EXCLUSIVE in schema/name C order, timeout
   5s. Verify both application/database gates false, the seven acceptance/
   sentinel tables empty, no acceptance event and no unsealed sentinel.
   The snapshot must be complete, not empty.
2. Resolve the snapshot native OID; fully verify owner/ACL/triggers/functions,
   rows/seal/versions/database identity and all three ROLE identities. Reject
   foreign/unexpected role dependencies. Copy its validated expected facts
   into the bounded transaction-local verifier memory under the held locks.
   This ephemeral copy is not external authority and cannot outlive/restart
   the transaction. Every later use derives from that verified read.
3. Verify the actual installed 0030 transform. Reverse exact temporary grants
   using the recorded original/trusted grantor contexts and RESTRICT. Remove
   any added owner SELECT on the event before returning ownership, preserving
   owner-revoked and arbitrary delegated grants. Do not rely on DROP OWNED.
4. Restore exact old event columns/checks/indexes/triggers/functions/gates,
   remove the seven new acceptance/sentinel tables and their new functions
   except the snapshot-only verifier machinery still needed. Compare all
   retained facts using §2 while snapshot and roles are still present.
   Reverify the snapshot immediately before its last consumption/drop.
5. Drop only the snapshot table (its own triggers/constraint/indexes disappear),
   then its dedicated seal function. Revoke the one introduced membership;
   recheck residual shared/foreign dependencies; DROP login, runtime, trusted.
   Native dependency failure aborts the entire transaction, restoring the
   snapshot and all prior 0030 state.
6. Alembic sets revision 0029 in the same transaction. Using the already verified
   in-transaction copy, perform final exact retained catalog/data/role comparison,
   confirm all eight new tables/functions/three stored role identities absent,
   and record actual raw ACL differences only as §2 permits. Commit once.
   Do not read a dropped table or silently recapture an alleged 0029 baseline.

No downgrade deletes acceptance history to become eligible. Logical disable
keeps 0030-aware readers. A later upgrade after successful downgrade captures
the current explicit ACLs as non-NULL; it cannot reuse the prior NULL exception.

### 6.4 Why no external uncertain state exists

PostgreSQL transactional DDL/shared-role catalogs/private audit rows and the
Alembic revision commit as one database transaction. SQL session or container
loss before commit rolls them back; a successful commit makes all visible.
A client may not know whether COMMIT succeeded, but it does not manufacture
another authoritative PREPARED/UNCERTAIN receipt. Reconnect, acquire the lock,
and classify native state before retry:

| Observed state after reconnect | Required action |
| --- | --- |
| revision 0029, exact retained shape, no new 0030 table/snapshot | Upgrade was rolled back or downgrade committed; new upgrade may begin with a fresh nonce after normal preflight. Do not delete orphan roles by prefix. |
| revision 0030, complete sealed snapshot, exact installed objects/roles | Upgrade committed or downgrade rolled back; do not recreate roles/snapshot. Verify and resume ordinary operation or explicitly retry downgrade. |
| snapshot/objects inconsistent with revision, partial row set, wrong seal/identity | ACL_TRANSACTION_STATE_INCONSISTENT; no retry/repair/rebind. Preserve evidence for independent recovery. |
| locks still held by a live/uncertain session | Bounded lock timeout; no competing write or compensating cleanup. |
| caller tries to continue in failed/aborted connection | Roll back/close; re-enter through the full state classifier. |
| autocommit/connection/XID invariant fails before mutation | Refuse; no state change. If code violated it despite guard, classify as inconsistent and block; never call partial state an approved 0030 installation. |

Crash after initial capture, after role creation, during ACL changes, or during
snapshot drop has only transaction rollback/commit outcomes. A role/table
created by a different trusted administrator is not ours; normal role collision/
dependency rules still apply. Operational PostgreSQL durability/backup policy
remains the existing database deployment responsibility; this proposal adds
no undefined filesystem fsync/provider/signing dependency.

## 2. Canonical ACL and raw equality contract

### 2.1 PostgreSQL semantics and closed object-kind mapping

The relation default is selected by ACL object kind, not by passing relkind
through blindly. Use this exact mapping:

| pg_class.relkind | Object | acldefault kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| r, p, v, m, f | ordinary/partitioned table, view, materialized view, foreign table | r |
| S | sequence | s (lowercase) |
| i, I, t, c and every unlisted value | not a retained relation ACL object | reject |

The 74 retained relations are all r. Supporting canonicalization of the other
listed kinds does not add them to the rollback exception. Columns use c;
NULL column ACL has an empty column-specific default. PUBLIC is grantee OID 0.
aclexplode supplies grantor, grantee, privilege and grantability. Uppercase S
is an ACL kind for a foreign server, not a sequence. These are PostgreSQL 16
API facts. [PostgreSQL ACL functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/functions-info.html)

Owners can revoke their own ordinary privileges while retaining ownership's
implicit grant authority. Therefore an explicit empty ACL is not equivalent
to a NULL ACL. Stored is_grantable must not be replaced with an inference from
ownership or effective role membership.
[PostgreSQL privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/ddl-priv.html)

### 2.2 Exact representation

For each retained relation, record separately:

1. Relation identity (schema/name/relkind), owner principal, and same-cluster
   relation OID plus owner OID in the deployment identity sidecar.
2. rawAcl: either null, or a closed object with arrayDims (the exact
   array_dims text, possibly null for an empty array), cardinality, and entries
   (native ACL text items in their original array-subscript order). Preserve
   SQL NULL versus an empty array and preserve entry order/lower bounds.
3. canonicalAcl: an ordered array of the closed tuple objects below, obtained
   from aclexplode(COALESCE(relacl, acldefault(kind, relowner))). Do not expand
   role inheritance, infer implicit owner grant options, group grantors, merge
   privileges, or use has_table_privilege as this oracle.
4. Every retained column's raw attacl, column-specific canonical tuples and
   identity attnum/name. Do not fold relation privileges into the column ACL.
5. All retained non-ACL catalog fields, definitions and row-validity evidence
   in the same complete scope as the approved 0029 physical snapshot.

Principal shape is a discriminated union, never an ambiguous role-name string:

~~~json
{
  "grantor": {"kind": "ROLE", "name": "paprnav_user"},
  "grantee": {"kind": "PUBLIC", "name": null},
  "privilege": "SELECT",
  "isGrantable": false
}
~~~

A real quoted role named PUBLIC is {"kind":"ROLE","name":"PUBLIC"}, not the
pseudo-role. Grantor and owner must be existing nonzero role OIDs; grantee is
either zero/PUBLIC or an existing role. Resolve with LEFT JOIN pg_roles and
reject unresolved nonzero OIDs as ACL_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN before serialization.
Never silently emit pg_get_userbyid's unknown-role display, omit the row through
an inner join, or translate it to PUBLIC. Reject grantor zero separately.

Tuple order is ascending by (PUBLIC=0/ROLE=1 grantee rank, grantee name with
PUBLIC's sort name "", grantor role name, privilege, isGrantable false before
true). Every text sort uses COLLATE "C"/UTF-8 byte ordering. Allowed privilege
strings are exactly DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE,
UPDATE for table-like relations; SELECT, UPDATE, USAGE for sequences; INSERT,
REFERENCES, SELECT, UPDATE for columns. Reject any unknown privilege. Retain
all distinct grantors. Duplicate identical exploded tuples are rejected, not
silently DISTINCTed. Empty results serialize as [], never null.

Role names enter portable canonical comparison. Raw OIDs never enter portable
fresh-cluster goldens. Within a deployment's pre/installed/post sequence,
the separately recorded name↔OID map must remain one-to-one and identical for
every pre-existing participating role and retained relation. A dropped/recreated
role with the same name, rename or recreated relation fails
ACL_IDENTITY_CHANGED even if its portable tuples match. A retained relation's
switch between two existing, correctly resolved owner principals instead
fails ACL_OWNER_CHANGED; the ownerOid association is checked at that stage,
not misreported as a role name-to-OID substitution. The newly
created three s4b roles are explicitly absent before, exact while installed,
and absent after. Their OIDs are installation-specific audit facts.

Raw equality means native catalog-value equality, including ordered ACL array
items and dimensions, not disk-page/WAL equality. It does not require OIDs to
match between separately initialized databases. Snapshot extraction must prove
that its lossless raw representation round-trips to the native aclitem[] under
the verified same-cluster role identities. Do not sort raw ACL arrays.

### 2.3 Concrete independent extraction/comparison sketch

The following is pseudo-SQL: :selected_oids is already resolved from the
closed ordered relation registry; validation assertions run before aggregation.

~~~sql
WITH objects AS (
  SELECT c.oid, n.nspname, c.relname, c.relkind, c.relowner, c.relacl,
         CASE WHEN c.relkind IN ('r','p','v','m','f') THEN 'r'::"char"
              WHEN c.relkind = 'S' THEN 's'::"char"
              ELSE NULL END AS acl_kind
  FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
  WHERE c.oid = ANY(:selected_oids)
), expanded AS (
  SELECT o.*, x.grantor, x.grantee, x.privilege_type, x.is_grantable,
         own.rolname AS owner_name, gtor.rolname AS grantor_name,
         gtee.rolname AS grantee_name
  FROM objects o
  JOIN pg_roles own ON own.oid = o.relowner
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL aclexplode(
    COALESCE(o.relacl, acldefault(o.acl_kind, o.relowner))) x
  LEFT JOIN pg_roles gtor ON gtor.oid = x.grantor
  LEFT JOIN pg_roles gtee ON gtee.oid = x.grantee
)
SELECT oid, grantor_name,
       CASE WHEN grantee=0 THEN 'PUBLIC' ELSE 'ROLE' END AS grantee_kind,
       CASE WHEN grantee=0 THEN NULL ELSE grantee_name END AS grantee_name,
       privilege_type, is_grantable
FROM expanded
ORDER BY oid,
         CASE WHEN grantee=0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
         COALESCE(grantee_name,'') COLLATE "C",
         grantor_name COLLATE "C", privilege_type COLLATE "C", is_grantable;
~~~

Before the JOIN owner above, independently anti-join the objects to pg_roles;
before aclexplode, reject a null acl_kind. Assert exact object coverage outside
the expanded rows, because empty ACLs produce zero rows. The outer assembler
initializes [] for every object, then appends validated tuples. Role checks
must not depend on a successful expansion of a nonempty ACL. The parallel
column query uses COALESCE(a.attacl, acldefault('c',c.relowner)); attnum>0,
NOT attisdropped, and the complete 983-column inventory. Native comparison
for the special case is exactly:

~~~sql
pre.relacl IS NULL
AND post.relacl IS NOT NULL
AND post.relacl IS NOT DISTINCT FROM acldefault('r'::"char", pre.relowner)
~~~

The surrounding identity, owner, canonical, non-ACL and allowlist checks are
mandatory; the SQL expression alone is not the policy. Default privileges
configured for future object creation are not consulted to reinterpret an
existing NULL relacl. Do not substitute pg_default_acl or today's grants for
the captured baseline. The historical field named effectiveAcl remains
unchanged in the old catalog; the new audit representation is named
canonicalAcl because it is deliberately not an effective-permission closure.

## 3. Raw rollback exception and complete allowlist

Apply checks in this order: snapshot/identity/schema validity; retained
non-ACL equality; owner/role identity; all raw column/schema/function ACL
equalities; canonical relation equality; raw relation equality/exception.
The result contains both actual raw digests and ordered exception records;
never substitute the old digest for a changed raw catalog.

| Pre raw ACL | Post raw ACL | Canonical/owner/non-ACL facts | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NULL | NULL | exact | RAW_EXACT |
| NULL | exact native original-owner default on an allowlisted r relation | exact | NULL_TO_EXACT_OWNER_DEFAULT |
| explicit owner default | identical explicit owner default | exact | RAW_EXACT |
| explicit empty or owner privilege revoked | identical original explicit ACL | exact | RAW_EXACT |
| arbitrary explicit grants/options/delegations | identical original ordered ACL | exact | RAW_EXACT |
| NULL | owner default plus any extra/zero-privilege ACL entry | any | reject |
| NULL | owner default missing any privilege | changed | reject |
| NULL | default with changed grantor, grantee or grant option | changed | reject |
| non-NULL | reordered/equivalent different representation, NULL, or changed dimensions | even equal tuples | reject |
| any | any owner, column ACL, schema ACL, function ACL or non-ACL change | changed | reject |
| NULL outside the allowlist, or any non-r relation | explicit default | even equal tuples | reject |

“Missing owner privilege” refers to a privilege lost from the pre-state/default,
not a rule that overwrites a pre-existing explicit owner revocation. Neither
an explicit empty ACL nor a default-plus-custom ACL can take the exception.

The exact ordered exception allowlist is the existing trustedSourcePrivileges
selectRelations tuple. It is a standalone literal in the successor leaf and
checker, not learned from a candidate snapshot. minItems=maxItems=74,
uniqueItems=true and 74 prefixItems const values. All observed kinds are r.

## 4. Snapshot, migration and validation algorithm

### 4.1 Verified external audit snapshot; no new SQL authority

P06 already requires a verified pre-upgrade snapshot. Make its format and
lifecycle concrete as paprnav-ad-v4-persistence-rollback-snapshot-1, validated
by acceptance-persistence-rollback-snapshot-v1.schema.json. It is deployment
audit evidence, outside the database, not a source of application semantics,
an extra persistence table, a table comment, or an acceptance row.

Exact root keys, in serialized order, are version, policyVersion, deploymentId,
databaseIdentity, migrationFrom, migrationTo, contractVersion, contractSha256,
capturedPhase, relationOrder, roleIdentities, relationIdentities,
retainedCatalog, aclRecords, plannedAclDeltas. Objects are closed at every
level. Constants: version as above; policyVersion
paprnav-ad-v4-persistence-acl-rollback-1; migrationFrom=20260913_0029;
migrationTo=20260916_0030; contractVersion=paprnav-ad-v4-acceptance-persistence-2;
capturedPhase=PRE_UPGRADE_LOCKED. The snapshot contains no own digest.

- deploymentId is an externally assigned immutable deployment UUID, not a
  value accepted merely because the snapshot asserts it.
- databaseIdentity has exactly systemIdentifier, databaseOid, databaseName,
  serverVersionNum, encoding, collation, ctype. Read systemIdentifier from
  pg_control_system().system_identifier with authorized read access. Failure
  to obtain it is ACL_AUDIT_CLUSTER_ID_UNAVAILABLE, not a database-name fallback.
  Do not grant broad superuser permission to work around it.
- relationOrder is the exact 74 tuple; retainedCatalog has the complete closed
  shape of the old physical catalog (all non-ACL fields retained). Existing
  physical ACLs are baseline values, not copied from a fresh fixture.
- roleIdentities is sorted by role name C, with unique oid/name pairs for all
  owners/grantors/non-PUBLIC grantees in captured objects, database/schema
  owners, migration principal and membership principals involved in the
  deployment profile. Include their role flags and relevant exact membership
  edges with grantor/admin/inherit/set flags. No password/verifier material.
  Each role record has exactly name, oid, flags, memberships. flags has exactly
  login, superuser, createDb, createRole, inherit, replication, bypassRls (all
  booleans), connectionLimit (integer), validUntil (canonical timestamp or
  null). memberships lists edges whose member is this role, each record exactly
  roleName, memberName, grantorName, adminOption, inheritOption, setOption;
  sort by roleName/memberName/grantorName C. Resolve every principal to the same
  roleIdentities map, reject duplicate edges, and include the transitive role
  closure rather than omitting an intervening membership or grantor.
- relationIdentities is the exact 74 tuple of relationId/oid/ownerOid.
- aclRecords is the same 74 tuple; each entry has relationId, owner, rawAcl,
  canonicalAcl, columns. columns is the exact per-relation attnum/name list,
  each with rawAcl/canonicalAcl. No missing empty ACLs, duplicate columns,
  unknown keys or inferred names.
- plannedAclDeltas is a closed tuple of 77 entries: 74 source SELECT
  obligations, the two UPDATE(id) lock obligations (users then
  organization_memberships), then the event runtime SELECT/INSERT obligation.
  Each entry declares relation/column scope, before owner/ACL facts, exact
  intended temporary grant delta, grantor, grantee, grant option false, and
  inverse; no arbitrary SQL text. A source obligation already satisfied by
  the post-owner-transfer canonical ACL has an empty delta, not another grant.
  These 77 semantic records are not 77 file/hash authority occurrences.

Each plannedAclDeltas record has exactly id, relationId, scope, columns,
requiredPrivileges, grantor, grantee, addedTuples, inverse. IDs are SRC-01
through SRC-74 in relation order, LOCK-01, LOCK-02, EVENT-RUNTIME. scope is
RELATION or COLUMN; columns is [] or exactly ["id"]; requiredPrivileges is
["SELECT"], ["UPDATE"] or ["INSERT","SELECT"] respectively. grantor/grantee
use the principal shape in §2. addedTuples has only independently derived
missing explicit recipient privileges, each isGrantable=false; an already
present privilege from any grantor satisfies an owner obligation without
resetting its grant option. PUBLIC SELECT does not remove the separately
declared explicit trusted-recipient grant obligation on non-event sources.
inverse is the constant REVOKE_ADDED_TUPLES_RESTRICT_BEFORE_OWNER_RESTORE.
The event owner relabeling is the one fixed deployment-policy operation,
not an arbitrary instruction added to this grant tuple. The reader independently
recomputes all 77 records and rejects any mismatch before executing SQL.
Only the three declared future s4b role names may appear in planned deltas
without a pre-upgrade roleIdentities entry. Existing ACL records cannot use
that exception. The deployment receipt records their actual allocated OIDs
after creation and binds them through the installed/downgrade sequence.

Schema strings/enums/digests are closed or constrained as appropriate, all
required fields present, integer OIDs positive except PUBLIC, bounded arrays
by the approved catalog shape, exactly 74/983 relation/column identities.
Arbitrary role names and existing grant chains cannot be a schema const;
independent semantic checks require exact lossless catalog correspondence,
valid privilege sets/order and the supported security profile. Reject duplicate
JSON keys/nonfinite JSON/malformed UTF-8 before Draft202012 validation.
The schema declares a digest format, not a fabricated current contract hash:
the reader compares contractSha256 to the separately approved subject bytes.

The trusted deployment change-control record pins the exact snapshot SHA-256,
deployment/database identity, new contract/checker hashes and approved
migration subject before commit. The same record is supplied independently
during downgrade. A digest stored next to an untrusted file is not sufficient
authority. Use a regular no-symlink exclusive-create artifact, flush and
read-back verify, and retain it append-only. Publication failure rolls back
the SQL transaction. A snapshot published before a failed/uncertain commit
is retained as PREPARED/NOT_CONFIRMED in a separate append-only deployment
receipt; never rewrite the snapshot to say COMMITTED. Reconcile actual revision,
contract and installed catalog before retry. Do not assume atomic commit
between a filesystem and PostgreSQL.

The snapshot is required for the actual deployment from which it was captured.
Missing, stale, cross-database or altered evidence refuses downgrade. Never
fall back to the clean fixture, a current post-upgrade snapshot, v1 policy or
a wildcard path. SHA-256 is content binding, not operator identity or approval.

### 4.2 Preconditions and supported topology

Before any mutating DDL/grant:

1. Verify reviewed successor contract, snapshot schema, migration/program and
   out-of-band deployment binding. Require PostgreSQL major 16, exact installed
   revision 0029, supported owner profile and no s4b_trusted_owner/s4b_runtime/
   s4b_login role or 0030 object already present.
2. The approved profile remains paprnav_user owning all 74 source relations,
   including the event relation. Alternate owners are not silently supported:
   ACL_DEPLOYMENT_OWNER_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED before mutation. This preserves
   P05's existing requirement for review of deployment role differences.
   A future alternate-owner profile needs a versioned independent design,
   including role-name/OID and inverse ownership tests.
3. Preserve arbitrary explicit ACLs and grant chains of pre-existing named
   roles within this profile, including owner-revoked/empty ACLs. Pre-existing
   roles cannot already include the absent s4b roles. Do not replace their
   grants with the clean fixture. Existing event PUBLIC privileges are forbidden
   by its approved PUBLIC=[] boundary; any such pre-state fails
   ACL_PUBLIC_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITION. On the other 73 sources, PUBLIC table/
   column SELECT is compatible; PUBLIC non-SELECT privileges are rejected as
   ACL_PUBLIC_SOURCE_PRECONDITION. This refuses a security-incompatible
   deployment unchanged; it does not revoke or erase its ACL.
4. Public schema CREATE must already be false for PUBLIC; retain its entire
   raw nspacl unchanged. Granting/revoking CREATE merely to materialize a NULL
   schema ACL is forbidden. New roles must have only the approved memberships,
   no CREATEROLE/CREATEDB/superuser/BYPASSRLS/ownership/DDL/sequence escape.
   Actual runtime probes, including inherited/PUBLIC access, remain mandatory.
5. Obtain an operator-controlled exclusive migration/role-DDL maintenance
   window and the bounded locks below. Runtime never gets role-DDL powers.
   PostgreSQL table locks do not protect against an uncooperative superuser
   changing cluster roles; do not claim otherwise. If this precondition cannot
   be established, fail deployment, not the ACL comparator.

### 4.3 Upgrade and precise inverse

A later production implementation shall add scripts/migrate-s4b-with-acl-audit.py
and backend/app/db/migrations/acl_audit.py, and minimally adapt Alembic env.py to
honor an explicitly supplied already-open connection/outer transaction.
Ordinary migrations keep their existing path. Crossing 0029↔0030 without the
validated wrapper context fails ACL_AUDIT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED; offline SQL-only
execution is not a supported bypass. These are later production changes, not
design F entries or current edit authorization.

Wrapper upgrade starts an outer transaction, applies lock_timeout=5s, acquires
ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on all 74 retained relations in schema/name C order, verifies
preconditions, captures and publishes the snapshot under those locks, then runs
the exact Alembic upgrade through that same connection. New tables acquire
their normal DDL locks. No before-snapshot privilege change is permitted.

Create the same seven new relations/functions and disabled gate. New objects
may be initialized to their exact approved ACLs, removing creation-default
extras on those new objects only; do not alter pg_default_acl. Transfer event
ownership explicitly to s4b_trusted_owner, preserving/relabeling original owner
grantor/grantee entries through PostgreSQL's ownership operation. For each
source privilege, inspect the projected original ACL: add only the missing
temporary obligation, with exact grantor and no grant option. On the event,
do not GRANT owner SELECT if it already exists. Add runtime SELECT/INSERT as
declared. Do not execute REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC on the existing event; its
preflight already proved the approved empty PUBLIC ACL. Do not touch existing
schema ACL or frozen function ACLs.

The owner-revoked event is a mandatory counterexample: transferring ownership,
granting SELECT to the new owner, then transferring ownership back can carry
that newly added owner SELECT back to paprnav_user. DROP OWNED by the departed
trusted role alone does not identify that delta. Record and reverse the exact
added owner SELECT under the trusted owner before transferring ownership back.
If baseline owner SELECT was absent, revoke only the newly added SELECT using
the recorded grantor and RESTRICT, retaining any pre-existing owner grant
options and grants made by other grantors. If SELECT was originally present,
the inverse performs no owner SELECT revoke. Never replace the entire ACL.
PostgreSQL REVOKE's grantor/dependency behavior makes explicit delta tracking
and RESTRICT essential. [PostgreSQL REVOKE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-revoke.html)

Independently extract installed 0030 catalog and verify the exact declared
DDL/owner/temporary-ACL transformation from the snapshot, including each grantor,
option, untouched ACL item order, columns and full non-ACL delta. Derive expected
tuples independently from captured original facts and the closed delta program;
do not compare only permission booleans or trust migration-generated output.
For NULL origins the upgrade's exact materialization plus temporary grants is
declared, not treated as the downgrade exception. Every explicit old ACL item
must survive with only the explicit reversible owner relabeling. Verify
privilege topology using a real runtime login. Alembic's revision update
occurs before the wrapper's final comparison/outer commit.

Execute each added grant and inverse revoke in its precise owner/grantor
context using authorized SET LOCAL ROLE and safely quoted identifiers, then
restore the wrapper's migration context. This involves only the recorded
original owner and the new trusted owner, never assuming arbitrary existing
delegate roles. Preflight legal ability to use those contexts; otherwise fail
ACL_GRANTOR_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE. Do not add persistent trusted-owner membership
to runtime/login or rely on PostgreSQL choosing an unspecified grantor. The
independent installed comparison verifies the actual recorded grantor.

Downgrade uses the matching immutable pre-upgrade snapshot. Under the same
outer transaction and 5s bound, lock all 81 current relations (74 retained
plus seven new) in schema/name C order, table-first before row checks.
Require independently observed application gate false and database gate false,
all seven new relations empty, no acceptance event and no unsealed sentinel.
Require installed catalog/ACLs to equal the exact expected 0030 transform,
not merely to have revision 0030. Unexpected administrative grants, changed
roles/owners or data refuse downgrade without resetting them.

Restore exactly the declared legacy event/check/index/trigger/function/gate
DDL and column order. Reverse temporary ACL deltas while their recorded
grantor/owner context still exists; reverse the owner delta before event
ownership returns. Remove runtime and trusted-source temporary grants with
RESTRICT, including only the two temporary column UPDATE(id) grants. Restore
event ownership to the verified original owner. Drop only the exact newly
created objects. DROP OWNED, if retained as a cleanup assertion, is RESTRICT
and may run only after an independently checked dependency inventory proves
there are no unexpected owned objects/grants; it is never a broad cleanup
mechanism. Unexpected dependencies in another database also refuse the role
drop and roll back. Remove only introduced membership edges and three roles.

After Alembic has updated revision to 0029 but before outer commit, compare
the complete retained catalog/role identities/rows to the snapshot with §3.
Commit only if every relation is RAW_EXACT or the single allowlisted exception.
Capture actual pre/post raw digests, exact exception tuples and canonical
digests in the detached deployment receipt. Refusal or any failure rolls back
all DDL/grants/role changes, leaving byte-exact pre-attempt 0030 catalog/data.
The NULL exception NEVER applies to a failed/aborted transaction.

### 4.4 Snapshot and live validation boundaries

Fresh design validation against the frozen clean 0029 catalog remains exact,
including its NULL ACLs. Deployment preflight compares all non-ACL facts and
owner profile to that baseline while capturing arbitrary compatible existing
ACLs as deployment facts. Installed 0030 comparison uses the snapshot plus
explicit delta; downgrade comparison alone uses the NULL exception.

The successor contract adds rollbackAclPolicy, deploymentAclBaselinePolicy and
sourceBaselineNamespace. Existing observed clean-fixture ACL values are
explicitly labeled observations, never substituted as deployment ACLs.
In delta0030, rename existingExplicitAclBefore to observed0029ExplicitAcl and
retain its original value; add restorationBaseline="verified_deployment_snapshot".
Frozen function ACL observations get the same stage distinction without
changing their value. Their deployment ACLs are always restored raw-exact.
No non-ACL observed field is demoted into optional evidence.

The comparator rejects all unexpected keys/differences. No blanket exclusion
of /explicitAcl, /effectiveAcl, owners, definitions or indexes; no replacing
actual values with goldens; no fallback from a mismatch to a weaker digest.
Legacy tests that prove exact fresh 0029 remain unchanged in historical
replay. New downgrade-specific tests assert the new policy and actual changed
raw digest, not a falsely equal legacy digest.

context. No startswith-only assertion and no arbitrary Python exception is a
successful kill. Diagnostic precedence is §3 order, then first relation/
column in the declared tuple. The following closed policy codes are required:

### 9.2 Rollback of the amendment and safe resume

Design bootstrap is additive. Before a new active selection is independently
approved, the old subjects remain immutable historical evidence and B-001
continues to block implementation. A failed successor leaves the old bytes
untouched; discard/quarantine only newly created candidate successor artifacts
through an explicitly scoped coordinator action, not by deleting old evidence.

Once the new design chain passes, resume the partial implementation with
targeted changes to its loader/generator/frozen copy, ACL migration/wrapper,
catalog comparison and tests. Preserve the correct non-ACL operations; generate
only from the new approved persistence subject and independently diff all 201
fields/constraints. Preserve migrations 0027/0028/0029 byte-for-byte. Do not
mark the current partial tree “approved” because its old component design was.

For an amended installation, operational rollback disables database then
application acceptance gates and keeps compatible readers. Physical downgrade
is only the verified §4 inverse with empty/disabled prerequisites. An occupied
database is never emptied, demoted or translated to rejection. A failed
downgrade leaves the compatible 0030 installation intact. A deployment that
successfully downgraded with explicit defaults must record those real bytes;
a subsequent upgrade captures a new baseline (now non-NULL, so future rollback
must preserve it raw-exactly), not reuse the old NULL baseline. Each new
deployment attempt/version has a new snapshot and out-of-band binding;
old history is never rewritten.

### 9.3 Which prior PASS claims become historical/stale

- adversarial-persistence-dag-implementation.md remains a valid record of

  new snapshot/inverse or resumed production migration.
- adversarial-resource-rebinding.md and its old result remain historical
  resource/persistence-v1 bindings; they are stale for the successor chain,

or design change.

## Exact blocker

An empty, default-disabled 0030 database downgrades to revision 0029 without a
DDL error, but does not restore the exact 0029 physical catalog. The approved
0029 catalog digest is:

`0583a88e75fb95e9c1e4a7237cc63aba13bf86d5656061db7298af6a8286d871`

The post-downgrade catalog digest is:

`7b6594c70ae8f09b65ac809a3581ee298bdcd6cf7934ae8b5ca0123e165677ad`

The difference is all 74 preexisting relation `explicitAcl` values. Each was
SQL NULL before 0030 and becomes the explicit owner-only array
`{paprnav_user=arwdDxt/paprnav_user}` after the 0030 source/event grants are
revoked and the three `s4b_*` roles are dropped. Representative direct catalog
rows after downgrade:

```text
ad_v4_feature_gates|{paprnav_user=arwdDxt/paprnav_user}
ad_v4_review_case_events|{paprnav_user=arwdDxt/paprnav_user}
users|{paprnav_user=arwdDxt/paprnav_user}
```

PostgreSQL ordinary `GRANT`/`REVOKE`, `DROP OWNED`, and ownership transfer do
not turn an explicit owner-only ACL back into SQL NULL. This is semantically
important here because the design freezes explicit ACL state, not only current
effective privileges, and also requires preserving arbitrary installed
grants/grant options rather than assuming every deployment begins with NULL.

## Governing requirements

- P02 requires preservation of every observed owner, function ACL, explicit
  grantee/privilege/grant option and legacy behavior, with exact before/after
  and downgrade restoration rather than privilege reset.
- P05 requires the hardened non-login trusted owner to receive the exact source
  privileges necessary for its security-definer validators while runtime and
  PUBLIC remain denied sentinel/trusted-function/DDL escape.
- P10 requires downgrade to restore exact 0029 constraints, triggers, schemas,
  gate inventory, owners and ACLs, and permits physical downgrade only from an
  empty disabled 0030 database.
- The detailed P05/P10 text further states that NULL ACL means default effective
  privileges, not an empty privilege set, and says never to reset ACLs
  wholesale.

These requirements jointly need a durable, authoritative pre-upgrade ACL/owner
snapshot and an approved exact restoration mechanism across separate upgrade
and downgrade transactions. The current approved relation inventory provides
neither.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

- Direct `UPDATE pg_class SET relacl=NULL`: rejected as an unapproved system
  catalog write; it also cannot restore arbitrary installed grants.
- Hidden snapshot table: rejected because only the approved six authority
  tables plus sentinel are authorized.
- Encoding a snapshot in comments or another covert catalog channel: rejected
  as undeclared persistence/authority.
- Hard-coding NULL or owner-only ACLs: rejected because P02/P10 require the
  installed pre-upgrade state, including arbitrary explicit grants/options.
- Keeping the 0030 roles/grants after downgrade: rejected because it does not
  restore the 0029 schema/security catalog.
- Granting trusted-owner membership in the migration/runtime owner role:
  rejected as a privilege escalation that violates P05.
- Weakening rollback comparison to effective privileges: rejected because the
  normative contract explicitly freezes owner/ACL catalog facts and NULL ACL
  semantics.

Required remediation must independently specify the snapshot authority,
allowed storage channel and lifetime, restoration algorithm, concurrency and
tamper behavior, NULL-versus-explicit ACL treatment, and downgrade cleanup.

## Normative blocker and deviation

After an empty disabled downgrade, the frozen 0029 physical digest changes
from `0583a88e75fb95e9c1e4a7237cc63aba13bf86d5656061db7298af6a8286d871`
to `7b6594c70ae8f09b65ac809a3581ee298bdcd6cf7934ae8b5ca0123e165677ad`.
Every one of the 74 preexisting relations changes `explicitAcl` from SQL NULL
to an explicit owner-only ACL array after the 0030 trusted-source grants are
revoked and the roles are dropped. PostgreSQL ordinary GRANT/REVOKE cannot
reconstitute SQL NULL from an explicit ACL.

P02/P05/P10 require preservation of arbitrary installed explicit
grants/grant-options and identical before/after/rollback owner/ACL catalogs,
and explicitly forbid wholesale ACL resets. No approved persistent relation or
other cross-transaction channel exists for recording the pre-upgrade ACL/owner
snapshot. The builder will not invent direct `pg_class` catalog mutation, a
hidden snapshot table, a comment-based storage channel, or hard-coded NULL ACL
semantics. A normative design decision must specify the snapshot authority,
storage lifetime, restoration algorithm, and treatment of NULL versus explicit
ACLs before implementation can be validated.

A separate deterministic mismatch in the legacy gate setter (`ELSE 5` versus
an explicit fifth `WHEN`) was corrected in the migration generator after the
catalog comparison. That correction does not resolve the ACL blocker.

# Slice 4B persistence/runtime authority: third-loop reassessment

Status: ARCHITECTURE_REASSESSMENT_ONLY_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_IMPLEMENTATION_PAUSED

## Model routing

Builder/design architect: `/root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor`.
Requested: `gpt-6-astra`, `xhigh`. Actual: `model not exposed by runtime`;
`effort not exposed`. No fallback claimed. Trigger: third unsuccessful

recommendation. Coordinator `/root` owns the next assignment and gate.

## 1. Outcome and missing invariant

Recommend **one stable, non-owner application login per database, used by the
existing single application DATABASE_URL; a separate persistent migration
administrator per database; and two per-installation NOLOGIN acceptance roles**.
The RDS master is deployment/bootstrap/break-glass only. It is never an API or
worker credential. A reviewed platform privilege cutover must precede 0030.
Creating another passwordless login inside 0030 is not the runtime solution.

The missing invariant is end-to-end authority continuity:

> For each supported database and binary, an authenticated deployment principal
> must be able to install and reverse the declared DDL using supported RDS
> permissions, while the actual API/worker principal can perform every required
> source and acceptance operation through its configured connection, cannot
> acquire administrator/owner authority, and cannot obtain another database's
> acceptance authority. Every credential, membership, object grant, function,
> transaction, rollout state and rollback transition must belong to that same
> reviewed topology and be falsified by the same production-compatible oracle.

The previous loops tested ACL mechanics under a stronger administrator and
treated the application principal and deployment wiring as external details.
Neither exact ACL equality nor a sealed snapshot can establish the missing
principal, usable credentials, source privileges or connection path.

There is also an unavoidable PostgreSQL-16 constraint: the non-superuser role
creator cannot remove its bootstrap-superuser-granted automatic ADMIN edge.
The recommendation explicitly retains that administrative edge while the child
role exists, removes only separately granted temporary access edges, and relies
on whole-role removal for final edge cleanup. A requirement for no such edge
after successful creation is incompatible with this ordinary CREATEROLE
profile. It must not be implemented as a warning-ignoring REVOKE.
[PostgreSQL 16 role attributes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/role-attributes.html).

## 2. Repository evidence, not an assertion about live AWS

Inspected staged/unstaged/untracked scope with `git status --short`, the current
run, deployment/configuration files, migration implementation and callers.
No AWS API, live secret, live database, Terraform plan/apply, or new test was
run. The repository describes an RDS/ECS target; it does not prove that target
is presently deployed. `.ai/AWS_DEPLOYMENT_STATUS.md` says the runtime skeleton
was not applied as of its 2026-07-10 update. That distinction is deliberate.

| Observed repository fact | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `infra/terraform/database.tf` provisions RDS PostgreSQL, database `paprnav`, master username `paprnav_app`, and `manage_master_user_password=true`. `variables.tf` declares engine `16.3`. | A name containing “app” does not make this a least-privilege runtime account. The supported minor version must be explicitly selected and measured; 16.3 in configuration is not evidence of current service availability. |
| Terraform creates one application `database-url` placeholder. README says to refresh it when the managed master password rotates. | The documented credential path conflates master administration with application access. There is no bound least-privilege provisioning/rotation path. |
| `ecs_runtime.tf` gives API and OCR worker the same `DATABASE_URL`/session-secret list. Both use one execution role; frontend also uses that execution role. No migrator task exists. | Add a distinct migrator execution/task boundary. Frontend must not inherit database-secret retrieval authority simply through a shared execution role. |
| `backend/app/core/config.py` has one `database_url`, local dotenv loading, and a development fallback. `db/session.py` constructs one module-level engine and `SessionLocal`. | There is no acceptance-specific engine. Runtime configuration is cached; secret changes do not replace existing processes/pools. Production must fail on missing/privileged/misbound credentials, not fall back locally. |

An externally supplied transaction is not currently an honored migration contract. |

| Current P05 says runtime cannot assume the trusted or migration owner; current roles/functions and authority ACLs are exact. | A successor must explicitly distinguish trusted deployment administrators from untrusted runtime and bind actual login identity. No silent reinterpretation of the old approved bytes. |
| Prior review found both “new login cannot read sources” and “old login cannot use authority”, plus missing independent namespace-OID/name mutations. | A usable source-to-acceptance transaction and coordinate-isolated identity tests are mandatory, not optional test expansion. |
