## 3. Alternatives and decision

| Alternative | Coherence and cost | Decision candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated migration administrator, stable application login, per-database NOLOGIN trusted/runtime roles; one application engine | Source checks, actor locks, authority rows, signoff, terminal event and deferred validation share one PostgreSQL transaction. Requires an explicit platform privilege cutover and source-grant inventory. | Recommend. Fits existing engine/callers without a second runtime transaction boundary. |
| Separate acceptance LOGIN, secret and engine | Can isolate acceptance credential access, but acceptance needs source access too. Existing source/actor reads and acceptance writes on two sessions are not one atomic transaction. A complete redesign must either move the whole operation to the acceptance session with source privileges, or define a separately reviewed distributed protocol. | Reject for this bounded slice. Two secrets alone do not solve atomicity; moving the whole operation would still require the missing source/credential design. |
| Explicit deployment change to self-managed PostgreSQL with true-superuser migration control | Can support superuser-only role-edge cleanup; introduces operating-system, patching, backup, HA, networking and recovery authority outside the current RDS design. | Reject without a separately authorized infrastructure project. Do not emulate it in tests and call it RDS. |
| Keep the current master/owner application credential, or grant it runtime membership | Appears to preserve source access but an administrator can bypass the intended owner/function boundary. | Reject. A master credential is not a runtime negative-test subject. |
| Zero persistent creator edges after CREATEROLE, implemented by ordinary self-REVOKE | Contradicts PostgreSQL's grantor rules; can also remove dependent memberships if a stronger actor uses CASCADE. | Reject. Retain declared administrative edges, or reopen the infrastructure/administrator decision. |

This recommendation does not claim that a complete source-grant manifest or
RDS execution proof already exists. Those are named prerequisites below. It
removes ambiguity about which architecture those artifacts must prove; it
does not authorize a builder to fill privilege gaps with GRANT ALL.

## 4. Principals, exact edge policy and administrator lifecycle

Use symbols only as bindings to persisted, verified role name/OID pairs:

- `D`: existing RDS master/deployment principal, currently configured as
  `paprnav_app`; retain AWS-managed attributes/memberships, never runtime.
- `B`: PostgreSQL's bootstrap grantor identity observed in the native catalog;
  do not hard-code its name or pretend a session can authenticate as it on RDS.
- `M`: persistent per-database migration administrator, provisioned by D.
- `L`: stable per-database application login, provisioned by M in the platform
  cutover, before 0030; remains through acceptance downgrade and password changes.
- `T`: per-installation NOLOGIN trusted owner; `R`: per-installation NOLOGIN
  acceptance runtime privilege role. M creates T/R inside the 0030 transaction.
  Existing logical IDs `s4b_trusted_owner` and `s4b_runtime` bind to T/R.
  `s4b_login` denotes existing L; 0030 no longer creates a third login.

M has `LOGIN NOSUPERUSER CREATEROLE NOCREATEDB NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION
NOBYPASSRLS`, connection limit -1 and non-expiring role password validity.
It has no `rds_superuser`, `rds_password`, `rds_iam`, replication, server-file,
program-execution or blanket catalog-reader membership. It owns this database,
its application schema and enumerated ordinary migration objects after the
platform cutover. It does not own objects in another application database.
It cannot be a service credential or an assumed role reachable from L.
Database ownership carries the database-local `pg_database_owner` relationship;
that implicit relationship must be observed separately from pg_auth_members.

L has `LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB INHERIT NOREPLICATION
NOBYPASSRLS`, connection limit -1, non-expiring password validity and no owned
schema, table, function, sequence or database. T/R have `NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER
NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS`, password NULL,
connection limit -1 and no role-specific settings/security labels. R owns no
objects. T owns only the exact declared acceptance/event/sentinel/snapshot
objects and trusted functions. The platform profile separately enumerates the
allowed settings on M/L; nothing grants SET session_replication_role.

M is intentionally a trusted administrator: ADMIN on T means M can obtain T's
authority. NOINHERIT/SET-false guards against accidental use, not malicious M.
That is compatible with separation from runtime, not protection against an
administrator. A compromised D/M is outside the runtime ACL threat boundary;
credential protection and independent deployment review are therefore part of
the trusted computing base.

### 4.1 Naming and stable identity

Retain the prior 48-ASCII-byte construction: `pn4b_<kind>_` + eight lowercase
hex digits of database OID + `_` + 32 lowercase hex digits of an installation
nonce. Kinds are `m`, `l`, `t`, `r`. The platform cutover reserves M/L's shared
namespace; 0030 uses a separately recorded T/R installation namespace. Roles
are not recomputed from the current database name. At most eight collision
candidates, all required names absent, no adoption of a preexisting matching
name/comment. A concurrent creation race aborts the transaction; no mutation
of the colliding role. Native OIDs, names, creator/grantor identities and scoped
installation IDs are persisted and validated. A database rename preserves
them. Drop/recreate, role rename or name/OID reuse is a mismatch, not a refresh.

The application login is stable within this database's platform lifecycle, not
one cluster-wide login shared by multiple databases. Database-OID reuse uses a
fresh nonce and must not adopt orphaned roles. Database creation is a separate
deployment operation outside the transactional acceptance migration.

### 4.2 PostgreSQL-16 automatic edges: retain, verify, then clean up correctly

An edge is `(granted_role, member, grantor, ADMIN, INHERIT, SET)`; the arrow
means granted role to member, not ownership. `SET LOCAL
createrole_self_grant=''` is required before role creation; read it back. This
does not suppress the automatic ADMIN edge. The setting controls additional
inherit/set access only.
[PostgreSQL client defaults](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/runtime-config-client.html#GUC-CREATEROLE-SELF-GRANT).

Expected relevant edges, excluding independently enumerated AWS-managed D/B
edges, are closed as follows:

| Lifecycle | Edge | Flags ADMIN / INHERIT / SET |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform M created by non-superuser D | M → D, grantor B | true / false / false |
| Platform L created by M | L → M, grantor B | true / false / false |
| 0030 installed | T → M and R → M, grantor B | true / false / false |
| 0030 installed | R → L, grantor M | false / true / false |
| Only during owner-sensitive migration steps | T → M, grantor M | false / false / true |

The last row is a separate grantor record, not a modification of B's edge.
Use an explicitly M-attributed grant, perform the required SET ROLE/ownership
work, RESET ROLE, then revoke only M's edge with explicit grantor and RESTRICT.
Read back pg_auth_members and require B's edge unchanged, the temporary M edge
absent, and R→L unchanged. Warnings or zero-row changes do not prove cleanup.
No additional R→M access edge, T→L edge, L→runtime edge, cross-database role
membership, ADMIN/SET on R→L, duplicate grantor, or indirect L→M/T path is
allowed. Temporary T schema CREATE used for supported ownership transfer is
also revoked and checked before commit.

The intended membership operations have this shape, with safely quoted actual
identifiers and native before/after verification; they are not commands to run
in this reassessment:

```sql
SET LOCAL createrole_self_grant = '';
-- M creates T/R; assert the B-attributed creator rows exactly.
GRANT T TO M WITH ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE GRANTED BY M;
GRANT R TO L WITH ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE GRANTED BY M;
-- Owner-sensitive work, explicitly bounded SET ROLE T, then RESET ROLE.
REVOKE T FROM M GRANTED BY M RESTRICT;
-- The B-attributed T->M row MUST remain; it is not a cleanup failure.
```

Ordinary M cannot revoke B's creator row. On successful downgrade, first revoke
R→L as M; restore/drop exactly the local dependent objects and explicit T/R
grants; then DROP R/T as M. Native role deletion removes incident memberships.
If any external dependency or unrecognized edge exists, abort the entire
downgrade, restoring its schema, snapshot and role graph. Never DROP OWNED or
CASCADE across databases. M/L and their creator edges remain after acceptance
downgrade; they are platform roles, not acceptance residue. Removal of M/L is a
separate whole-database decommission, not hidden in 0030. On failed upgrade,
transaction rollback removes newly created T/R and all their edges.
[PostgreSQL role removal](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/role-removal.html).

Grantor-specific dependency and SET semantics are part of the oracle, not
interchangeable ACL spellings. Removing an administrator's ADMIN edge is not
safe merely because current INHERIT/SET flags are false.
[PostgreSQL GRANT](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-grant.html),
[REVOKE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-revoke.html).

The RDS profile is **ordinary NOSUPERUSER M**, not “rds_superuser equals
superuser.” AWS does not expose a true-superuser session. D bootstraps database
ownership and any narrowly enumerated helper permission M needs; M performs
0030 without D in that transaction. Whether RDS permits the exact helper grants
and records the assumed B/D edges is an empirical prerequisite. Do not bypass
a failed profile by granting rds_superuser to M.
[AWS RDS roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.PostgreSQL.CommonDBATasks.Roles.rds_superuser.html).

## 5. Object privileges and the platform cutover boundary

The platform cutover is necessary new scope requiring explicit approval. It
must convert a master/owner runtime into L and give M explicit ownership before
the ACL snapshot for 0030 exists. It is not part of the 74-relation rollback
exception. For an already initialized database, D transfers only enumerated
application objects, preserving data and recording every owner/ACL consequence;
no cluster-wide REASSIGN OWNED shortcut. M/old-owner D must be able to restore
that platform baseline independently. Fresh databases can run historical
revisions under M, but must yield the same reviewed logical profile.

No claim is made that the current source catalog already authorizes those
owner changes. Historical source bytes and observed catalogs remain historical.
A new platform baseline and its provenance must precede the future persistence
leaf, physical snapshot and source-catalog validation. If that changes literal
owner assumptions, those changes require versioned authority review; they may
not be disguised as the existing NULL-relacl exception.

Required effective privilege policy:

| Principal/object | Exact permitted class | Exclusions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L, ordinary pre-0030 application source | Explicit object/column grants from a closed caller-derived platform manifest: SELECT; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only for admitted operations; sequence USAGE only for enumerated generated-ID dependencies; lock-required UPDATE columns explicitly declared | No ownership, GRANT OPTION, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, schema CREATE or inherited administrator privilege. No future-object wildcard. |
| L, immutable legacy source/review rows | SELECT/INSERT as required; narrow lock/update privileges only where a frozen existing trigger/locking protocol actually requires them, with immutable triggers retained | Ownership-era ability to disable/replace triggers must not survive. “Immutable” is not permission to omit locks or invoker-trigger writes. |
| L, `ad_v4_feature_gates` | SELECT; capability read function as declared | No direct writes; no EXECUTE of `paprnav_set_v4_feature_gate(text,boolean,text)`. Gate mutation is deployment/M-only. |
| L via R, the six new graph/signoff tables and `ad_v4_review_case_events` | SELECT, INSERT; no grant options | No UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER or ownership. Event privileges needed by old rejection-only binaries remain available through this same membership. |
| L/R/PUBLIC, sentinel and ACL snapshot | None, including columns | No runtime read/DDL/DML or direct trusted-function execution. |
| T, trusted source | Exact current ordered 74 SELECT targets and UPDATE(id) on `public.users` and `public.organization_memberships` solely for locks; necessary schema USAGE | No extra source DML, CREATE, ownership or runtime membership. Temporary grants have exact inverse deltas. |
| T, declared authority/sentinel/snapshot and trusted functions | Ownership of the exact declared objects; SECURITY DEFINER functions with fully qualified relations and fixed safe search paths | No unqualified attacker-controlled relation resolution; no arbitrary SQL or application-chosen SET ROLE. |
| L, ordinary functions | EXECUTE only on frozen callable signatures needed by runtime or invoker-function dependencies; capability/read helpers included | No migration, gate setter, snapshot or seven acceptance trusted function entry points. Trigger firing is tested as L despite lack of direct EXECUTE. |

This is a precise privilege policy, **not an already completed exact object
grant list**. The 74 acceptance sources are not the entire application schema.
An implementation-complete platform grant manifest covering authentication,
uploads/OCR, discovery, matching, historical review/materialization, scripts,
sequences and invoked helpers is a prerequisite. Its entries must name object,
native identity, grantee, grantor, privilege, option and caller/negative test.
Unknown objects/callers fail inventory closure; the builder may not infer
permissions from “all tables in public.” No implementation is authorized until
that manifest and its executable runtime oracle are independently reviewed.

All arbitrary explicit grants/grant options, grantor chains and column ACLs in
the admitted pre-0030 baseline retain the previous preservation requirements.
If existing grants make runtime effectively an owner/administrator or expose a
new trusted object, the baseline is incompatible: stop for an explicit platform
remediation rather than silently revoke the external principal or accept it.
After platform approval, 0030 still preserves every non-NULL raw ACL and all
non-ACL facts except its declared changes; only the original exact allowlist's
pre-NULL relation ACLs may finish at exact native owner defaults. A prior owner
transition is not an excuse to normalize arbitrary non-NULL ACL arrays.

### Database and schema policy

For every managed application database, the platform cutover revokes PUBLIC
CONNECT/TEMP/CREATE and grants CONNECT directly to its own L and M, with D's
administrative access explicitly represented. M owns the database/schema; L/R
get schema USAGE only; T gets USAGE and no steady-state CREATE. PUBLIC gets no
application-schema CREATE/USAGE and no application-function EXECUTE. Explicit
application function grants replace reliance on PUBLIC. Default privileges are
closed per creator: no automatic runtime table grants; PUBLIC function EXECUTE
revoked for newly created application functions; future migrations add named
grants through a reviewed manifest. These are platform changes, not undeclared
edits to the 0030 rollback snapshot.

L/R have no TEMP, including through PUBLIC or an indirect membership. T's
search path must explicitly handle pg_temp ordering or fully qualify every
relation/type access; caller-controlled search_path never supplies authority.
Do not attempt to revoke standard pg_catalog visibility globally. Catalog
observation permissions for M are enumerated separately from source DML.
Default database CONNECT/TEMP and function EXECUTE must be tested explicitly,
not inferred from a table ACL or absence of a direct grant.
[PostgreSQL privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/ddl-priv.html).

Managed database B must reject L_A even if both share an RDS instance. Denying
CONNECT is evaluated cluster-wide for managed databases, including direct and
inherited grants; bootstrap also audits the administrative `postgres` database.
AWS-owned maintenance databases/roles are provider scope: any unavoidable
connection or catalog visibility is documented and tested not to expose
application objects, not falsely called a complete cluster isolation proof.
Template databases cannot carry an installed 0030 snapshot into a new database.

## 6. Credentials, processes and transactions

There is **one application credential/secret and one application engine per
database**. The existing `/project/environment/database-url` secret becomes L's
URL and is shared by API and worker for that database. There is a separate
`migration-database-url` secret for M, injected only as `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`
into the migrator. The AWS-managed D credential is a third, deployment-only
administrative secret; it is neither application nor migrator input. The
session secret is unrelated. No acceptance-specific password or connection is
created inside 0030, so credential publication cannot split its SQL transaction.

Ownership of credential lifecycle belongs to the deployment/security operator
under the reviewed deployment IAM role and runbook, not request handlers,
workers, migration trigger functions, or this agent:

1. D provisions M; M provisions L; generated secrets are written directly to
   Secrets Manager over the authenticated administrative path, never committed,
   logged, put in Terraform values/state, or placed in the ACL snapshot.
2. Database username/OID and secret ARN/version are separately verified in a
   deployment attestation; secret bytes/password verifiers are not audit payloads.
3. Use SCRAM passwords and certificate-verifying TLS to RDS with the reviewed CA
   bundle. API/worker execution roles can retrieve L's exact secret ARN only;
   the migrator can retrieve M's only; frontend receives neither. Runtime task
   roles cannot read D/M secrets or run/pass the migrator task role.
4. Initially use an explicitly coordinated maintenance-window rotation of L,
   keeping its role name/OID and grants stable: disable writes/scheduling,
   drain tasks/connections, change password, publish the new secret version,
   verify a fresh L connection, start fresh tasks, then reopen gates. Do not
   promise zero-downtime dual-password behavior. M rotation is a separate
   deployment-only window; D remains AWS-managed.
5. SQL ALTER ROLE and Secrets Manager publication are not one transaction. If
   publication/acknowledgement fails, keep workloads stopped, use the independent
   administrator path to establish and verify one known credential/version,
   and restart only after verification. Never fall back to D or stale M/L URLs.
6. Revocation means NOLOGIN plus stop/drain/terminate authorized sessions and
   revoke runtime membership as appropriate; password change alone is not
   evidence that existing sessions have ended. Preserve role identity and
   immutable history. An incident-altered role graph blocks physical downgrade
   until independently reconciled; snapshot verification must not ignore drift.

ECS does not hot-refresh environment-injected secrets. New task deployment is
required after rotation, including the scheduled worker's next task definition
and all long-lived API replicas.
[AWS ECS secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/secrets-envvar-secrets-manager.html).
Certificate/hostname validation and the RDS CA lifecycle must be proven through
the actual client configuration.
[AWS PostgreSQL TLS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/PostgreSQL.Concepts.General.SSL.html).

API requests, all workers and ordinary domain administrative scripts retain
`SessionLocal` under L. An acceptance operation owns exactly one connection and
one transaction for source reads, current actor/membership locks, freshness/CAS
checks, all graph/signoff/event inserts and deferred validation. No side engine,
SET ROLE T/M, nested independent commit, or cross-connection compensation is
allowed. Read-only snapshot paths keep their existing repeatable-read boundary.
Workers share this database capability ceiling; application authorization still
controls which human can approve. Splitting worker credentials further is a
separate least-privilege project, not a covert second acceptance connection.

Migrations and feature-gate administration run only in a one-shot migrator task
under M. Its image is immutable/pinned, command is explicit, and there is no
API startup `alembic upgrade head`. `env.py` must eventually honor an injected
single connection and explicit migration URL, reject fallback to DATABASE_URL,
offline mode, autocommit blocks, two-phase commit and intermediate commits for
0030. Revision row, T/R roles/edges, sealed snapshot and all DDL are committed
once. Connection/XID continuity is checked across the whole migration.

The database-local sealed snapshot remains the right rollback authority. Capture
before retained-object owner/ACL changes, seal and revalidate before each use,
read and verify before drop on downgrade; unexpected schema/table/role identity,
shape, owner, ACL, trigger, row/hash/count or delta fails closed. A crash before
commit rolls the transaction back. A lost commit acknowledgement is resolved
after reconnect/advisory lock by the exact revision plus sealed installed or
absent state, not by recapturing the current ACLs. Mixed/inconsistent states
block. Platform provisioning/secret publication have their own explicit
deployment lifecycle and are not mistaken for that atomic SQL boundary.

## 7. Rollout, rollback and multiple databases

1. Freeze/snapshot the current partial tree and exact historical recovery bytes;
   no regeneration from modified core.py and no use of the failed downgrade to
   manufacture a baseline. Establish the independently approved platform profile
   on a pristine/restored 0029 database first.
2. Keep all acceptance gates off. Complete D/M/L separation, explicit source
   grants, database/schema policy and credential rollout. Run the existing
   application and worker flows as L before installing 0030. If any owner-only
   operation is found, the grant/caller design returns to review; do not grant
   owner membership. D no longer appears in runtime secrets or live sessions.
3. Install a future reviewed 0030 with M while L credentials remain unchanged.
   Acceptance membership is installed transactionally, so an old source-capable
   binary can continue only within its already reviewed compatibility boundary.
4. Deploy acceptance-aware readers/writers to every API and worker before gate
   activation. Binary/build versions, database capability result and credential
   identity are measured together. Retain the prior rules prohibiting old
   readers after incompatible immutable history has been committed.
5. Operational rollback disables acceptance application/database gates and
   retains a compatible reader, schema, sealed snapshot and roles. Physical
   downgrade is allowed only with the exact occupancy/lock/gate checks; M reads
   and verifies the snapshot, restores supported DDL/ACL state, removes T/R
   dependencies and drops T/R in the same transaction. L/M remain and the
   stable DATABASE_URL still supports 0029 source operations.
6. Do not roll application credentials back to the master as a recovery tactic.
   Reversing the platform privilege cutover is separately reviewed maintenance,
   with actual before/after ACL/owner evidence; acceptance downgrade does not
   authorize it.

A and B each have separate M/L/T/R identities, secrets and database CONNECT
grants. Administrators are trusted per database, but CREATEROLE is cluster-wide:
M can create new roles, so its isolation is not a claim that a malicious
deployment administrator is sandboxed from the cluster. It must lack ADMIN on
another database's roles and no managed database may trust arbitrary new roles
through PUBLIC. If isolation between mutually hostile administrators is required,
use separate RDS instances; that is an explicit topology decision.

For independent downgrade, inspect pg_shdepend and the closed membership graph;
foreign ownership, ACL dependencies, unexpected membership/grantor dependencies
or another database's use of T/R abort local removal. Never clean another
database opportunistically. Native DROP ROLE is the final race check. Database
rename changes endpoint/URL routing metadata only, preserving role bindings.
Drop/recreate, logical restore or cloning with new database/role OIDs requires
a separately reviewed rebind/migration, not a new snapshot of old acceptance
history. Physical restore requires measured identity and sealed-state proof;
matching names alone are insufficient. Orphan-role cleanup is a separate
explicit target-resolved deployment action.

## 8. Normative deployment inputs and authority direction

The future decision must bind a closed platform authority, not leave Terraform
and runbooks outside the review boundary. The following existing paths become
normative inputs for the deployment/runtime topology they express:

| Input family | Required paths and role |
| --- | --- |
| RDS/secret/network definition | `infra/terraform/database.tf`, `variables.tf`, `network.tf`, `outputs.tf`, provider/version lock and selected non-secret environment values: engine/profile, database ownership bootstrap, secret ARNs, TLS and permitted network callers. |
| ECS/IAM execution | `infra/terraform/ecs_runtime.tf`, `infra/aws-iam/paprnav-terraform-deploy-policy.json`, associated trust policy/README: API/worker/migrator/frontend separation, exact secret/PassRole/RunTask authority and immutable task/image routing. The existing secret policy pattern must actually match the slash-prefixed secret ARNs; do not infer permission from a policy label. |
| Configuration/connection | `backend/app/core/config.py`, `backend/app/db/session.py`, `backend/app/db/migrations/env.py`, `backend/alembic.ini`, `backend/.env.example`: no production fallback; one runtime engine and explicit M-only migration connection. |
| Local/runtime parity | `backend/docker-compose.yml`, `backend/Dockerfile`, `backend/README.md`, `backend/app/db/migrations/README.md`, selected migration verification scripts: bootstrap-only local superuser, then the same ordinary M/L flow. |
| Rollout/provisioning/credential runbook | `infra/terraform/README.md`, `infra/aws-iam/README.md`, applicable `backend/app/contracts/*rollout.md`; new narrowly scoped platform grant/provisioning and rotation specifications must be named in the next authorized design, not invented during implementation. |
| Caller and migration scope | API dependencies/routes, worker and ordinary administration entry points, source SQL/functions, 0030 migration/SQL/contract, generation tool and privilege tests: derived subjects to be checked against the platform policy. |

The deployment status log is historical evidence, not a normative source of
current AWS state. Live attestation binds account/region, RDS resource identity,
actual server version, parameter group, role/object catalog, secret version IDs,
task-definition revisions, image digests and observed principal, without secrets.

Direction is platform requirements/profile → explicit provisioning/grant subject
and source baseline → independent component evidence; persistence foundational
requirements remain a standalone leaf with the selected profile's necessary
normative facts stated directly. The persistence contract must not acquire a
reverse edge to Terraform results, matrix, a review, or its future integration
review. Deployment files are component subjects/closed integration inputs,
not mutable prose silently incorporated into the foundational leaf. The active
audit wrapper selects exact independently approved component versions; historical
v1/v2 maps and snapshots remain immutable. Matrix and final validator consume
the completed lower-level subjects and detached reviews. A future overall review
is downstream and never an input to what it reviews.

No successor paths/versions or arithmetic are issued here. The rejected
remediation-2 proposal's F/FR 92, 67 registries, 2,042 occurrences, 43/1,639
ordered inventory and 11,553 minimum probes are historical proposed counts, not
an authority for this changed platform topology. Adding platform/config/IAM
subjects, creator edges, existing L/M identity bindings, grants and lifecycle
evidence changes inventories and may change snapshot row/layout accounting.
Do not assume its 24-column/1,138-row shape remains closed just because the
database-local snapshot mechanism remains useful. Recalculate only after the
architecture/profile and component scope are approved.

Semantic acceptance/mapping behavior is not being changed. Existing mapping,
semantic interpreter/fixtures, calibration source and history stay byte-identical
in this pass. They can be replayed later if their selected bytes remain valid;
do not regenerate semantic goldens to accommodate a deployment error. The old
SQL topology harness and administrator-based evidence are useful historical
mechanical evidence, not the missing non-superuser/RDS runtime oracle.

### Independent namespace mutation requirement

For every one of the 74 retained relation slots, preserve the same-name/new-
relation-OID case and introduce two separately named single-coordinate checks:

- `ACL_NAMESPACE_OID_CHANGED`: same schema name, relation identity and other
  payload coordinates, substituted namespace OID only.
- `ACL_SCHEMA_NAME_CHANGED`: same namespace OID and other coordinates, schema
  name changed only.

N16 can become one cohort; the other adds one 74-case rejected cohort before
any new runtime/administrator/credential cases. This is a conceptual adjustment,
not a regenerated corpus total. Each test must independently fail if its sole
comparison is removed. Native schema rename proves name drift with retained
namespace OID; same-name namespace replacement and compound real DDL cases are
additional mechanism evidence, not substitutes for isolated catalog-payload
mutations. Keep all same-name/new relation OID, owner name/OID, role identity,
wrong relkind, column ACL and grant-chain tests; publish detector precedence
separately where real DDL necessarily changes several coordinates.

## 9. Shared production-compatible oracle and evidence boundaries

The oracle must have an independent observer and a real authenticated L
connection, not a superuser SET ROLE convenience test. Expected role/grant
topology comes from the independently reviewed platform manifest, not from the
builder's emitted SQL or from simply accepting whatever the catalog returns.
The migration principal is authenticated M with rolsuper=false and the exact
declared profile; neither setup superuser nor D executes 0030 on its behalf.

| Named oracle boundary | Positive and negative evidence required | Where it can be proved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ORACLE-ADMIN-PROFILE` | M owns intended DB/schema/legacy objects; cannot administer another DB's roles; no rds_superuser/runtime reachability; every catalog/helper privilege works without broad membership. | Vanilla PG16 for ordinary privileges; disposable matching RDS for provider restrictions, D bootstrap and actual parameter profile. |
| `ORACLE-CREATOR-GRANTOR` | Exact B-attributed ADMIN-only rows; explicit M SET edge appears/disappears; failed attempt to remove B's edge cannot pass cleanup; R→L survives temporary-edge removal; DROP/rollback removes intended edges only. | Vanilla PG16 directly; repeat on RDS because its bootstrap/master grantor behavior is part of the profile. |
| `ORACLE-RUNTIME-PATH` | Fresh L login runs authentication, source reads/locks, representative normal writes and complete acceptance on one connection/XID; all API/worker/script paths have classified grants. | Full application image against ordinary PG16 M/L, then ECS/RDS smoke using actual task secret injection. |
| `ORACLE-RUNTIME-DENY` | L cannot SET ROLE M/T, grant role membership, create roles/schema/temp objects, replace functions/triggers, change owner, write gates/sentinel/snapshot, or invoke trusted functions directly; indirect edges and PUBLIC grants fail the profile. | Vanilla PG16 and real RDS L connection. |
| `ORACLE-ATOMIC-ACL` | Complete supported upgrade/downgrade under M, native NULL/default ACL equivalence and byte-exact non-NULL/column/grant-chain preservation, sealed snapshot/use/drop checks, cap/occupancy abort, XID continuity, crash/retry and autocommit rejection. | Full future migration in disposable PG16; matching RDS confirms no hidden superuser/system-catalog requirement. |
| `ORACLE-DATABASE-ISOLATION` | A/B independently install/downgrade in both orders; L_A cannot connect/read/write/assume roles in B; foreign dependency blocks local drop and rolls back; rename/reuse/restore mismatch cases fail precisely. | Two databases in one vanilla cluster, then two databases in the same disposable RDS instance. |
| `ORACLE-CREDENTIAL-DELIVERY` | Runtime tasks lack M/D secret access; migrator lacks runtime routing ambiguity; frontend no DB-secret capability; rotation restarts all consumers; revoked sessions do not remain usable; stale secret/version fails closed. | IAM policy analysis plus disposable AWS Secrets Manager/ECS/RDS end-to-end evidence. Vanilla cannot prove IAM, ECS injection, RDS TLS or managed-password behavior. |
| `ORACLE-ROLLOUT` | Old/new compatible binaries under L, gates off/on, operational rollback with retained history, forbidden old reader, empty-only physical downgrade and retained M/L/source behavior. | Version-pinned images against PG16 and a production-compatible deployment smoke. |
| `ORACLE-IDENTITY-COORDINATES` | Each relation/namespace/owner/role name and OID independently falsified; detector-removal mutations fail the oracle; compound supported DDL separately classified. | Independent catalog fixtures and isolated native PG16/RDS mechanism tests. |

Local/CI must bootstrap an ordinary M, then disconnect the setup superuser;
run the actual migrator command as M and normal API/workers as L. The current
Compose same-user pattern cannot be the acceptance oracle. Pin server/image
minor versions and record psycopg/SQLAlchemy/Alembic versions. SQLite or static
schema validation cannot attest any PostgreSQL privilege or transaction fact.

RDS evidence must verify exact permitted catalog reads (including pg_auth_members,
pg_roles, pg_shdepend and whichever server/cluster identity helper the snapshot
requires). In particular, do not assume ordinary M can call pg_control_system
because the earlier superuser probe could. A narrowly reviewed D-granted helper
privilege is acceptable only if available and demonstrated on the selected RDS
version; otherwise the identity observation/profile must return to design review.
Granting pg_monitor/rds_superuser or silently dropping the identity check is not
an allowed fallback. This is a named remaining feasibility gate, not a claim of
an already verified RDS implementation.

The prior proposal and independent reviewer established bounded PG16.14
transactional role/table rollback, multi-database dependency refusal, independent
cleanup and rename behavior. The reviewer also reproduced the automatic creator
edge and disconnected source/authority runtime grants. Those are inherited
evidence with the exact hashes in §2; they do not attest this recommendation.
This reassessment ran no new probes or tests. Official documentation establishes
the relevant service/SQL constraints, but cannot prove the repository's eventual
IAM wiring, grants, migration program or crash behavior.

Any disposable AWS experiment requires separately approved scope, account,
region, cost, TTL, isolated data and teardown evidence. Do not use the pilot
database, retrieve its secrets or create infrastructure under this task. If RDS
access/budget is unavailable, record the missing evidence and keep the production
gate blocked; a vanilla superuser success is not a substitute.

## 10. Exact decision questions, prerequisites and bounded next gate

The coordinator and independent architecture reviewer must decide:

1. Approve one L per database/single runtime engine, with M separate and D
   deployment-only, instead of a separate acceptance login/connection?
2. Approve persistent, exact B-attributed ADMIN creator edges as part of trusted
   administrator authority, with temporary access cleanup and whole-role final
   removal, instead of the impossible ordinary-creator zero-edge requirement?
3. Approve the separately versioned platform cutover: source ownership/grants,
   database/schema PUBLIC/TEMP policy, gate administration and credential/IAM
   separation before the persistence ACL snapshot baseline?
4. Is the intended isolation runtime-per-database under trusted deployment
   administrators, or hostile-admin isolation requiring separate RDS instances?
5. Approve maintenance-window credential rotation and restart, with one stable
   login identity and no zero-downtime/dual-password claim?
6. Select the supported RDS PostgreSQL 16 minor/profile and authorize a separate
   disposable production-compatible oracle, including catalog/helper feasibility?

Prerequisites before a successor design can authorize implementation: exact
caller/object grant manifest; measured platform baseline; complete native role
and grantor graph; concrete credential issuer/rotator/revoker runbook and IAM
bindings; migration connection/transaction contract; RDS profile/helper proof;
namespace-coordinate corpus correction; independently calculated authority DAG
and bounds after the new scope is closed. A missing item is a blocker, not a
builder choice. No unresolved feasibility is asserted as a PASS.

The **next gate is independent architecture review of this reassessment and
explicit resolution of those questions**, not production implementation or an
automatic remediation-3 authoring task. After that gate, the coordinator may
authorize a bounded platform/profile design and disposable oracle separately;
only their approved outcomes may feed a later implementation-complete versioned
persistence amendment. That amendment must preserve history, recalculate closed
inventories/probes, obtain independent design review, then resume the saved
partial implementation in a separate assignment.

The saved Sol work is not discarded or relabeled approved. Its current owner/
role helpers and downgrade path are incompatible with the recommended profile;
valid graph/constraint logic can be reused only after byte-level comparison to
the future approved contract. Historical core/source-test recovery remains
separate from current modified files. No failed partial installation may be
adopted or snapshotted as if it were the pristine pre-0030 authority.

Preservation evidence for this pass is a read-only hash manifest of 197 existing
run/deployment/config/migration/caller files captured before writing; final
comparison and this document's SHA-256 are reported externally. No review
approval, finding closure, test result, successor hash or deployment claim is
manufactured by this document.

def archive_bytes(entries):
    buf=io.BytesIO()

       'overlay':{'path':MODEL,'bytes':226411,'sha256':OVERLAY_HASH,'recoveryPathHistoricalOnly':str(p),'runtimeDependencyOnRecoveryPath':False,'unifiedDiff':diff,'replacementLines':4},

def relationships(b,p):

    from app.models.core import Base

            for mode,loader in [('lazy',lazyload),('selectin',selectinload),('joined',joinedload)]:
                with Session(e) as s:
                    rows=s.scalars(sa.select(cls).options(loader(attr))).unique().all()
                    nonempty=sum(bool(getattr(row,r['attribute'])) for row in rows)
                    observations.append({'id':r['id']+':'+mode,'sourceRows':len(rows),'nonemptySourceRows':nonempty,'status':'PASS_NONEMPTY' if nonempty else 'NOT_RUN_NO_VALID_DOMAIN_ROWS'})

            m.execute('RESET ROLE')
            m.execute(f"REVOKE {b.ident(b.ROLES['T'])} FROM {b.ident(b.ROLES['M'])} GRANTED BY {b.ident(b.ROLES['M'])} RESTRICT")
            m.execute(f"GRANT UPDATE(id) ON public.{b.ident(rel)} TO {b.ident(b.ROLES['T'])}")

    """Complete real service transaction with native initially-deferred mode.

    Frozen v1 forced constraints IMMEDIATE between materializers and review;
    its 42703 stop hid that harness-only premature-flush error. V2 restores

    try:

        with Session(le) as s:
            actor=s.get(User,user);parsed=_request(directive,document,source,fragment,fragment_hash,decision_key='local-oracle-v2')
            identity=s.execute(sa.text('SELECT session_user,current_user,pg_backend_pid(),pg_current_xact_id()::text')).one()

            s.flush();b.check('L_CANDIDATE_SERVICE',True)

            s.execute(sa.text('SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE'));b.check('L_0028_MATERIALIZER',True)
            s.execute(sa.text('SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED'))

            case=create_review_case(s,directive_id=directive,proposal_id=candidate.proposal.id,actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key='local-case',expected_authorization_observation_hash=observed['authorizationObservationHashes']['create_ad_v4_review_case'],expected_input_identity_hash=observed['inputIdentityHash']);b.check('L_REVIEW_CASE_CREATED',True)
            draft=save_review_draft(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key='local-draft',expected_authorization_observation_hash=case['authorizationObservationHashes']['save_ad_v4_review_draft'],expected_input_identity_hash=case['inputIdentityHash'],expected_predecessor_event_hash=case['latestEventHash'],annotations=[{'pointer':'/requirements','text':'Remediate'}],intended_action='reject');b.check('L_REVIEW_DRAFT_SAVED',True)
            requested=request_review(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key='local-request',expected_authorization_observation_hash=draft['authorizationObservationHashes']['request_ad_v4_review'],expected_input_identity_hash=draft['inputIdentityHash'],expected_predecessor_event_hash=draft['latestEventHash'],draft_revision_id=draft['draftRevisionId']);b.check('L_REVIEW_REQUESTED',True)

def run(destination,current_model):
    root,manifest=extract_bundle(destination);kills=[];b=load_base(root)
    b.OUT['format']='platform-local-oracle-2';b.OUT['bundleMutationKills']=kills
    b.OUT['bundleMutationExecution']='SEPARATE_HOST_VERIFY_BUNDLE_TWO_REPLAYS; native execution still validates full pinned archive and extraction'
    try:
        p=authority(b,root,manifest)
        b.bootstrap_and_migrate();funcs=b.cutover(p);b.t_r_fixture(p);b.grant_and_guard_probes(p,funcs)
        historical_workflows(b)
        b.OUT['observations']['completedLifecycle']='AUTHENTICATED_L_CANDIDATE_APP_OBLIGATION_CASE_DRAFT_REQUEST_REJECTION_COMMIT_AND_VERIFY'
        relationships(b,p);t_mutations(b)
        # The negative fixture is a second ephemeral directory. Its 211 other
        # files come from the same durable archive, never current working tree.
        negative=root.with_name(root.name+'-current-negative');need(not negative.exists(),'NEGATIVE_DEST_EXISTS')
        import shutil
        shutil.copytree(root,negative)
        current=Path(current_model);need(not current.is_symlink() and sha(current.read_bytes())==CURRENT_HASH,'NEGATIVE_CURRENT_MODEL_HASH')
        (negative/MODEL).write_bytes(current.read_bytes())
        contract=REPO/NEGATIVE_CONTRACT
        need(not contract.is_symlink() and sha(contract.read_bytes())==NEGATIVE_CONTRACT_HASH,'NEGATIVE_CONTRACT_HASH')
        # This read-only JSON enables current mapper import ONLY. It is absent
        # from positive bundle/extraction and is never executed as migration.
        (negative/NEGATIVE_CONTRACT).write_bytes(contract.read_bytes())
        with b.conn(b.ROLES['M']) as m:
            before=b.native_catalog(m)
            count_names=('ad_v4_candidate_proposals','ad_v4_candidate_app_projections','ad_v4_candidate_obligation_projections','ad_v4_review_cases','ad_v4_review_draft_revisions','ad_v4_review_requests','ad_v4_review_rejections','ad_v4_signoff_events','ad_v4_review_case_events')
            before_counts={n:b.scalar(m,'SELECT count(*) FROM public.'+b.ident(n)) for n in count_names}
        completed=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-B',str(Path(__file__).resolve()),'--negative-current',str(negative),'--role',b.ROLES['L']],cwd=negative,env={**os.environ,'PYTHONPATH':str(negative/'backend')+':'+str(negative/'backend/tests')},text=True,capture_output=True,timeout=60)
        need(completed.returncode==0,'NEGATIVE_CHILD_FAILED:'+completed.stderr)
        negative_result=strict(completed.stdout);b.check('CURRENT_BINARY_0029_REJECTED_42703',negative_result['status']=='EXPECTED_REJECTION' and negative_result['sqlstate']=='42703')
        b.OUT['observations']['requiredCurrentBinaryNegative']=negative_result
        with b.conn(b.ROLES['M']) as m:
            after_counts={n:b.scalar(m,'SELECT count(*) FROM public.'+b.ident(n)) for n in count_names}
            b.check('NEGATIVE_EXACT_CATALOG_UNCHANGED',before==b.native_catalog(m))
            b.check('NEGATIVE_EXACT_ROWS_UNCHANGED',before_counts==after_counts,after_counts)
            b.check('COMPLETE_COMMITTED_LIFECYCLE_COUNTS',list(after_counts.values())==[1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,4],after_counts)
        verify_extraction(root,manifest)
        b.check('BUNDLE_EXTRACTION_STILL_EXACT',True)

    except Exception as exc:

        b.OUT['blocker']={'phase':b.PHASE,'type':type(exc).__name__,'sqlstate':getattr(orig,'sqlstate',None),'message':str(orig),'traceback':traceback.format_exc()}
    b.OUT['counts']={'passedSubcases':len(b.OUT['checks']),'bundleMutationKills':len(kills),'wholeFamilyPass':0}
    b.OUT['boundary']='Only historical 0029 binary positive. Current partial binary negative only. No 0030 successors, RDS/IAM/TLS/secret rotation, complete platform state/inverse/identity lifecycle, hostile TEMP security, production Alembic injection or deployment approval.'
    print(json.dumps(b.OUT,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),default=str))


def validate_native_result(candidate,reference):
    """Strict result mutations use the OTHER fresh replay as reference.

    Not a production authorization validator or a self-approval mechanism.
    Exact native positive assertions and version-negative diagnostics are
    required in addition to reference tuple/coverage equality.
    """
    need(set(candidate)==set(reference),'RESULT_ROOT_KEYS')
    need(candidate['format']=='platform-local-oracle-2' and candidate['status']=='VERSIONED_LOCAL_EVIDENCE_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW' and candidate['blocker'] is None,'RESULT_STATUS')
    checks=candidate['checks'];expected=reference['checks']
    need([x['id'] for x in checks]==[x['id'] for x in expected] and len({x['id'] for x in checks})==len(checks),'RESULT_CHECK_ORDER_OR_COVERAGE')
    need(all(set(x)=={'id','status','evidence'} and x['status']=='PASS' for x in checks),'RESULT_CHECK_SHAPE_OR_STATUS')
    need(candidate['counts']=={'passedSubcases':len(checks),'bundleMutationKills':0,'wholeFamilyPass':0},'RESULT_COUNTS')
    ob=candidate['observations'];bundle=ob['historicalBundle']
    need(bundle['archiveSha256']==ARCHIVE_HASH and bundle['manifestSha256']==MANIFEST_HASH and bundle['files']==212 and bundle['models']==113 and bundle['relationships']==192,'RESULT_BUNDLE_BINDING')
    neg=ob['requiredCurrentBinaryNegative']
    need(neg['status']=='EXPECTED_REJECTION' and neg['sqlstate']=='42703' and neg['modelSha256']==CURRENT_HASH and neg['importOnlyContractSha256']==NEGATIVE_CONTRACT_HASH and neg['source']=='backend/app/services/ad_v4_reviews.py:758' and 'ad_v4_review_case_events.candidate_decision_id' in neg['query'],'RESULT_VERSION_NEGATIVE')
    need(ob['completedLifecycle']=='AUTHENTICATED_L_CANDIDATE_APP_OBLIGATION_CASE_DRAFT_REQUEST_REJECTION_COMMIT_AND_VERIFY','RESULT_LIFECYCLE')
    rel=ob['nativeMigratedRelationships']
    need(len(rel)==576 and [x['id'] for x in rel]==[x['id'] for x in reference['observations']['nativeMigratedRelationships']],'RESULT_RELATIONSHIP_COVERAGE')
    need(all(set(x)=={'id','sourceRows','nonemptySourceRows','status'} and x['status']==('PASS_NONEMPTY' if x['nonemptySourceRows']>0 else 'NOT_RUN_NO_VALID_DOMAIN_ROWS') for x in rel),'RESULT_EMPTY_RELATIONSHIP_FALSE_PASS')
    return True


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument('--build-bundle');parser.add_argument('--verify-bundle',action='store_true');parser.add_argument('--run');parser.add_argument('--current-model');parser.add_argument('--negative-current');parser.add_argument('--role');args=parser.parse_args()
    if args.build_bundle:build_bundle(args.build_bundle)
    elif args.verify_bundle:print(json.dumps({'mutationKills':mutations(),'archiveSha256':ARCHIVE_HASH,'manifestSha256':MANIFEST_HASH}))
    elif args.negative_current:negative_current(Path(args.negative_current),args.role)
    elif args.run:run(args.run,args.current_model)
    else:parser.error('explicit mode required')


if __name__=='__main__':main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded local evidence, never a platform installer or production validator.

Run only in the cached backend image sharing a --network none PG16 container's
network namespace; use an exact copied-input fixture. Emits JSON to stdout. No
file writes, downloads, subprocesses, production env.py execution, or 0030 DDL.
Builder /root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor; requested Astra xhigh;
actual model not exposed by runtime; effort not exposed. Independent review
required. A failed native assertion stops the experiment; grants are not widened.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import sys
import traceback

from alembic.config import Config
from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
from alembic.operations import Operations
from alembic.script import ScriptDirectory
import psycopg
from psycopg import sql
import sqlalchemy
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
RUN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
# The cached image has older /app modules: copied repository source must win
# even under python -c/runpy, whose sys.path[0] otherwise points at image cwd.
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / "backend"), str(ROOT / "backend/tests")]
DB = "paprnav_platform_local_oracle"
D = "platform_oracle_d"
FIXTURE_PASSWORD = "disposable-network-none-not-a-deployment-credential"
INPUTS = {
    "platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.json": "a3bff43719fc6db031a0bbb54cef32b83839eddf88013d35e7cdcbfbfdf80a31",
    "platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.schema.json": "2a2c11e5e4def0c9b2cecadf798f047dbb68576d14249af11070fd4198d7d2b0",
    "platform-runtime-authority-relationship-results.json": "37fa652e45ede9112bca3e5f97ad414a207d44338deaecae9946c1038ae13163",
    "adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.md": "7fe6b84eb8cc3b65f71aca7cee186af0672a1950fbe311d9ed5cb30bcfd13e3a",
}
OUT = {"format": "platform-local-oracle-1", "status": "RUNNING", "inputs": [],
       "checks": [], "observations": {}, "blocker": None}
PHASE = "authority_preflight"
ROLES = {"D": D, "B": "postgres"}


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def strict(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise ValueError("DUPLICATE_KEY:" + key)
        result[key] = value
    return result


def check(case, condition, evidence=None):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(case + ": " + repr(evidence))
    OUT["checks"].append({"id": case, "status": "PASS", "evidence": evidence})


def ident(value):
    return '"' + value.replace('"', '""') + '"'


def relation(value):
    return ".".join(ident(v) for v in value.split("."))


def conn(role, database=DB, autocommit=False):
    return psycopg.connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=5432, dbname=database,
                          user=role, password=FIXTURE_PASSWORD,
                          autocommit=autocommit, connect_timeout=5)


def engine(role):
    return create_engine(sqlalchemy.URL.create("postgresql+psycopg", username=role,
                         password=FIXTURE_PASSWORD, host="127.0.0.1", database=DB),
                         connect_args={"options": "-c statement_timeout=30000 -c lock_timeout=2000"})


def scalar(c, statement, args=()):
    return c.execute(statement, args).fetchone()[0]


def deny(c, case, statement, state="42501", message=None):
    c.execute("SAVEPOINT negative_probe")
    try:
        c.execute(statement).fetchall() if statement.startswith("SELECT") else c.execute(statement)
    except psycopg.Error as exc:
        observed = {"sqlstate": exc.sqlstate, "message": exc.diag.message_primary}
        c.execute("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT negative_probe")
        check(case, exc.sqlstate == state and (message is None or message in str(exc)), observed)
    else:
        c.execute("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT negative_probe")
        raise AssertionError(case + ": forbidden operation succeeded")
    c.execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT negative_probe")


def edges(c):
    rows = c.execute("""SELECT r.rolname,m.rolname,g.rolname,a.admin_option,
        a.inherit_option,a.set_option FROM pg_catalog.pg_auth_members a
        JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles r ON r.oid=a.roleid
        JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles m ON m.oid=a.member
        JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles g ON g.oid=a.grantor
        WHERE r.rolname = ANY(%s) ORDER BY 1,2,3""", (list(ROLES.values()),)).fetchall()
    reverse = {v: k for k, v in ROLES.items()}
    return sorted([[reverse.get(a,a),reverse.get(b,b),reverse.get(g,g),ad,inh,st]
                   for a,b,g,ad,inh,st in rows])


def native_catalog(c):
    # Complete raw rows, including native explicit ACLs, retained for bounded
    # fixture state. No claim this substitutes for the future closed snapshot.
    queries = {
        "database": "SELECT row_to_json(d) FROM pg_catalog.pg_database d WHERE datname=current_database()",
        "namespace": "SELECT row_to_json(n) FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace n WHERE nspname='public'",
        "classes": "SELECT row_to_json(c) FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY c.oid",
        "attributes": "SELECT row_to_json(a) FROM pg_catalog.pg_attribute a JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c ON c.oid=a.attrelid JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY a.attrelid,a.attnum",
        "constraints": "SELECT row_to_json(k) FROM pg_catalog.pg_constraint k JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=k.connamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY k.oid",
        "triggers": "SELECT row_to_json(t) FROM pg_catalog.pg_trigger t JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c ON c.oid=t.tgrelid JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY t.oid",
        "functions": "SELECT row_to_json(p) FROM pg_catalog.pg_proc p JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY p.oid",
        "defaults": "SELECT row_to_json(d) FROM pg_catalog.pg_default_acl d ORDER BY d.oid",
    }
    return {k:[r[0] for r in c.execute(q).fetchall()] for k,q in queries.items()}


def load_authority():
    for name, expected in INPUTS.items():
        p = RUN / name
        if p.is_symlink() or not p.is_file():
            raise ValueError("AUTHORITY_PATH_SUBSTITUTION:" + name)
        data = p.read_bytes()
        check("AUTHORITY_SHA256:" + name, digest(data) == expected)
        OUT["inputs"].append({"path": name, "bytes": len(data), "sha256": digest(data)})
    profile = json.loads((RUN / "platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.json").read_bytes(), object_pairs_hook=strict)
    schema = json.loads((RUN / "platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.schema.json").read_bytes(), object_pairs_hook=strict)
    check("SCHEMA_CLOSED_CONST_SECTIONS", schema.get("additionalProperties") is False
          and set(schema["required"]) == set(profile)
          and all(schema["properties"][k].get("const") == v for k,v in profile.items()))
    json.loads((RUN / "platform-runtime-authority-relationship-results.json").read_bytes(), object_pairs_hook=strict)
    check("PRISTINE_EXPECTED_COUNTS", [len(profile["sourceGrants"]),len(profile["functionGrants"]),len(profile["oracleCases"])] == [113,69,22])
    for row in profile['relationshipAuthority']['callerFiles']:
        path=ROOT/row['path']
        check('CALLER_SOURCE_HASH:'+row['path'],not path.is_symlink() and digest(path.read_bytes())==row['sha256'])
    check('MODEL_SOURCE_HASH',digest((ROOT/'backend/app/models/core.py').read_bytes())==profile['relationshipAuthority']['modelSha256'])
    for row in profile['inventory']['regularFiles']:
        if row['path'].startswith('backend/app/db/migrations/versions/') and '_0030_' not in row['path']:
            check('MIGRATION_SOURCE_HASH:'+row['path'],digest((ROOT/row['path']).read_bytes())==row['sha256'])
    return profile


def bootstrap_and_migrate():
    global PHASE
    PHASE = "disposable_bootstrap"
    check("NO_DOTENV", os.environ.get("PAPRNAV_DISABLE_DOTENV") == "1")
    with conn("postgres", "postgres", True) as b:
        version = scalar(b, "SHOW server_version")
        check("POSTGRES_16", int(scalar(b, "SHOW server_version_num")) // 10000 == 16, version)
        check("EMPTY_DATABASE_NAME", not scalar(b, "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname=%s)",(DB,)))
        check("EMPTY_D_ROLE", not scalar(b, "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=%s)",(D,)))
        b.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE ROLE {} LOGIN NOSUPERUSER CREATEDB CREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOBYPASSRLS NOREPLICATION PASSWORD {}").format(sql.Identifier(D),sql.Literal(FIXTURE_PASSWORD)))
    with conn(D, "postgres", True) as d:
        d.execute(f"CREATE DATABASE {ident(DB)} OWNER {ident(D)}")
    PHASE = "pristine_0029_single_connection_shim"
    e = engine(D)
    config = Config()
    config.set_main_option("script_location", str(ROOT / "backend/app/db/migrations"))
    script = ScriptDirectory.from_config(config)
    revisions = list(reversed(list(script.walk_revisions(base="base", head="20260913_0029"))))
    observed = []
    with e.begin() as c:
        context = MigrationContext.configure(c, opts={"transactional_ddl": True})
        with Operations.context(context):
            for revision in revisions:
                observed.append([revision.revision,*c.execute(text("SELECT pg_backend_pid(),pg_current_xact_id()::text,session_user,current_user")).one()])
                revision.module.upgrade()
            context.stamp(script,"20260913_0029")
    e.dispose()
    OUT["observations"]["migrationConnections"] = observed
    check("ALL_29_REVISIONS", len(observed) == 29)
    check("SHIM_ONE_D_PID_XID", len({(x[1],x[2],x[3],x[4]) for x in observed}) == 1)


def cutover(p):
    global PHASE
    PHASE = "native_0029_catalog"
    with conn(D) as d:
        dboid = scalar(d,"SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database()")
        nonce = secrets.token_hex(16)
        for symbol in ("M","L","T","R"):
            ROLES[symbol] = f"pn4b_{symbol.lower()}_{dboid:08x}_{nonce}"
        check("ROLE_NAMES_48_BYTES", all(len(ROLES[k].encode()) == 48 for k in ("M","L","T","R")))
        tables = d.execute("SELECT c.relname,r.rolname FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid=c.relowner WHERE n.nspname='public' AND c.relkind='r' ORDER BY 1").fetchall()
        expected = sorted([g["relation"].split(".")[1] for g in p["sourceGrants"]]+["alembic_version"])
        check("113_TABLES_PLUS_REVISION_OWNED_D", tables == [(n,D) for n in expected])
        funcs = d.execute("SELECT p.oid,p.proname,pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid),pg_get_functiondef(p.oid),p.prosecdef,r.rolname FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid=p.proowner WHERE n.nspname='public' ORDER BY p.proname,3").fetchall()
        check("69_FUNCTIONS", len(funcs)==69)
        function_map={(g["name"],g["arguments"]):g for g in p["functionGrants"]}
        for oid,name,args,definition,definer,owner in funcs:
            g = function_map[("public."+name,args)]
            check("FUNCTION_BASELINE:"+name, digest(definition.encode())==g["definitionSha256"] and not definer and owner==D)
        check("ZERO_SEQUENCES",scalar(d,"SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' AND c.relkind='S'")==0)
        pre=native_catalog(d)
        check("PUBLIC_PG_DATABASE_OWNER",scalar(d,"SELECT pg_get_userbyid(nspowner) FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname='public'")=="pg_database_owner")
        PHASE="forward_profile_cutover"
        d.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(71604029)")
        d.execute("SET LOCAL createrole_self_grant=''")
        m,l=ROLES["M"],ROLES["L"]
        attrs="LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB CREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOBYPASSRLS NOREPLICATION VALID UNTIL 'infinity'"
        d.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE ROLE {} "+attrs+" PASSWORD {}").format(sql.Identifier(m),sql.Literal(FIXTURE_PASSWORD)))
        check("M_CREATOR_ADMIN_ONLY",edges(d)==[["M","D","B",True,False,False]])
        d.execute(f"GRANT {ident(m)} TO {ident(D)} WITH ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE GRANTED BY {ident(D)}")
        check("D_EXACT_SET_ONLY_EDGE",edges(d)==[["M","D","B",True,False,False],["M","D","D",False,False,True]])
        d.execute(f"SET ROLE {ident(m)}")
        d.execute("SET LOCAL createrole_self_grant=''")
        d.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE ROLE {} LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE INHERIT NOBYPASSRLS NOREPLICATION VALID UNTIL 'infinity' PASSWORD {}").format(sql.Identifier(l),sql.Literal(FIXTURE_PASSWORD)))
        d.execute("RESET ROLE")
        d.execute(f"GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO {ident(m)}")
        for symbol in ("M","L"):
            # D has no ADMIN on L; set M for its owned creator operation.
            if symbol == "L": d.execute(f"SET ROLE {ident(m)}")
            d.execute(sql.SQL("COMMENT ON ROLE {} IS {}").format(sql.Identifier(ROLES[symbol]),sql.Literal(f"paprnav-platform-v1:{dboid:08x}:{nonce}:{symbol}")))
            if symbol == "L": d.execute("RESET ROLE")
        for table in expected:
            d.execute(f"ALTER TABLE public.{ident(table)} OWNER TO {ident(m)}")
        for oid,name,args,definition,definer,owner in funcs:
            d.execute(f"ALTER FUNCTION public.{ident(name)}({args}) OWNER TO {ident(m)}")
        d.execute(f"ALTER DATABASE {ident(DB)} OWNER TO {ident(m)}")
        d.execute(f"SET ROLE {ident(m)}")
        d.execute(f"REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM {ident(m)} RESTRICT")
        d.execute(f"REVOKE CONNECT,CREATE,TEMPORARY ON DATABASE {ident(DB)} FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute(f"GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE {ident(DB)} TO {ident(D)}")
        d.execute(f"GRANT CONNECT,TEMPORARY ON DATABASE {ident(DB)} TO {ident(l)}")
        d.execute("REVOKE CREATE,USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute(f"GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO {ident(l)}")
        for g in p["sourceGrants"]:
            d.execute(f"GRANT {','.join(g['tablePrivileges'])} ON TABLE {relation(g['relation'])} TO {ident(l)}")
            for col in g["columnPrivileges"]:
                d.execute(f"GRANT {col['privilege']}({ident(col['column'])}) ON TABLE {relation(g['relation'])} TO {ident(l)}")
        for oid,name,args,definition,definer,owner in funcs:
            sig=f"public.{ident(name)}({args})"
            d.execute(f"REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION {sig} FROM PUBLIC")
            if function_map[("public."+name,args)]["runtimeExecute"]:
                d.execute(f"GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION {sig} TO {ident(l)}")
        d.execute("ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute("ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES REVOKE USAGE ON TYPES FROM PUBLIC")
        # Test-only exact gate guard. No legacy function body is rewritten.
        moid=scalar(d,"SELECT oid FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=%s",(m,))
        gateoid=scalar(d,"SELECT 'public.ad_v4_feature_gates'::regclass::oid")
        d.execute(f"""CREATE FUNCTION public.paprnav_platform_gate_guard() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER SET search_path=pg_catalog,public,pg_temp AS $g$
        BEGIN IF session_user::text <> '{m}' OR current_user::text <> '{m}'
          OR (SELECT oid FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user) <> {moid}
          OR TG_RELID <> {gateoid} THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'PLATFORM_GATE_MUTATION_DENIED' USING ERRCODE='42501'; END IF;
          IF TG_OP='DELETE' THEN RETURN OLD; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $g$""")
        d.execute("REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.paprnav_platform_gate_guard() FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute("CREATE TRIGGER trg_platform_gate_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.ad_v4_feature_gates FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.paprnav_platform_gate_guard()")
        d.execute("ALTER TABLE public.ad_v4_feature_gates ENABLE ALWAYS TRIGGER trg_platform_gate_guard")
        d.execute("RESET ROLE")
        d.execute("ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute("ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES REVOKE USAGE ON TYPES FROM PUBLIC")
        d.execute(f"REVOKE {ident(m)} FROM {ident(D)} GRANTED BY {ident(D)} RESTRICT")
        check("STEADY_PLATFORM_MEMBERSHIPS",edges(d)==[["L","M","B",True,False,False],["M","D","B",True,False,False]])
        OUT["observations"]["preCutoverCatalogSha256"]=digest(json.dumps(pre,sort_keys=True,separators=(",",":"),default=str).encode())
        OUT["observations"]["roles"]=dict(ROLES)
        OUT["observations"]["nativeIdentity"]={"databaseOid":dboid,"roleOids":dict(d.execute("SELECT rolname,oid FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=ANY(%s)",(list(ROLES.values()),)).fetchall())}
        OUT["observations"]["functions"]= [{"name":name,"arguments":args,"oid":oid,"definitionSha256":digest(definition.encode())} for oid,name,args,definition,definer,owner in funcs]
    return funcs


def t_r_fixture(p):
    global PHASE
    PHASE="measured_T_R_source_privilege_fixture_not_0030"
    with conn(ROLES["M"]) as m:
        check("AUTHENTICATED_M",scalar(m,"SELECT session_user=current_user AND current_user=%s",(ROLES["M"],)))
        m.execute("SET LOCAL createrole_self_grant=''")
        for symbol in ("T","R"):
            m.execute(f"CREATE ROLE {ident(ROLES[symbol])} NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOBYPASSRLS NOREPLICATION PASSWORD NULL VALID UNTIL 'infinity'")
            m.execute(f"GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO {ident(ROLES[symbol])}")
        for rel in p["trustedSourceGrants"]["selectRelations"]:
            m.execute(f"GRANT SELECT ON TABLE {relation(rel)} TO {ident(ROLES['T'])}")
        for col in p["trustedSourceGrants"]["columnUpdates"]:
            m.execute(f"GRANT UPDATE({ident(col['column'])}) ON TABLE {relation(col['relation'])} TO {ident(ROLES['T'])}")
        for f in p["functionGrants"]:
            if f["trustedExecute"]:m.execute(f"GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION {f['name']}({f['arguments']}) TO {ident(ROLES['T'])}")
        m.execute(f"GRANT {ident(ROLES['R'])} TO {ident(ROLES['L'])} WITH ADMIN FALSE,INHERIT TRUE,SET FALSE GRANTED BY {ident(ROLES['M'])}")
        expected=[["L","M","B",True,False,False],["M","D","B",True,False,False],["R","L","M",False,True,False],["R","M","B",True,False,False],["T","M","B",True,False,False]]
        check("FIVE_STEADY_EDGES",edges(m)==expected,edges(m))
        check("T_R_NOLOGIN", scalar(m,"SELECT bool_and(NOT rolcanlogin AND NOT rolsuper AND NOT rolcreatedb AND NOT rolcreaterole AND NOT rolbypassrls AND NOT rolreplication AND NOT rolinherit) FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=ANY(%s)",([ROLES['T'],ROLES['R']],)))


def grant_and_guard_probes(p,funcs):
    global PHASE
    PHASE="authenticated_L_source_grants_and_guard"
    try:
        bad=psycopg.connect(host="127.0.0.1",dbname=DB,user=ROLES['L'],password="intentionally-incorrect-fixture-password",connect_timeout=5)
    except psycopg.OperationalError as exc:
        check("L_WRONG_PASSWORD_REJECTED","password authentication failed" in str(exc))
    else:
        bad.close()
        raise AssertionError("FIXTURE_AUTH_NOT_SCRAM: wrong password connected")
    with conn(ROLES["L"]) as l:
        check("AUTHENTICATED_L",scalar(l,"SELECT session_user=current_user AND current_user=%s",(ROLES["L"],)))
        for g in p["sourceGrants"]:
            for priv in ("SELECT","INSERT","UPDATE","DELETE","TRUNCATE","REFERENCES","TRIGGER"):
                actual=scalar(l,"SELECT has_table_privilege(current_user,%s,%s)",(g['relation'],priv))
                check(f"L_TABLE_ACL:{g['relation']}:{priv}",actual==(priv in g["tablePrivileges"]))
            l.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {relation(g['relation'])} LIMIT 0")
            check("L_SELECT_EXECUTES:"+g["relation"],True)
            for col in g['columnPrivileges']:
                check(f"L_COLUMN_ACL:{g['relation']}:{col['column']}",scalar(l,"SELECT has_column_privilege(current_user,%s,%s,'UPDATE')",(g['relation'],col['column'])))
        for oid,name,args,definition,definer,owner in funcs:
            expected=next(g['runtimeExecute'] for g in p['functionGrants'] if g['name']=='public.'+name and g['arguments']==args)
            check("L_FUNCTION_EXECUTE:"+name,scalar(l,"SELECT has_function_privilege(current_user,%s,'EXECUTE')",(oid,))==expected)
        for r in ("D","M","T","R"):
            deny(l,"L_CANNOT_SET:"+r,f"SET ROLE {ident(ROLES[r])}")
        deny(l,"L_CANNOT_CREATE_PUBLIC","CREATE TABLE public.forbidden_runtime_table(id integer)")
        l.execute("CREATE TEMP TABLE local_runtime_cache_probe(id integer)")
        check("L_TEMP_ALLOWED",True)
        for lock in ("SHARE","UPDATE"):
            rows=l.execute("SELECT gate_key FROM public.ad_v4_feature_gates FOR "+lock).fetchall()
            check("L_GATE_FOR_"+lock,len(rows)>0,{"rows":len(rows)})
        deny(l,"L_GATE_NOOP_UPDATE_GUARD","UPDATE public.ad_v4_feature_gates SET gate_key=gate_key",message="PLATFORM_GATE_MUTATION_DENIED")
        deny(l,"L_GATE_ENABLED_UPDATE","UPDATE public.ad_v4_feature_gates SET enabled=enabled")
        deny(l,"L_GATE_DELETE","DELETE FROM public.ad_v4_feature_gates")
        deny(l,"L_GATE_TRUNCATE","TRUNCATE public.ad_v4_feature_gates")
        deny(l,"L_GATE_SETTER","SELECT public.paprnav_set_v4_feature_gate('validator2_write_enabled',true,'forbidden')")
        deny(l,"L_GATE_DISABLE_TRIGGER","ALTER TABLE public.ad_v4_feature_gates DISABLE TRIGGER trg_platform_gate_guard")
        deny(l,"L_REPLICATION_ROLE","SET LOCAL session_replication_role=replica")
        l.rollback()
    with conn(ROLES['M']) as m:
        for gate in ("validator2_write_enabled","materializer3a_enabled","materializer3b_enabled","reviewer4_draft_enabled","reviewer4_decision_enabled"):
            m.execute("SELECT public.paprnav_set_v4_feature_gate(%s,true,'local-oracle-M')",(gate,))
        check("AUTHENTICATED_M_GATE_SETTER",True)
        for role in ("D","M","L","T","R"):
            rights=[scalar(m,"SELECT has_database_privilege(%s,current_database(),%s)",(ROLES[role],p)) for p in ("CONNECT","CREATE","TEMPORARY")]
            expected={"D":[True,False,False],"M":[True,True,True],"L":[True,False,True],"T":[False,False,False],"R":[False,False,False]}[role]
            check("DATABASE_RIGHTS:"+role,rights==expected,rights)
        check("PUBLIC_DATABASE_EMPTY",scalar(m,"SELECT count(*) FROM pg_database d,LATERAL aclexplode(d.datacl) a WHERE d.datname=current_database() AND a.grantee=0")==0)


def workflows():
    global PHASE
    PHASE="M_fixture_then_authenticated_L_candidate_materializers_review"
    for key in ("PAPRNAV_AD_V4_VALIDATOR2_WRITES_ENABLED","PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE3A_ROUTES_ENABLED","PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE3B_ROUTES_ENABLED","PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE4_READS_ENABLED","PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE4_DRAFTS_ENABLED","PAPRNAV_AD_V4_SLICE4_DECISIONS_ENABLED"):
        os.environ[key]="true"
    from app.core.config import get_settings
    import app.services.ad_v4_candidates as candidate_module
    check("EXACT_COPIED_SERVICE_SOURCE",Path(candidate_module.__file__).resolve()==ROOT/'backend/app/services/ad_v4_candidates.py')
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    from test_ad_v4_postgres import _seed,_request
    from app.models.core import User
    from app.services.ad_v4_candidates import store_v4_candidate,VALIDATOR_VERSION_V2
    from app.services.ad_v4_applicability import materialize_applicability
    from app.services.ad_v4_obligation_persistence import materialize_obligations
    from app.services.ad_v4_reviews import review_proposal_observation,create_review_case,save_review_draft,request_review,reject_review_case,verified_review_case
    me,le=engine(ROLES['M']),engine(ROLES['L'])
    try:
        with Session(me) as s:seed=_seed(s)
        user,membership,directive,document,source,fragment,fragment_hash=seed
        with Session(le) as s:
            actor=s.get(User,user)
            parsed=_request(directive,document,source,fragment,fragment_hash,decision_key="local-oracle-v2")
            candidate=store_v4_candidate(s,directive_id=directive,parsed=parsed,actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-oracle-candidate",validator_version=VALIDATOR_VERSION_V2)
            s.flush()
            check("L_CANDIDATE_SERVICE",True)
            app=materialize_applicability(s,directive_id=directive,proposal_id=candidate.proposal.id,actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-oracle-app")
            s.flush()
            check("L_0027_MATERIALIZER",True)
            ob=materialize_obligations(s,directive_id=directive,proposal_id=candidate.proposal.id,app_projection_id=app.projection.id,actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-oracle-obligation")
            s.execute(text("SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE"))
            check("L_0028_MATERIALIZER",True)
            observed=review_proposal_observation(s,directive_id=directive,proposal_id=candidate.proposal.id,actor=actor,membership_id=membership)
            case=create_review_case(s,directive_id=directive,proposal_id=candidate.proposal.id,actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-case",expected_authorization_observation_hash=observed['authorizationObservationHashes']['create_ad_v4_review_case'],expected_input_identity_hash=observed['inputIdentityHash'])
            draft=save_review_draft(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-draft",expected_authorization_observation_hash=case['authorizationObservationHashes']['save_ad_v4_review_draft'],expected_input_identity_hash=case['inputIdentityHash'],expected_predecessor_event_hash=case['latestEventHash'],annotations=[{"pointer":"/requirements","text":"Remediate"}],intended_action="reject")
            requested=request_review(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-request",expected_authorization_observation_hash=draft['authorizationObservationHashes']['request_ad_v4_review'],expected_input_identity_hash=draft['inputIdentityHash'],expected_predecessor_event_hash=draft['latestEventHash'],draft_revision_id=draft['draftRevisionId'])
            rejected=reject_review_case(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,idempotency_key="local-reject",expected_authorization_observation_hash=requested['authorizationObservationHashes']['reject_ad_v4_review'],expected_input_identity_hash=requested['inputIdentityHash'],expected_predecessor_event_hash=requested['latestEventHash'],expected_request_id=requested['reviewRequestId'],reason_codes=['remediation_requested'],explanation='Candidate requires remediation.')
            s.execute(text("SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE"))
            s.commit()
            verified=verified_review_case(s,case_id=case['caseId'],actor=actor,membership_id=membership,event_limit=2,event_offset=1)
            check("L_0029_REJECTION_LIFECYCLE",rejected['state']==verified['state']=='rejected' and verified['eventTotal']==4)
        PHASE="T_narrow_column_lock_and_immutability"
        with conn(ROLES['M']) as m:
            m.execute(f"GRANT {ident(ROLES['T'])} TO {ident(ROLES['M'])} WITH ADMIN FALSE,INHERIT FALSE,SET TRUE GRANTED BY {ident(ROLES['M'])}")
            m.execute(f"SET ROLE {ident(ROLES['T'])}")
            check("T_FROM_AUTHENTICATED_M_NOT_SUPERUSER",scalar(m,"SELECT session_user=%s AND current_user=%s",(ROLES['M'],ROLES['T'])))
            for rel in ('ad_v4_candidate_app_projections','ad_v4_candidate_obligation_projections','ad_v4_review_requests'):
                check("T_LOCK_NONEMPTY:"+rel,len(m.execute(f"SELECT id FROM public.{ident(rel)} FOR SHARE").fetchall())==1)
                deny(m,"T_IMMUTABLE_NOOP:"+rel,f"UPDATE public.{ident(rel)} SET id=id",state="P0001",message="immutable")
                deny(m,"T_DELETE_DENIED:"+rel,f"DELETE FROM public.{ident(rel)}")
            m.execute("RESET ROLE")
            m.execute(f"REVOKE {ident(ROLES['T'])} FROM {ident(ROLES['M'])} GRANTED BY {ident(ROLES['M'])} RESTRICT")
            check("T_TEMP_EDGE_REMOVED",not any(x[:3]==['T','M','M'] for x in edges(m)))
    finally:
        me.dispose();le.dispose()


def main():
    global PHASE
    p=load_authority()
    OUT["observations"]["runtime"]={"python":sys.version.split()[0],"sqlalchemy":sqlalchemy.__version__,"psycopg":psycopg.__version__}
    try:
        bootstrap_and_migrate()
        funcs=cutover(p)
        t_r_fixture(p)
        grant_and_guard_probes(p,funcs)
        workflows()
        OUT["status"]="BOUNDED_LOCAL_EVIDENCE_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW"
    except Exception as exc:
        original=getattr(exc,"orig",exc)
        OUT["status"]="LOCAL_PLATFORM_BLOCKER_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW"
        OUT["blocker"]={"phase":PHASE,"type":type(exc).__name__,"sqlstate":getattr(original,"sqlstate",None),"message":str(original),"traceback":traceback.format_exc()}
        if getattr(original,'sqlstate',None)=='42703':
            OUT['blocker']['id']='PLATFORM-LOCAL-B-001'
            # Read-only post-failure diagnosis, not continuation past blocker.
            with conn(ROLES['M']) as m:
