`backend/tests`, `backend/alembic.ini`, this runner, and the four exact bound
inputs into `/repo` using `docker cp -`. Inputs were never edited in the
repository. Python runs with `-B`, `PAPRNAV_DISABLE_DOTENV=1`, cwd `/repo`, and
`PYTHONPATH=/repo/backend:/repo/backend/tests`. `runpy.run_path(...,
run_name='__main__')` captures stdout, strictly parseable JSON; stdout was
compacted in memory before retrieval, not written as another run artifact.
The runner itself also places copied source first and verifies its import path.

Docker inspection confirmed network `none`, zero published ports, tmpfs data,
and the runner sharing only its paired PG network namespace. Fixed fixture
passwords are public throwaway test values, not deployment credentials.

The initial host read-only bind mount failed at Python startup (`Errno 24`).
The first tar copy then rejected macOS xattrs, corrected by `--no-xattrs`.
Development runs `01`/`02` uncovered only harness return-field and import-path
errors; they were discarded. Run `03` first reproduced the actual blocker.
Runs `04`/`05` use identical final runner bytes and both reproduce it.

The normalized logical projection is byte-identical across final runs:
`c79def0feb07523b393346cd17463683fbfd62247810160c0accf8b07532ced3`.
Normalization replaces exact random role names with logical aliases in checks
only and compares checks, counts, blocker classification/message, all family
statuses and read-only diagnosis. UTF-8 compact JSON preserves the recorded
`logicalReplayProjection` key order. Raw PIDs/XIDs/OIDs/nonces/catalog hashes
and fixture UUID tracebacks remain in both raw results but are excluded from
the deterministic claim. They are not rewritten into fake fixed identities.

regular files and five symlinks**, gathered from git's cached/untracked,
non-ignored path inventory before any local-oracle write. Every byte hash,
size and symlink target remained equal after native work; final validation
repeats that comparison after these three artifacts exist. The scope excludes
ignored paths; no broader preservation claim is made. Existing run artifacts,
production, partial migration, findings/state/reviews/packet and git staging
were not changed. Exactly the three authorized local files were added.

All ten named fixture containers from attempts `01`–`05` were removed; final
`docker ps -a --filter name=paprnav-platform-` returned no entries. Only
disposable test containers and tmpfs data were destroyed; those fixtures cannot
be recovered but can be replayed. No user database or repository data was
deleted.

# Platform relationship oracle v2

Status: **DESIGN_PROPOSAL_ONLY_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**.

## Model routing

Builder `/root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor`; requested GPT-6 Astra,
xhigh. Actual model: model not exposed by runtime. Actual effort: effort not
exposed. Trigger: implicit ORM authorization-access family after v1 FAIL.
Builder results are evidence, not independent review or finding closure.

## Binding and independent expected result

Profile SHA-256:
`a3bff43719fc6db031a0bbb54cef32b83839eddf88013d35e7cdcbfbfdf80a31`.
Schema SHA-256:
`2a2c11e5e4def0c9b2cecadf798f047dbb68576d14249af11070fd4198d7d2b0`.
Oracle SHA-256:
`88baae7ae1903db2afe8d7b85d46cabec99b087d302ab1a089588a238ef84168`.
Result SHA-256:
`37fa652e45ede9112bca3e5f97ad414a207d44338deaecae9946c1038ae13163`.

The oracle reads actual current model/caller source and the immutable installed
0029 function catalog. It configures SQLAlchemy mappers, cross-checks all 192
declarations, resolves FKs including dynamically installed constraints, checks
back-populated inverses, and derives complete conservative reachability. It
independently enumerates the filesystem caller set so adding a caller cannot
remain hidden by the frozen v1 file list. It distinguishes declaration facts,
exact loader syntax, conservative attribute candidates and actual measured
SQL. No const-schema equality substitutes for these joins.

`relationshipAuthority` contains source paths, exact line spans/text hashes,
expression hashes/previews, mapper directions, joined columns, secondary
tables, loader modes, FK resolution, query/helper facts and closure results.
Expression previews may be truncated to 256 characters; full expression and
source-line hashes remain bound to available source. No truncated preview is
treated as an executable oracle or authority replacement.

All 113 source-table grants are rejoined to conservative caller reachability.
The 47 distinct relationship target tables receive omission and native denial
tests. The absence of secondary relationships is verified; mapped association
objects, including `ADSupersession`, are ordinary mapped target tables, not
skipped because they are not named in direct caller imports. Four view-only
and composite joins are included. SQLAlchemy's mapper and loader behavior is
the primary framework basis, pinned here to the installed 2.0.52 package.
[Mapper inspection](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/mapping_styles.html#inspection-of-mapper-objects),
[relationship loaders](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/queryguide/relationships.html)

## Positive corpus

Every one of 192 reached mapper directions runs under lazy, select-in and
joined loaders, producing 576 nonempty cases. Actual model classes and mapper
join expressions are used. Fixture tables reproduce column types/identities
but deliberately omit production FK/check/trigger constraints, isolating SQL
reachability and privilege behavior from unrelated domain-validation setup.
No production database or production migration is used.

Three additional bounded source fragments are executed:

1. The SELECT expression extracted from `released_signed_extractions` in
   `ad_release.py`, including nested select-in relationships.
2. The SELECT expression extracted from `collect_issue_specs` in
   `ad_reconciliation.py`, including both supersession directions.
3. `extraction.directive.superseded_by_edges` from matching's read path,
   evaluated on the release-loaded fixture row.

These are not whole service function executions: release's downstream writes,
matching decisions, reconciliation side effects and signed packet semantics
are not claimed tested. The fixture has three directives and two edges:
A supersedes B, C supersedes A. Expected endpoint pairs are asserted, not
merely collection truthiness. Both reverse mapper directions are also in
the 576-case matrix.

The focused PostgreSQL login is `rel_oracle_l`, LOGIN/INHERIT and
NOSUPERUSER/NOCREATEDB/NOCREATEROLE/NOBYPASSRLS/NOREPLICATION. The runner
authenticates as it and reads its native attributes. It has SELECT only on
the 113 baseline source tables and no table ownership. This proves bounded
L-like SELECT behavior, not installation of the complete D/M/L/T/R topology.
Seven paused authority models are present in metadata but receive no fixture
runtime SELECT grant and have no relationships in this graph.

## Negative corpus and diagnostics

| Mutation cohort | Count | Intended diagnostic |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Remove each distinct relationship target SELECT | 47 | `REL_MISSING_TARGET_SELECT` |
| Remove each actual mapper direction | 192 | `REL_MODEL_EDGE_MISSING_OR_CHANGED` |
| Remove each source caller-evidence edge | 1,355 | `REL_CALLER_EDGE_MISSING_OR_CHANGED` |
| Revoke each native target SELECT under PostgreSQL | 47 | SQLSTATE `42501`, intended table named |

The first three total 1,594 independently checked semantic omissions. The
expected graph is re-derived from bound source, not copied from the candidate
being mutated. Every omission has a recorded case ID and diagnostic. A
mutation failing for an unrelated reason is a failed test, not a killed case.
Native revokes use separate administrator transactions; a fresh authenticated
runtime session executes the affected joined query; each grant is restored
after the expected failure. No grant option or unrelated privilege is added.

Additional validation independently compares all 16 protected v1 platform
sections, source DML/column/owner/grantor/options, the 69 native function
signatures/body hashes, transitive helper EXECUTE requirements, all function
source references, and empty sequence/identity inventory. Unknown dynamic
text SQL, a new installed dynamic-SQL function, an unclassified mapper or new
caller file fails closed. The existing dynamic completion trigger is explicitly
bound to its 25 native trigger relation identities; its future safe-qualification
and TEMP-shadow oracle is not waived.

# Slice 4B shared platform authority oracle plan

Status: **DESIGN_PROPOSAL_ONLY_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**.

## Model routing

Builder `/root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor`; requested GPT-6 Astra,
xhigh. Actual model: model not exposed by runtime. Actual effort: effort not
exposed. Trigger: production-compatible authority and migration oracle after
the third unsuccessful ACL loop. No self-review or approval claimed.

## Declarative binding and independence

This plan binds `platform-runtime-authority-profile-v1.json`, SHA-256
`d0aeb528728de740c16bed931459f8c0d6dee2b8f9edf3bab4df36ee74c8d0fc`.
Its `oracleCases` array is the ordered, closed set of 22 oracle families;
roles, native edges, callers, grants, proposed deviations and diagnostics come
from that JSON, not another SQL/Python/IaC configuration. The schema is the
exact validation mirror, SHA-256
`8b539d9a3b2af9b00e7359beb261caa0a136082a9034e594b98c5a13c1b4a00e`.

A separately assigned reviewer must inspect profile, runner and measured
results. The runner must use native catalogs and independently constructed
fixtures; importing the production validator as the expected-answer oracle
is forbidden. Expected successful state is compared completely, not merely
by a success exit code. Negative tests must fail at their intended guard and
assert SQLSTATE/message, catalog unchanged and transaction rollback. An
incidental earlier permission error is not proof of a later invariant.

## Closed case families

| IDs | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| O01–O04 | Exact roles/native grantors/flags; D CREATEDB; forward and inverse temporary edges; collision/name/OID lifecycle; independent databases |
| O05 | Every classified API/worker/operator path, dynamic/lazy SQL and trigger/helper closure under actual L; reject unclassified objects/callers |
| O06 | Actual gate locks under one-column UPDATE and owner-protected guard; direct SQL and setter/trigger/owner bypass negatives |
| O07 | Full 69 legacy + seven proposed trusted + two platform-guard function inventory; invoker temp positives and malicious temp/name/cache attacks |
| O08 | Three T lock grants from PLATFORM-CALLER-B-001; locking positives and direct immutable UPDATE negatives |
| O09–O11 | Explicit relation/column/grantor/option ACLs; PUBLIC vs quoted PUBLIC; database/schema/default policy; sealed platform state before each use/drop |
| O12–O13 | Injected M connection/PID/XID; no fallback/offline/autocommit/intermediate commit; crash/retry/lost acknowledgement resolution |
| O14–O16 | Retained relation identities; isolated schema-name and namespace-OID cohorts; compound native-DDL evidence separately |
| O17–O18 | One L transaction for source/acceptance; old/new binaries, gate ordering, app rollback and physical downgrade |
| O19 | Credential issue/rotation/revoke maintenance and failed publication/session cases |
| O20–O21 | Mandatory disposable RDS native role/catalog profile, TLS, real ECS/IAM/secret delivery and task boundaries |
| O22 | Exact subject hashes, raw evidence, reviewer separation, no self/future-review dependency or path substitution |

This table is a reading aid, not an alternate inventory. Within each family,
the JSON positive/negative list is mandatory. Every function gets a direct-call
or trigger-firing fixture; a function is not excluded because L lacks direct
EXECUTE. Legal runtime temp-cache use is a positive, not a reason to skip
malicious cache prepopulation. Trusted acceptance must never use that cache
as validation authority. New snapshot functions introduced by a later
successor must extend the inventory in that successor, not be silently assumed
covered by these 78 function identities.

For O15, exactly 74 isolated fixture mutations change only schema name, keeping
namespace OID, relation OID and every other coordinate fixed. For O16, exactly
74 change only namespace OID, keeping schema name and all other coordinates
fixed. Same-name/new-relation-OID is O14. Native schema rename/move/drop/recreate
is additional compound integration evidence, not a substitute for either
isolated cohort. Test-oracle fixture mutation is not permission to update
PostgreSQL system catalogs in a real database.

## Vanilla and provider boundaries

Vanilla PostgreSQL 16 can establish SQL ownership, grants, creator edges,
effective privilege checks, transactional DDL, local snapshots, crash/retry,
function/temp behavior, direct SQL and multiple-database semantics. Bootstrap
superuser may create D but must stop participating before the measured work.
All positive/negative operations are authenticated as the named D/M/L roles;
T invocation is exercised via trusted functions or controlled administrator
oracle steps, never passed off as a runtime T login.

Vanilla cannot prove the RDS-managed B/D edge graph, helper/catalog access,
provider restrictions, real secret/KMS IAM scopes, ECS task isolation or TLS
certificate/hostname validation. O20/O21 therefore require a separately
authorized disposable RDS PostgreSQL 16 instance and AWS resources. Record
actual engine patch, parameter group, RDS configuration and immutable subject
hashes; Terraform's existing engine version declaration is not deployment
evidence. The RDS master is NOSUPERUSER with provider-managed powers, not an
ordinary PostgreSQL superuser. Provider-managed databases/roles must be
explicitly observed; unsupported isolation or catalog access fails the profile.
[AWS RDS roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.PostgreSQL.CommonDBATasks.Roles.rds_superuser.html)

TLS requires `verify-full`, trusted RDS CA and hostname validation, with wrong
CA/hostname negative cases; no client-default `prefer` assumption. Secret
rotation needs fresh tasks and must prove stale task/session revocation.
[AWS RDS TLS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/PostgreSQL.Concepts.General.SSL.html),
[AWS ECS secret injection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/secrets-envvar-secrets-manager.html)

## Executed bounded probes — not the shared suite

One isolated, network-disabled, no-published-port, tmpfs container was used:
`paprnav-s4b-platform-profile-probe-20260916`, `postgres:16-alpine`, image ID
`sha256:d845e7f0ac8517b9d9868b6d20379f9688ba3676595e50ca7c0b664964b2a760`.
Server reported PostgreSQL 16.14 aarch64 Alpine. No application database,
credentials, AWS API or Terraform execution was used. The container was stopped
and final `docker inspect` reported `no such object`.

Gate probe: authenticated non-superuser L with SELECT only could not FOR SHARE.
After `GRANT UPDATE(gate_key)` it could FOR SHARE and FOR UPDATE, while
table-level UPDATE remained false and enabled-column UPDATE remained false.
An M-owned SECURITY INVOKER BEFORE-row guard rejected `UPDATE gate_key=gate_key`
with SQLSTATE 42501 / `PLATFORM_GATE_MUTATION_DENIED`. Updating enabled,
INSERT, DELETE and TRUNCATE failed ACL checks. M update succeeded and was
rolled back. This was a simplified table/role fixture, not the actual migration.

Ownership probe: D NOSUPERUSER/CREATEROLE/CREATEDB created M with the observed
B-attributed ADMIN-only edge. A separate D-attributed SET-only edge enabled
source-object then database transfer. `public` retained `pg_database_owner`.
Changing database owner and then trying D's schema-owner transfer failed
`must be owner of schema public`; that transaction rolled back. Correct inverse
used the temporary D-attributed INHERIT-only edge, D restored database first,
then table, and revoked the edge RESTRICT. M remained NOCREATEDB. Final owner
checks succeeded and only the original B ADMIN edge remained. Full inventory,
L-role cleanup and provider behavior were not executed by this probe.

These probes are feasibility evidence for specific declarative choices. They
are not O01–O22 PASS, not an approval of guard/source changes and not RDS proof.
The ownership/grantor rules are documented independently in
[PostgreSQL GRANT](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-grant.html),
[ALTER DATABASE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-alterdatabase.html), and
[role-creator configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/runtime-config-client.html#GUC-CREATEROLE-SELF-GRANT).

## Static validation performed

Available host interpreter:
`/Users/hostiletakeover/.cache/uv/archive-v0/7yFUSAy59HA-iD2R/bin/python`,
Python 3.11 with jsonschema 4.26.0. No dependency or runtime file was installed.
Two identical executions performed strict `json.loads` using a duplicate-key
rejecting `object_pairs_hook` and a rejecting `parse_constant`,
`Draft202012Validator.check_schema`, and validation of the profile. Exact
inventory/order/count assertions, unique paths/IDs, bounded-input and recovered
historical-source hashes, live preservation hashes and grant-count joins ran
in both executions.

Thirty copied in-memory schema counterexamples were rejected: unknown/missing
root; wrong version; future approval; wrong input hash/path; unknown role;
M CREATEDB widening; L ownership; edge reorder/omission/grantor substitution;
surviving temporary SET; runtime R SET; GRANT ALL; source omission/unknown
column; table-wide gate UPDATE; DEFINER gate guard; denied required TEMP;
omitted T lock; PUBLIC EXECUTE leak; sentinel SELECT; unclassified/missing
inventory; conflated namespace cohorts; second app connection; application-URL
migration fallback; claimed RDS execution; self hash. Duplicate root key,
nested duplicate key and NaN were the three rejected parser cases. These are
schema/parser checks, not database counterexamples.

Both executions yielded profile/schema VALID, 30/30 schema counterexamples
rejected, 3/3 parser counterexamples rejected, zero unclassified inventory
records, 722 unchanged regular files and five unchanged symlink targets.
Preservation manifest SHA-256:
`f222f49b5c80df911d04e7144961e7b93dbae583af041aec04abd48718288822`.
Manifest serialization is ordered `path TAB decimal-byte-size TAB sha256 LF`
for every `inventory.regularFiles` row. Symlinks are compared as literal targets
and cannot be authority inputs. Inventory excludes only these four new
derivative design files to avoid self-hash cycles; all prior bytes are preserved.

## Evidence and construction gate

After independent design approval, a separately scoped builder may construct
the profile-driven platform subject and shared harness. Save exact commands,
expected and actual diagnostics, native role/ACL/catalog rows, backend IDs,
transaction IDs, server/image/provider versions, fixture identifiers and
subject hashes. Redact passwords, not role identities or failure evidence.
Deterministic static/native captures are replayed twice; timed/concurrency/crash
cases retain both independent run outcomes rather than claiming byte-identical
timestamps. A separate reviewer must reproduce critical positives/negatives.

The construction/review order is profile → platform subject and native baseline

```text
# Platform runtime authority profile v2 — relationship closure

Status: **DESIGN_PROPOSAL_ONLY_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**.

## Model routing

Builder `/root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor`; requested GPT-6 Astra,
xhigh. Actual model: model not exposed by runtime. Actual effort: effort not
exposed. Trigger: PLATFORM-PROFILE-B-001 requires a complete implicit ORM
relationship-access correction, not a one-table patch. No reviewer or approval
is claimed by this builder.

## Version and authority

The single active proposed declarative source is
`platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.json`, SHA-256
`a3bff43719fc6db031a0bbb54cef32b83839eddf88013d35e7cdcbfbfdf80a31`.
Its closed validation-only schema is
`2a2c11e5e4def0c9b2cecadf798f047dbb68576d14249af11070fd4198d7d2b0`.
Both close all 32 root sections and every nested key, tuple/order, owner/role,
binding, grant and count by exact constants. Schema identity is not semantic
proof: the executable relationship oracle separately derives actual mapper,
source and caller facts and checks the proposed grants without using the const
schema to manufacture its expected result.

V1 and its FAIL remain byte-immutable historical inputs. The FAIL report hash
is `5b6cb8634c574358b578cdd230936cad62d188eb4ecd994b55bcf3c665125f76`.
The reassessment PASS remains upstream and bounded. V2 is a proposed repair of
the concrete profile, not a reinterpretation of that PASS or a finding closure.
The oracle/result are downstream evidence; the profile names their paths but
does not consume result hashes or a future approval. The final integration
review can never be an input to its own subject.

## Complete access family

The v1 direct-class AST scan missed relationship SQL. V2 instead combines:

- SQLAlchemy 2.0.52 configured mappers, independently joined to all source
  `relationship()` declarations and exact source-line hashes;
- explicit and implicit FK resolution, composite joins, view-only joins,
  `back_populates`, actual inverse directions, and association candidates;
- current filesystem enumeration of all 97 non-migration/non-model application
  Python files, with 83 admitted and 14 explicitly non-admitted callers;
- exact loader syntax and conservative instance-attribute candidates, raw
  Core/text SQL, imported helper calls, dynamic attribute access, and all 69
  installed function bodies, including the one dynamic SQL trigger function.

The rule is conservative: every declared relationship reachable from an
admitted file's direct model roots requires target/association SELECT, even
when an attribute's instance type cannot be proven statically. `callerPaths`
therefore means conservative reachability, not that every path executes every
edge. Direct AST paths remain separately recorded. Observed source expressions,
mapper declarations, loader strategy, and executed loader/caller fragments
are distinct evidence classes; v2 does not label ambiguous syntax an exact
runtime observation.

SQLAlchemy relationships can resolve foreign keys from metadata and load
related rows through several strategies. Back-populated directions are
separate mapped attributes, and association tables can add SQL dependencies.
[Relationship configuration](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/relationship_api.html),
[relationship loading](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/queryguide/relationships.html)

| Inventory | Exact count |
| --- | ---: |
| Mappers: baseline source / paused future authority | 113 / 7 |
| Relationship declarations and resolved mapper directions | 192 |
| Explicit-FK / implicit-FK relationships | 12 / 180 |
| Back-populated directions / unpaired directions | 158 / 34 |
| View-only relationships | 4 |
| Secondary relationships / generated backrefs / model properties or hybrids | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Resolved FK constraints / column edges, all 120 models | 535 / 799 |
| Resolved FK constraints / column edges, 113 baseline models | 508 / 734 |
| Mapped multi-parent FK association candidates, all / baseline | 98 / 92 |
| Source caller evidence: explicit loaders / model attributes / conservative candidates | 160 / 1 / 1,194 |
| Core query calls / literal text SQL calls / imported app helper calls | 321 / 7 / 813 |
| Dynamic attribute calls / installed function bodies | 56 / 69 |
| Reached source tables / distinct relationship target tables | 113 / 47 |

All 192 default mapper strategies are lazy `select`; the oracle additionally
exercises select-in and joined loading for every direction. Zero secondary
relationships and generated backrefs are measured absences, not omissions.
The 98 multi-parent tables are explicitly labelled association *candidates*,
not falsely reported as secondary relationships. Mapper inspection also captures
FK constraints installed by module-level helper functions, which a class-only
declaration scan misses.

The one installed dynamic SQL function is
`public.paprnav_v4_candidate_obligation_complete_trigger()`. Its `TG_TABLE_NAME`
domain is closed by 25 native trigger-bound tables. Its qualification/TEMP
attack gate remains mandatory; source dependency enumeration is not a claim
that the current body already meets the proposed platform security rules.

## Exact grant delta and preserved architecture

The only privilege delta is M granting L `SELECT` on
`public.ad_supersessions`, without grant option. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE,
ownership, role membership, function EXECUTE or sequence grant is widened.
The required source paths are explicit:

- `ad_release.py:80–89`: `ADExtraction.directive` and
  `AirworthinessDirective.superseded_by_edges` via select-in loading.
- `ad_matching.py:215–216`: the same nested relationship on release-loaded rows.
- `ad_reconciliation.py:95–104`: both `superseded_by_edges` and
  `supersedes_edges` via select-in loading.

The inverse `ADSupersession.superseding_ad` and `.superseded_ad` mapper
directions are independently enumerated and exercised. All other reached
targets were already SELECT-authorized: no second analogous SELECT omission
was found. The recomputed source grant inventory is 113 SELECT, 108 INSERT,
31 table UPDATE, three DELETE and 11 column UPDATE grants. The 69-function
inventory and 41 runtime EXECUTE grants remain unchanged; application sequence
grants remain empty and mapper sequence/identity absence is rechecked.

Sixteen protected v1 sections compare exactly, including D/M/L/T/R profiles,
PRA-M-001/AUTH-REASSESS-M-001 forward/inverse edges and ownership ordering,
database/schema policy, sealed platform state, the TEMP exception, guarded
UPDATE(`gate_key`), PLATFORM-CALLER-B-001's three T lock grants, one L app
connection, M-only migration connection, IAM/credential direction and rollout.
All source DML/column grants, grantors, options and ownership fields also
compare exactly. These preserved design choices remain subject to their
unexecuted production-compatible gates, not automatically approved by this
relationship repair.

## Executable evidence and remaining gates

`platform-runtime-authority-relationship-oracle.py` SHA-256:
`88baae7ae1903db2afe8d7b85d46cabec99b087d302ab1a089588a238ef84168`.
`platform-runtime-authority-relationship-results.json` SHA-256:
`37fa652e45ede9112bca3e5f97ad414a207d44338deaecae9946c1038ae13163`.
The latter is exact canonical stdout from two deterministic PostgreSQL runs.

The oracle rejected all 1,594 semantic omissions: 47 target SELECT grants,
192 model-direction records and 1,355 caller-evidence records. These mutations
are checked against independently re-derived source facts, not just the schema.
On actual PostgreSQL 16.14, authenticated non-superuser `rel_oracle_l` executed
576 nonempty loader cases and three bounded caller read fragments. Each of
the 47 independent native target SELECT revocations failed with SQLSTATE
42501 and the intended table diagnostic. The A→B, C→A supersession fixture
distinguishes both directions; it does not hide a swapped FK behind self-edges.

These are synthetic, constraint-free table fixtures. They do not prove full
release/matching/reconciliation workflows, source constraints/triggers,
migration/rollback, full TEMP attacks, IAM/TLS, or RDS behavior. Those gates
remain NOT_RUN. The companion plan gives replay commands and boundaries.

Strict duplicate-key JSON and Draft 2020-12 validation passed twice; 42 schema
mutations and three parser mutations were rejected per pass. All 727 preexisting
regular files and five symlink targets stayed unchanged. Ordered preservation
manifest digest (`path TAB bytes TAB sha256 LF`) is
`21047bc4954bffa2bdb8f1ddc04ae09ccca5b897f26b5bba0506495cd49dac3e`.

Only this six-file family is created. Production, partial implementation,
findings/reviews/state/packet, staging and immutable authorities are unchanged.
No remediation-3 F/FR/registry/occurrence/freshness counts or schema successors
are generated. The next gate is independent review of this remediation and
focused evidence; implementation and prior findings remain paused/open.

# Slice 4B platform runtime authority profile

Status: **DESIGN_PROPOSAL_ONLY_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**.

## Model routing

Builder: `/root/v4_s4b_decision_authority_extractor`. Requested GPT-6 Astra,
xhigh; actual model: model not exposed by runtime; actual effort: effort not
exposed. Trigger: third-loop authorization, migration, IAM and rollback
architecture reset. No reviewer assignment or approval is claimed here.

## Binding and boundary

`platform-runtime-authority-profile-v1.json` is the single declarative design:
SHA-256 `d0aeb528728de740c16bed931459f8c0d6dee2b8f9edf3bab4df36ee74c8d0fc`.
Its validation-only schema is SHA-256
`8b539d9a3b2af9b00e7359beb261caa0a136082a9034e594b98c5a13c1b4a00e`.
The schema uses exact section constants and a closed required root, so all
nested keys, records, ordered inventories, role/owner/phase enums and values
are closed, rather than accepting an unspecified future grant. A future edit
requires a successor version and separate review, not regeneration over v1.
This prose explains the JSON; it does not override or independently generate
SQL, Python or Terraform. Conflicts fail the review gate.

Only the frozen reassessment and its detached PASS are architecture inputs:

- Reassessment: `439200cfe99223883330943ead044e3e123dbd138933e6863e006feb184e1ce8`.
- Review: `20a341962f50e8f1738a35a909d78c602b1ef15e7b0cef4725f5397a0445ab10`.

The assignment's AUTH-REASSESS-M-001 refers to the immutable review's
PRA-M-001. Both designate the missing temporary ownership-transfer edge.
Neither the prior PASS nor this proposal approves implementation. Current
persistence contracts and partial 0030 remain explicitly incompatible with
this proposed topology. No findings are closed. No production, partial tree,
prior artifact, packet, ledger, staging or commit was changed. No successor
persistence/resource/map or remediation-3 arithmetic is constructed.

## Selected topology

One stable application login L and one application `DATABASE_URL` serve the
API, four worker modules and five enumerated operator scripts. Acceptance
inherits R privileges on that same connection: source locks and acceptance
writes share the transaction. M is a separate persistent, non-superuser,
CREATEROLE/NOCREATEDB/NOINHERIT migration administrator. Only the one-shot
migrator gets `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`. D remains deployment-only, including
the RDS master credential. T and R are NOLOGIN per-0030-installation roles;
T owns authority and R owns nothing. D/M are trusted administrators, not
hostile tenants. Hostile administrator isolation requires separate instances.

The JSON defines all role attributes, nine phase-specific membership records,
native identity lifecycle, database/schema policy, object grants and credential
boundaries. Automatic B-attributed ADMIN-only creator edges are retained;
they are not falsely described as removable by an ordinary M/D REVOKE. Every
temporary edge is grantor-specific, revoked RESTRICT and read back. The two
inverse D-attributed rows describe successive states of one native edge, not
simultaneous duplicate memberships. PostgreSQL distinguishes ADMIN, INHERIT
and SET and associates a role grant with its grantor.
[PostgreSQL 16 GRANT](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-grant.html)

Role names have exactly 48 ASCII bytes: `pn4b_<m/l/t/r>_<8-hex-db-oid>_<32-hex-nonce>`.
Eight collision attempts are allowed; no existing role is adopted. Names and
OIDs are persisted, not recomputed after database rename. Reused database OID,
renamed/recreated role, new OID behind the same name, cross-database dependency,
or unreviewed logical restore fails closed. Each database has separate M/L/T/R;
dropping one installation may not clean up another database's objects.

## Ownership transfer and inverse

D must actually have CREATEDB and own the declared database/source objects.
The forward D-attributed M→D edge is ADMIN=false, INHERIT=false, SET=true.
M creates L while D explicitly SET ROLE M, producing the expected L→M creator
edge. D transfers ordinary objects while it still owns the database, then
transfers the database. `public` retains `pg_database_owner`; its effective
owner follows the database. Temporary schema CREATE and SET edges are removed
before commit. These ownership requirements cannot be replaced by assuming
that the RDS master is a PostgreSQL superuser.
[ALTER DATABASE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-alterdatabase.html),
[AWS RDS roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.PostgreSQL.CommonDBATasks.Roles.rds_superuser.html)

Inverse maintenance first requires complete 0030 downgrade and drained L
sessions. D, still CREATEDB, temporarily inherits M without SET, restores
database ownership first, then source objects. For final L-role cleanup only,
the same D-granted edge becomes SET-only: D SET ROLE M, M drops dependency-free
L using its native ADMIN edge, D resets and revokes that edge RESTRICT, then
drops dependency-free M using D's retained creator ADMIN edge. M never needs
CREATEDB. The full inverse is an unexecuted oracle gate; the bounded probe
covered database/table transfer, not L cleanup or the complete object catalog.

The database-local `public.paprnav_platform_authority_state` is a separate
proposed platform control object, not an external receipt and not the future
0030 ACL snapshot. Its five columns, one sealed row, 8 MiB payload cap,
domain-separated hash, exact closed payload keys, M ownership, no runtime ACL,
immutable trigger and read/verify-before-use/drop rules are in the JSON.
It captures the pre-cutover catalog in the same DDL transaction. Runtime may
not read or mutate it. Supported-DDL inverse and raw-NULL ACL behavior require
full independent proof; no unreviewed raw ACL exception is allowed. Its new
object/field/function occurrences must enter the eventual recalculated DAG.

## Explicit compatibility proposals

Three changes require independent approval; none is silently inherited from
the current approved persistence subject.

1. **PLATFORM-TEMP-D-001:** L receives TEMPORARY because retained Slice-3A
   SECURITY INVOKER functions require `pg_temp.paprnav_v4_app_validation_state`.
   PUBLIC does not receive TEMP. Every trusted function and transitive helper
   must have fixed safe search_path and qualified permanent relation/type/
   operator references. Acceptance must not trust L-writable validation cache.
   The complete closed function inventory receives malicious-temp tests.
2. **PLATFORM-GATE-D-002:** L receives only column UPDATE(`gate_key`) on
   `public.ad_v4_feature_gates` in addition to SELECT, supporting existing row
   locks. M owns `public.paprnav_platform_gate_guard()` and the ALWAYS-enabled
   BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE row trigger `trg_platform_gate_guard`. It is
   SECURITY INVOKER and permits mutations only when both session/current user
   name+OID equal bound M and TG_RELID equals the bound gate table OID. L/R
   cannot execute the gate setter, own/alter the guard, or disable triggers.
3. **PLATFORM-CALLER-B-001:** paused trusted SQL lines 161/163/165 lock app
   projections, obligation projections and review requests FOR SHARE. The
   current contract grants T UPDATE(id) only on users and memberships. The
   proposed extension adds exactly UPDATE(id) on those three immutable source
   tables, no table UPDATE or grant option. Actual T direct UPDATE, including
   no-op updates, must fail the existing immutable guards. The successor
   persistence contract and ACL snapshots must explicitly bind this delta.

The gate-column probe establishes privilege feasibility, not implementation
safety. A guard bypass, direct source mutation, temp-shadow acceptance, or
caller requiring an unlisted grant remains a release blocker. PostgreSQL's
security guidance requires trusted functions to exclude untrusted schemas
from name resolution; this profile additionally requires explicit qualification.
[CREATE FUNCTION security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-createfunction.html)

## Inventory and deployment contracts

The JSON records every preexisting repository entry: 722 regular files with
hash/size/classification and five explicitly rejected symlink audit aliases.
It contains 97 application Python caller records, 113 baseline ORM source
tables, seven paused future authority tables and all 69 installed 0029
functions. Source privileges enumerate 112 SELECT, 108 INSERT, 31 table UPDATE,
three DELETE and 11 column UPDATE entries; 41 non-trigger functions are
runtime-executable. Trigger invocation is separate from direct EXECUTE.
No sequence grant is proposed; complete live catalog absence is a gate, not a
conclusion inferred solely from source. `ad_supersessions` has no runtime
caller and no L grant. All five operator scripts are explicitly named in the
JSON; seed/fixture/verification callers are denied production credentials.

Static classification is not proof that every dynamic SQL path works. The
independent SQL/OID trace oracle must exercise direct SQL, ORM lazy access,
dynamic factories, triggers and imports; any unclassified access blocks
release rather than widening privileges. Read/update/delete grants are explicit
object grants, not GRANT ALL or schema wildcards.

Exact existing Terraform, IAM, compose, config, session, Alembic and deployment
documentation paths/hashes are normative *observations* in `deployment.normativeFiles`.
They are not declared compliant implementations. Future reviewed provisioning
and runbook must bind concrete native identities, exact secret/KMS ARNs,
execution/task roles, security groups, image digests and credential operator.
API/worker execution roles read only L/session secrets; migrator reads only M;
frontend reads neither and cannot reach RDS. Master is never injected into ECS.

Rotation is controlled maintenance: drain and NOLOGIN, change the database
password, publish the secret version, authenticate, restart tasks, then resume.
SQL password updates and Secrets Manager are not atomic. Failure leaves the
runtime stopped until reconciliation. Existing sessions must be terminated on
revocation. ECS secret injection does not hot-refresh running tasks.
[AWS ECS secret injection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/secrets-envvar-secrets-manager.html)

## Evidence and next gate

The JSON/schema validated twice deterministically under Draft 2020-12 with
strict duplicate-key/non-JSON-number rejection. Thirty schema counterexamples
and three parser counterexamples were rejected per replay. All 722 preexisting
regular files and five symlink targets remained unchanged. Ordered manifest
digest (path TAB size TAB SHA-256 LF) is
`f222f49b5c80df911d04e7144961e7b93dbae583af041aec04abd48718288822`.
No generated results file was necessary; this builder evidence is not a PASS.

The companion oracle plan separates two executed simplified PG16.14 probes
from 22 planned families and mandatory disposable RDS/AWS gates. Independent
profile review is the next gate. It must disposition all three compatibility
proposals, owner/inverse/control-state rules and exact caller grants before
authorizing any implementation or successor design. No RDS PASS is claimed.

are absent and their creation/cleanup is not authorized by the active
deployment identity. This is a blocker for executing this profile in this

ECS likewise needs its service-linked role for task ENIs and creates it with
cluster/service creation.

These are provider-fixed account resources, outside the experiment's

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only AWS capability evidence for the bounded Slice 4B RDS oracle.

No secret values, network/database connections, resource writes, or file writes.
The sole create-shaped call is EC2 CreateVpc with mandatory --dry-run.
Emit exact non-secret CLI stdout/stderr plus deterministic subject hashes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

RUN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = RUN.parents[2]
PREFIX = "paprnav-s4b-rds-oracle-20260916-2108"
ACCOUNT = "527257972989"
REGION = "us-east-1"
POLICY = f"arn:aws:iam::{ACCOUNT}:policy/paprnav-terraform-deploy"


def utc():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def probe(case):
    cid, args = case
    if args[:2] == ["ec2", "create-vpc"]:
        assert "--dry-run" in args
    else:
        assert args[1].startswith(("get-", "list-", "describe-"))
    cmd = ["aws", *args, "--output", "json", "--no-cli-pager"]
    env = dict(os.environ, AWS_PROFILE="paprnav-deploy", AWS_REGION=REGION,
               AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=REGION, AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG="1",
               AWS_PAGER="", AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS="1")
    start = utc()
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True,
                            timeout=45, check=False)
    row = {"id": cid, "command": cmd, "startedAt": start, "endedAt": utc(),
           "exitCode": result.returncode, "stdout": result.stdout,
           "stderr": result.stderr}
    if result.returncode == 0:
        row["parsed"] = json.loads(result.stdout)
    return row


CASES = [
    ("identity", ["sts", "get-caller-identity"]),
    ("deployment_role", ["iam", "get-role", "--role-name", "paprnav-terraform-deploy",
     "--query", "Role.{Arn:Arn,Name:RoleName,Boundary:PermissionsBoundary}"]),
    ("attached_policies", ["iam", "list-attached-role-policies", "--role-name", "paprnav-terraform-deploy"]),
    ("inline_policies", ["iam", "list-role-policies", "--role-name", "paprnav-terraform-deploy"]),
    ("policy_current_version", ["iam", "get-policy", "--policy-arn", POLICY,
     "--query", "Policy.{Arn:Arn,DefaultVersionId:DefaultVersionId,AttachmentCount:AttachmentCount}"]),
    ("policy_v5", ["iam", "get-policy-version", "--policy-arn", POLICY,
     "--version-id", "v5", "--query", "PolicyVersion.Document"]),
    ("rds_service_role", ["iam", "get-role", "--role-name", "AWSServiceRoleForRDS",
     "--query", "Role.{Arn:Arn,Name:RoleName,Path:Path}"]),
    ("ecs_service_role", ["iam", "get-role", "--role-name", "AWSServiceRoleForECS",
     "--query", "Role.{Arn:Arn,Name:RoleName,Path:Path}"]),
    ("engine", ["rds", "describe-db-engine-versions", "--engine", "postgres",
     "--engine-version", "16.14", "--query",
     "DBEngineVersions[].{Version:EngineVersion,Status:Status,ParameterFamily:DBParameterGroupFamily,Certificates:SupportedCACertificateIdentifiers}"]),
    ("micro_shape", ["rds", "describe-orderable-db-instance-options", "--engine", "postgres",
     "--engine-version", "16.14", "--db-instance-class", "db.t4g.micro", "--query",
     "OrderableDBInstanceOptions[].{Version:EngineVersion,Class:DBInstanceClass,Vpc:Vpc,Storage:StorageType,MinGB:MinStorageSize,Encrypted:SupportsStorageEncryption,AZ:AvailabilityZones[].Name}"]),
    ("rds_quotas", ["rds", "describe-account-attributes"]),
    ("availability_zones", ["ec2", "describe-availability-zones", "--filters", "Name=state,Values=available",
     "--query", "AvailabilityZones[].{Name:ZoneName,Id:ZoneId,State:State}"]),
    ("rds_ca", ["rds", "describe-certificates"]),
    ("vpc_quota", ["service-quotas", "get-service-quota", "--service-code", "vpc", "--quota-code", "L-F678F1CE"]),
    ("fargate_quota", ["service-quotas", "get-service-quota", "--service-code", "fargate", "--quota-code", "L-3032A538"]),
    ("vpc_dry_run", ["ec2", "create-vpc", "--cidr-block", "10.247.0.0/24", "--dry-run"]),
    ("kms_service_alias", ["kms", "list-aliases", "--query",
     "Aliases[?AliasName=='alias/aws/secretsmanager'].{AliasName:AliasName,AliasArn:AliasArn,TargetKeyId:TargetKeyId}"]),
    ("absence_vpc", ["ec2", "describe-vpcs", "--filters", f"Name=tag:OracleRun,Values={PREFIX}",
     "--query", "Vpcs[].VpcId"]),
    ("absence_db", ["rds", "describe-db-instances", "--db-instance-identifier", PREFIX]),
    ("absence_cluster", ["ecs", "describe-clusters", "--clusters", PREFIX,
     "--query", "{clusters:clusters[].clusterArn,failures:failures}"]),
    ("absence_roles", ["iam", "list-roles", "--query", f"Roles[?starts_with(RoleName, '{PREFIX}')].Arn"]),
    ("absence_secrets", ["secretsmanager", "list-secrets", "--include-planned-deletion", "--filters",
     f"Key=name,Values={PREFIX}", "--query", "SecretList[].ARN"]),
    ("absence_ecr", ["ecr", "describe-repositories", "--repository-names", PREFIX]),
    ("absence_logs", ["logs", "describe-log-groups", "--log-group-name-prefix", PREFIX,
     "--query", "logGroups[].logGroupName"]),
]


def main():
    started = utc()
    # Account guard precedes all other queries, including the no-mutation dry run.
    identity = probe(CASES[0])
    assert identity.get("parsed", {}).get("Account") == ACCOUNT, "WRONG_ACCOUNT_ABORT"
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        records = [identity, *pool.map(probe, CASES[1:])]
    inputs = []
    for name in ["platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.json",
                 "platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.schema.json",
                 "platform-runtime-authority-oracle-plan.md",
                 "platform-runtime-authority-oracle-plan-v2.md",
                 "adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.md",
                 "adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-local-v2.md",
                 "platform-runtime-authority-local-results-v2.json",
                 "persistence-runtime-authority-reassessment.md",
                 "risk-adjusted-routing-audit.md"]:
        path = RUN / name
        assert path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()
        data = path.read_bytes()
        inputs.append({"path": name, "bytes": len(data),
                       "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()})
    print(json.dumps({"format": "paprnav-s4b-rds-preflight-1",
        "status": "PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE_ONLY", "startedAt": started, "endedAt": utc(),
        "account": ACCOUNT, "region": REGION, "prefix": PREFIX,
        "modelRouting": {"builder": "/root/v4_s4b_managed_rds_oracle_builder",
                         "requestedModel": "gpt-6-astra", "requestedEffort": "xhigh",
                         "actualModel": "model not exposed by runtime",
                         "actualEffort": "effort not exposed",
                         "reviewer": None},
        "mutationsExecuted": [], "secretValueReadsExecuted": [],
        "inputs": inputs, "records": records}, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

# Package C: native RDS prerequisite and execution amendment

Status: **READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**; design only. Account/resource
authorization and fresh execution bindings remain required. This artifact
supersedes the C execution proposal in the failed
[manifest](platform-runtime-authority-rds-execution-manifest.md), without
rewriting that historical evidence or approving implementation.

## Model routing

Builder `/root/v4_s4b_rds_prerequisite_designer`; requested `gpt-6-astra` /
`xhigh`; actual **model not exposed by runtime** / **effort not exposed**.
Trigger: R/C/D/U **5/4/5/5**, unresolved account IAM, provider identity,
credential transport, key and cleanup prerequisites after four preflight
findings. No fallback or self-approval claimed. Coordinator assigns a separate
read-only Astra xhigh reviewer and records the returned identity.

## Decision, authority and alternatives

Use one disposable private RDS instance, two synthetic databases, and one
disposable EC2 node that forwards encrypted traffic through Systems Manager
(SSM). The oracle and credential handling run on the trusted local operator
machine. The EC2 node receives **no database password, secret ARN permission,
application code or database client**. This is a concrete non-ECS D path under
profile v2 `deployment.masterSecret.ecsReaders=[]`.

The [partition](local-cloud-partition-amendment.md) and its
[Package A PASS](adversarial-local-cloud-partition-amendment.md) permit this
design. The [routing audit](risk-adjusted-routing-audit.md),
[profile v2](platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.json), its
[bounded PASS](adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-profile-v2.md),
[local-v2 evidence](platform-runtime-authority-local-results-v2.json) and
[PASS](adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-local-v2.md) remain upstream.
The [preflight result](platform-runtime-authority-rds-preflight-results.json),
[provenance](platform-runtime-authority-rds-preflight-provenance.md) and
[FAIL](adversarial-platform-runtime-authority-rds-preflight.md) establish missing
authority, not native feasibility. All four `RDS-PREFLIGHT-*` findings remain
open; whole-finding closure belongs to the coordinator/reviewer.

Local construction remains productive: two local runs each passed 1,418
bounded checks. AWS evidence is needed because native provider membership,
grantors, ordinary-M catalog/helper access and ownership reversal can change
D's persisted ACL design. Building the application on AWS would not remove
those design obligations. The existing Terraform skeleton is an intended
deployment target, not a compliant executor: its shared execution role,
master-credential advice, unpinned images and current connection behavior need
E/F work. No existing pilot resource or Terraform state is used by C.

Rejected for this run: D in ECS (profile conflict); public RDS (unnecessary
exposure); NAT/interface endpoints (extra resources/cost for one short run);
customer-managed keys (delayed deletion); local emulation as native RDS proof;
an unrestricted intermediary IAM role; full ECS/rotation evidence in C.

## Fixed scope and late-bound identities

Account `527257972989`, region `us-east-1`; operator IAM role
`arn:aws:iam::527257972989:role/paprnav-terraform-deploy`.
At execution entry bind fresh `P=paprnav-s4b-c-<UTCYYYYMMDDHHMM>-<8lowerhex>`
(CSPRNG suffix), start `T0`, measurement deadline `T0+60m`, and cleanup deadline
`T0+120m`. Never reuse the expired `paprnav-s4b-rds-oracle-20260916-2108` attempt.
Tags on every supported customer-created resource: `Project=paprnav`,
`Environment=oracle`, `ManagedBy=codex`, `OracleRun=P`,
`Purpose=T081-V4-SCHEMA-SLICE-4B-C`, `ExpiresAt=<cleanup deadline>`.
Provider-fixed roles/keys and AWS-generated default objects have explicit
ledger exceptions, not fabricated tags.

| Resource | Exact binding and permitted shape |
|---|---|
| VPC | New `10.247.0.0/24`, DNS support/hostnames true; IPv4 only; no peers/VPN/transit/NAT/endpoints or attachment to existing networks. |
| Subnets/routes | `P-db-a`=`10.247.0.0/27` in `us-east-1a`; `P-db-b`=`10.247.0.32/27` in `us-east-1b`; `P-ssm`=`10.247.0.64/27` in `us-east-1a`. Bind AZ IDs, currently observed `use1-az1`/`use1-az2`. DB route table has local route only. SSM route table has local plus `0.0.0.0/0` to new `P-igw`. |
| Security groups | `P-db`: TCP/5432 ingress solely from `P-ssm`; no default outbound rule. `P-ssm`: no inbound; TCP/5432 egress to `P-db`, TCP/443 egress to `0.0.0.0/0`; remove default all-egress. Amazon-provided VPC DNS; no custom DNS. Default network ACL permits return traffic; it is confined to this isolated VPC. |
| RDS | Identifier `P`, PostgreSQL `16.14`, `db.t4g.micro`, single-AZ `us-east-1a`, 5-GiB gp2, encrypted, no storage autoscaling, `PubliclyAccessible=false`, backup retention 0, no replicas/proxy/PI/enhanced monitoring/log export, no deletion protection, auto-minor-upgrade false. Subnet group `P`, parameter group `P-pg16`, CA `rds-ca-rsa2048-g1`. No substitution of class/patch/storage/AZ after preflight. |
| SQL | Master D=`paprnav_oracle_d`, RDS-managed password. Initial DB `oracle_a`; D creates `oracle_b`. Distinct profile-derived M/L/T/R per database, with OIDs and CSPRNG nonces; only synthetic 0029 data. All other databases enumerated and measured. |
| SSM node | One on-demand `t4g.nano`, `us-east-1a`, explicit auto-assigned public IPv4, no Elastic IP, no SSH key, no inbound ports, IMDSv2 required/hop-limit 1, encrypted 8-GiB gp3 root volume with DeleteOnTermination, no data volume, detailed monitoring off, CPU credits standard. AMI: resolve Amazon-owned AL2023 ARM64 through public parameter `/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64`; bind exact image ID/owner/root snapshot/architecture and packaged SSM-agent version before launch; agent must be at least 3.1.1374.0. No unpinned package installation or application user-data. |
| Node IAM | New exact `role/P-ssm` and `instance-profile/P-ssm`, EC2-only service trust. Sole inline policy is the five SSM-agent operations below. No existing managed policy attachment. |
| Session | New exact SSM `document/P-forward`, version 1; type `Session`, `sessionType=Port`; immutable exact RDS endpoint and remote port 5432, local port 15432, no caller parameters. Exact document SHA pinned before StartSession. CLI plugin and libpq/psycopg versions pinned locally. One session at a time. |
| Secrets | Only RDS-generated D secret `S`, resolved from this instance's `MasterUserSecret.SecretArn` and joined to `DbiResourceId`. No M/L application Secrets Manager secrets in C: synthetic M/L credentials exist only in local process memory. |

The current captured capabilities support the chosen RDS patch/class/storage/CA;
they do not establish current capacity or the EC2 shape. Fresh preflight must
resolve every generated ID to exact ARN plus create response, tags and parent
VPC/instance. A resource name or prefix alone never authorizes mutation/deletion.

## Shared account prerequisites and exact temporary authority

The selected plan creates and **retains only the RDS service-linked role** if
absent. Its fixed ARN is
`arn:aws:iam::527257972989:role/aws-service-role/rds.amazonaws.com/AWSServiceRoleForRDS`.
It is shared account infrastructure; it is not deleted during experiment cleanup.
ECS's fixed `AWSServiceRoleForECS` remains an E prerequisite, uncreated by C.
Consequently C cannot close the ECS clause of `RDS-PREFLIGHT-B-001`.
[AWS RDS service-linked-role policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAM.ServiceLinkedRoles.html)
supports this exact creation scope:

```json
{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole","Resource":"arn:aws:iam::527257972989:role/aws-service-role/rds.amazonaws.com/AWSServiceRoleForRDS","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"iam:AWSServiceName":"rds.amazonaws.com"}}}
```

Add `DateLessThan:{"aws:CurrentTime":<T0+15m>}` to that statement at binding;
apply in dedicated inline policy `P-rds-role`, remove immediately after exact
role/trust/attached-policy readback, and prove the policy absent. No
`iam:DeleteServiceLinkedRole`, wildcard service name, custom suffix, ECS role
creation, trust edit or service-role policy edit is permitted. If another
administrator has already created the matching role, record its baseline and
omit the grant/create step. Wrong trust/policy is a blocker, not an edit target.

The complete captured v5 policy already permits region-wide RDS/EC2 writes and
`paprnav-*` role/profile management. Those broad historical permissions remain
unchanged and do not make this run itself broadly authorized. It lacks
generated-secret create/tag, SSM session/document operations, EC2 PassRole and
quota reads. The following is the **complete additional permission schedule**;
all are Allow statements, no wildcard action. Expand symbols into literal ARNs
in one reviewed execution binding before application. Date-bound experiment
creation/delivery permissions expire at `T0+120m`; removal is still mandatory.

| Phase/action | Resource and conditions | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| `secretsmanager:CreateSecret`, `secretsmanager:TagResource` | `arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:527257972989:secret:rds!db-*`; `aws:RequestedRegion=us-east-1`, ten-minute window starting immediately before CreateDBInstance, ending no later than `T0+45m` | Inline `P-master-create`, only around the single CreateDBInstance call. No Get/Put/Rotate/Delete on this wildcard. |
| `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` | Exact returned `S`; `secretsmanager:VersionStage=AWSCURRENT`, region and cleanup deadline | Inline `P-master-read`, installed only after metadata join; remove when D work ends. SDK requests AWSCURRENT explicitly and records returned version ID, never value. |
| `iam:PassRole` | Exact `arn:aws:iam::527257972989:role/P-ssm`; `iam:PassedToService=ec2.amazonaws.com`, cleanup deadline | Dedicated inline `P-ec2-passrole`, installed immediately before node creation; remove and verify absent after node/profile readback, or after resolving a failed/unknown create. No document authority or other IAM role/service in this policy. |
| `ssm:CreateDocument`, `ssm:AddTagsToResource`, `ssm:GetDocument` | Exact `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:527257972989:document/P-forward`; regional, cleanup deadline | Inline `P-document-create-read`, installed after RDS endpoint binding and immediately before document creation, only after the deletion policy below is installed. Remove and verify absent after document content/version/hash/tag readback, before StartSession; on failure remove after create-outcome resolution. No UpdateDocument, default-version change, SendCommand, Automation, SSH or shell permission. |
| `ssm:DeleteDocument` | Exact `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:527257972989:document/P-forward`; regional | Dedicated inline `P-document-delete`, installed before any CreateDocument attempt; retain only this document cleanup authority through verified document absence, including failed/unknown creates and cleanup beyond the deadline, then remove and verify absent. No create/read or PassRole action. |
| `ssm:StartSession` | Exact created EC2 instance ARN **and** exact `document/P-forward` ARN, separate required resource entries, region and cleanup deadline; instance statement requires `ssm:SessionDocumentAccessCheck=true` | Inline `P-session`, installed after IDs/document are bound. No AWS default session document. |
| `ssmmessages:OpenDataChannel` | `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:527257972989:session/P-operator-*`, regional and cleanup deadline | Fresh assumed deployment-role session named exactly `P-operator`; returned SessionId must match this documented session-name prefix or stop. No broad session channel grant. |
| `ssm:TerminateSession` | Exact session ARN after StartSession response, regional | Inline `P-session-cleanup`, retained until session termination verified. No ResumeSession. |
| `servicequotas:GetServiceQuota` | `arn:aws:servicequotas:us-east-1:527257972989:vpc/L-F678F1CE` and `arn:aws:servicequotas:us-east-1:527257972989:ec2/L-1216C47A`; regional | Temporary read-only preflight grant `P-quota`; no quota increases. |

Generated D-secret ARN cannot be known before RDS assigns its resource ID. The
create/tag prefix exception is the unavoidable bootstrap breadth of this plan:
it can tag other matching secrets during its short window. It must be explicitly
authorized as such, not described as an exact-secret grant. No unverified
`aws:CalledVia`, assumed request-tag propagation or service-linked-role bypass
is used to pretend a narrower provider path exists. Delete `P-master-create`
immediately after the create response (also on failure/unknown result), before
any GetSecretValue. Metadata must show the new instance's exact D secret,
RDS ownership and expected key. Add the run tags only to `S` through a separately
bound exact-ARN `TagResource` permission if RDS did not propagate them, then
remove that permission. Never retag an existing secret. The AWS prerequisites
are CreateSecret, TagResource and DescribeKey; customer-key permissions differ.
[RDS secret integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html)
and [Secrets Manager action/resource semantics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_secretsmanager.html).

An authorized account administrator applies/removes these dedicated policies;
the existing managed policy v5 is never replaced. The coordinator may perform
those exact temporary self-policy edits only if the user explicitly authorizes
them after independent review. Existing CreatePolicyVersion/PutRolePolicy
capability is not authorization. Do not invent an administrator identity or
use the bootstrap user's assume-only policy as administrator authority.
Record the actual administrator IAM principal, literal policy name, exact policy
document SHA-256, installation/readback time and removal/absence time for every
temporary policy, including distinct `P-ec2-passrole`,
`P-document-create-read` and `P-document-delete` entries. Remove only this run's
policies, preserve preexisting policies, and compare the complete before/after
attachment/inline/boundary/trust state; all three distinct entries must be absent
from the final inline-policy inventory. If independent
review or the owner rejects the temporary breadth, C remains blocked.

The SSM node's inline policy allows only `ssm:UpdateInstanceInformation`,
`ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel`, `CreateDataChannel`, `OpenControlChannel`,
and `OpenDataChannel` (all five fully prefixed in the bound JSON), on `*` with
`aws:RequestedRegion=us-east-1`. These agent-channel operations require that
resource breadth; it does not include secret, KMS, S3, IAM or RDS actions.
[AWS's minimal Session Manager instance policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/getting-started-create-iam-instance-profile.html).
Do not enable Default Host Management Configuration or create its account role.

## D transport, keys and secret handling

The local process uses AWS profile `paprnav-deploy` in a fresh session named
`P-operator`; IAM caller, account and role ID must match the bound identity.
SSM transports TCP through the EC2 node to the private native endpoint. The
session document has these literal properties after endpoint binding:

```json
{"schemaVersion":"1.0","description":"Bound Package C database tunnel","sessionType":"Port","parameters":{},"properties":{"host":"<exact-new-RDS-endpoint>","portNumber":"5432","localPortNumber":"15432"}}
```

Use StartSession via a local adapter that keeps TokenValue/StreamUrl private,
adds the exact returned cleanup Session ARN, then launches the plugin. Renew
only by terminating the old session and creating a newly bound one; no token
or plugin debug stream enters artifacts. Verify local listener is loopback-only
and port 15432 was free before StartSession; otherwise terminate and stop.
SSM-agent version/name resolution and remote port requirements are explicit in
[AWS remote-host forwarding](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-sessions-start.html).
SSM port-forwarding has no SQL transcript; record API/session IDs and sanitized
oracle results, not a claim of session-content audit logging.

For every D/M/L connection, psycopg receives separate in-memory kwargs:
`host=<native RDS endpoint>, hostaddr=127.0.0.1, port=15432,
sslmode=verify-full, sslrootcert=<pinned regional RDS CA bundle>` plus exact
database/user/password. The native hostname remains the certificate identity
while hostaddr directs traffic to the tunnel.
[PostgreSQL 16 host/hostaddr rules](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/libpq-connect.html).
Record CA SHA-256, server certificate identity, `pg_stat_ssl`, authenticated
`session_user/current_user`, PID and transaction ID. No first unverified SQL
connection is permitted. A tunnel connection is not TLS/hostname-negative or
ECS delivery evidence.

Before create, resolve `alias/aws/secretsmanager`, `alias/aws/rds` and
`alias/aws/ebs` using ListAliases. Describe only returned concrete key IDs in
the read-only preflight; verify account/region, `KeyManager=AWS`, enabled
symmetric encrypt/decrypt key and expected alias mapping. The captured secrets
key was `ea9571ad-3bc5-4ed5-96d9-070bcad47d60`, not a permanent current binding.
If an alias has no target, initialization is an explicit **persistent account
prerequisite**: an authorized administrator calls DescribeKey for that exact
AWS alias and records the new ID before disposable resources are created.
DescribeKey on an unbound predefined alias can create its AWS-managed key;
it is not classified as read-only here.
[KMS DescribeKey behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeKey.html).

RDS storage uses the pinned `aws/rds` key; managed D secret uses
`aws/secretsmanager`; EC2 root EBS uses pinned `aws/ebs`. Confirm actual key ARNs
in RDS/secret/volume metadata. These AWS-managed keys/aliases persist and are
never tagged, edited, scheduled for deletion or counted as disposable leftovers.
No customer key, custom key policy, grants experiment or direct KMS decryption
grant is added. Failure under native AWS-managed-key policy stops the run.
Customer-managed-key policy/grant/context negatives remain **NOT_RUN**, and E
must either retain this same managed-key selection or separately review/test a
customer-key design. [RDS key behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.Keys.html).

Only `S` may be read, only after exact instance/secret/key checks, and only into
the local runner's memory. Never output SDK responses containing SecretString,
SecretBinary, session tokens or credential URLs. No dotenv, argv, Terraform,
image, file, console history, tracing, core dump or exception repr may contain
them. M/L passwords are locally generated CSPRNG values; client-side SCRAM
verifiers are installed over TLS and also treated as secrets. No password
recovery, user/customer data or existing secret is used. Disable SQL echo and
assert server `log_statement=none`, `log_min_duration_statement=-1`,
`log_min_error_statement=panic`, `log_parameter_max_length_on_error=0`, no
pgaudit/auto_explain before credential SQL. The parameter group also sets
`rds.force_ssl=1` and `password_encryption=scram-sha-256`; required static
settings must be in-sync before first connection. A failure preserves no
credential-containing diagnostic; sanitized SQLSTATE/statement ID suffices.

## Fresh preflight, execution order and cost bound

Before any account mutation, freeze the design, reviewer PASS and explicit
authorization. Before any disposable resource, bind a new run-local execution
subject containing exact expanded policies, caller/admin identities, names,
timestamps, key IDs, AMI/image/plugin/CA/SQL-runner hashes and cleanup ledger
schema. Review the subject with this design as one C boundary; later generated
IDs may only fill the declared joins, never introduce a new choice or privilege.

Required fresh checks (maximum age 15 minutes at first disposable create):
identity and full live policy/boundary/session-policy/SCP restrictions insofar
as visible; exact prerequisites; name/tag absence; RDS orderability and CA;
AZs/subnet/address capacity; VPC quota and live VPC count; EC2 standard On-Demand
vCPU quota/headroom for two vCPUs and instance-type AZ offering; RDS instance,
parameter/subnet-group quota headroom; AMI/agent suitability; three key bindings;
local plugin/libpq/CA/hash readiness; all create/delete permissions and exact
policy action/resource/condition validation. An IAM simulation is supporting
evidence, never proof that SCPs or service internals allow execution. Missing
quota, policy or cleanup evidence is an abort **before** resource creation;
no quota increase, alternate AZ/class, trial resource or network widening.
Fargate quota is irrelevant to C and remains required in E.

A resource ledger records create intent before each request and the exact ID,
ARN, parent, tags, timestamp and request ID after it. Unknown create outcomes
are resolved by exact-name/tag lookup; never repeat a create blindly. Construct
network/groups and node role/profile; install `P-ec2-passrole`; create/read back
node and instance-profile binding; remove/verify `P-ec2-passrole` absent; observe
SSM Online; create RDS with managed master; remove wildcard secret-create
authority; bind endpoint, `S` and returned keys. Install `P-document-delete`
first, then `P-document-create-read`; create/read back document content, exact
version, hash and tags; remove/verify `P-document-create-read` absent. Install
narrow delivery/session grants, establish TLS, run native matrix, enter cleanup.
Use the original policy's `ssm:DescribeDocument` to recheck the pinned version
and SHA-256 immediately before each StartSession and to verify document absence
during cleanup; no removed GetDocument/create permission is reused. If SSM is not Online within
10 minutes, abort before RDS creation. If RDS is not available by minute 45,
abort measured work. Begin cleanup by minute 60 on either success or failure.

Before launch, capture current public regional rates and project two hours of
RDS, EC2, storage, one public IPv4, one secret/API usage and at most 100 MiB
traffic, including worst-case T4g database credit charges. Proceed only if the
conservative projection is at most **US$5** and the user authorizes this
resource/cost envelope. This is a planning ceiling, not an AWS-enforced billing
cap; asynchronous deletion or provider failure can exceed the TTL/projection.
No price or $5 sufficiency is asserted from stale evidence. An available named
account administrator must own cleanup escalation before launch. No unattended
TTL tag or unenrolled budget alert is represented as an automatic destroyer.

## Teardown, authorization and review exit

On normal/error/timeout paths, stop SQL work, roll back active transactions and
close local D/M/L connections; erase in-memory credentials and remove D-read
grant. Terminate the exact SSM session and observe terminated/absent. Delete
the exact RDS instance with SkipFinalSnapshot=true and DeleteAutomatedBackups=true;
poll its DB ARN/ID, DbiResourceId backups/snapshots, generated `S`, RDS ENIs and
parameter/subnet references. RDS owns master-secret destruction: never force
delete an attached RDS secret. If the DB is gone but `S` remains, record an
orphan and escalate to the named administrator; any direct orphan deletion
requires separately bound exact ownership evidence/authorization, not a
wildcard secret-delete fallback. This run creates no application secret; E's
synthetic application secrets must use ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery and poll
ResourceNotFound, not merely a scheduled-deletion timestamp.

Terminate the exact EC2 instance; verify terminated, instance ENI released,
DeleteOnTermination volume absent and public IPv4 released. Verify
`P-ec2-passrole` and `P-document-create-read` already absent (remove either on
an early-abort path after its create outcome is resolved). Delete exact
`P-forward` using retained `P-document-delete`; poll `ssm:DescribeDocument`
under the original policy until `InvalidDocument` confirms absence, including
all versions, then remove/verify `P-document-delete` absent. If document creation
never occurred, verify absence before removing any installed deletion policy.
Then remove node inline policy, role/profile association, profile and role.
After RDS absence delete its parameter/subnet groups; revoke run SG references,
delete run SGs, disassociate/delete non-main routes, delete subnets, detach/
delete IGW, then VPC (including its implicit defaults). Remove any remaining
run-specific cleanup policies only after their respective absence proofs;
creation/delivery policies retain the earlier removal points above. Keep
read-only evidence access from the original policy. Baseline v5,
trust, attached policies/boundary must match exactly. No shared service role or
AWS key is removed.

Each delete is preceded by exact ledger ID/account/parent/tag validation, never
a prefix deletion loop. Poll asynchronous state with exponential backoff capped
at 30 seconds; require service NotFound (EC2 may retain a terminated-instance
record) and an independent fresh inventory with no billable children. At minute
120 stop all new work and declare **C_CLEANUP_FAILED** if any disposable item
remains; preserve exact residual ledger and immediately escalate to the named
account administrator, continuing safe cleanup with existing authority. A
deadline never justifies abandoning resources, accepting scheduled deletion as
absence or granting new privileges. No C PASS until all required absence and
temporary-policy removal evidence exists. Provider audit/SSM session metadata
retention is not a live billable resource and is declared separately.

Still-required explicit authorization: (1) create/retain the exact shared RDS
service-linked role and initialize/retain any missing AWS-managed RDS/EBS key;
(2) the exact temporary policy schedule, including short-lived generated-secret
create/tag breadth and exact master-secret read, with a bound administrator or
explicitly authorized self-policy application/removal; (3) the one-instance/
one-node/two-database disposable experiment, up-to-$5 projected envelope and
irreversible destruction of its synthetic data. The current assignment grants
none of these; no AWS API, secret read or cloud mutation occurred in this pass.

Independent design PASS plus authorization and fresh clean preflight precede
resource creation. Independent executed-evidence review follows cleanup; no
self-approved finding disposition. Provider/B/helper/grantor/owner/DB-exception
changes reopen C, profile and D successor design/arithmetic; credential/principal/
transaction changes in E reopen affected C/D; delivery-only changes reopen E.
Patch/collation/SQL changes replay affected B/C/F proof without changing literal
semantic goldens. Unknown dependencies make evidence stale. O19/O21 and customer
key limitations remain explicit; all successor/0030 work stays behind D/E/F.
